Design at Brex

Design at Brex creates the experiences that make complex systems feel effortless through thoughtful, scalable design. Whether crafting interfaces, shaping product strategy, or harnessing AI to empower our users, we obsess over quality and clarity. This is a team where creativity meets high craft, and where designers grow by building for ambitious customers.

What you’ll do

You will work with Product and Engineering teams to successfully communicate, evolve, and execute a strong product design standard that showcases Brex as a leader in financial innovation. You are a crucial component of our company’s growth and product launches through your contributions to short and long-term strategic direction, creating and maintaining high visual standards and a strong focus on user needs. You have an owner’s mentality, taking pride in your work and in your team’s work, and view what you do as a part-owner and builder of Brex.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our San Francisco, Seattle, or New York office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require three days per week in office - Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities
• Use creative thinking toward establishing and executing on the vision for the team initiatives
• Challenge the status quo, push innovation, and inspire people toward a unified outcome
• Efficiently execute to ship products that deliver impact for our business and customers
• Partner with the leadership team to successfully communicate concisely across the team and influence product and design outcomes
• Work across the entire business stack and make an impact at different stages of the product: building vision strategy, ensuring all the loose ends are tied up when executing, and making sure the operational components to support onboarding are in place, not just the product
• Contribute toward growing and scaling design across the broader company and within the Design org
• Push forward and maintain a high design bar and level of execution
• Work closely with stakeholders across the organization, partnering with Engineering, Product, Operations, and Data teams to define and launch new products and features

Requirements
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a talent for detailed articulations of strategy, process, and leading cross-functional meetings to align teams
• Experience working cross-functionally with engineering, marketing, design, and product management teams
• Strong ability to craft a clear narrative and paint a vision that communicates and aligns teams
• Passion for team building and development
• 10+ years of experience as a product designer
• Experience building customer-facing products from 0 to 1 

Bonus points
• Experience working with tools including but not limited to Figma, Jira, Looker, Slack, Google Apps, Salesforce, Chrome Console
• Experience working on products in both B2B and B2C companies
• Experience writing/editing/contributing to documentation, training materials, and help articles to support product launches

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $240,000 - $300,000. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

We are looking for a risk manager to join the CDNA Clearing Organisation. 
The position is based in Asia to give the clearing house risk coverage outside US hours, so you will be the first line of response for overnight incidents. 

The emphasis is on clearing risk and operations, but you will also contribute to the margin and stress-testing models behind them. You will be contributing to the building of a fast-growth trading platform with innovative, multi-asset products bridging traditional finance (TradFi) and digital markets. For all roles, we look for people who are passionate about financial market innovation, equipped with energy, act as owners, and have exemplary work ethics.

Aspire career alternatives through us - our internal mobility program offers employees a new scope.

jobs.title: Head of Compliance: Multilateral Trading Facility (MTF)
jobs.description:
Reports to: Regional Head of Compliance, EMEA (with matrix reporting to the OEM Board and Global Compliance) 

Regulator: Malta Financial Services Authority (MFSA) 

About the Team

The compliance function at OKX is responsible for the overall compliance culture at the company. We are a team of risk-minded problem solvers who advise the business on the company's AML and regulatory obligations and enterprise risks.

OKX Europe Markets Limited is our MFSA-authorised investment services entity. Its licence covers the operation of a multilateral trading facility alongside our MiFID derivatives business. Operating a trading venue puts a distinct set of obligations on the firm: venue rulebook governance, member admission, market surveillance, transparency and reporting, systems resilience and orderly trading controls. This role owns compliance for that venue.

What You Will Be Doing

As Head of Compliance for the MTF, you will hold the MiFID compliance function for the trading venue and act as the MFSA-approved person for that role. The MLRO function sits separately; you will work alongside the OEM MLRO on financial crime matters that touch venue activity.

You will:
• Own the MTF compliance framework end to end: policies, procedures, controls, registers and the compliance monitoring programme covering MiFID II, MiFIR, MAR and the MFSA Investment Services Rules applicable to MTF operators.
• Act as the primary compliance point of contact for the MFSA on venue matters: authorisation variations, notifications, thematic reviews, RFIs, inspections and remediation.
• Own the venue rulebook. Keep it current, ensure it is enforceable, and run the governance process for changes.
• Oversee member and participant admission: eligibility criteria, non-discriminatory access, direct electronic access arrangements, sponsored access controls, and ongoing monitoring of members' compliance with the rules of the venue.
• Oversee admission to trading of financial instruments, including the compliance assessment of new instruments, product classes and tokenised or DLT-based instruments where relevant.
• Provide compliance oversight of orderly trading

requirements:

systems capacity and resilience, testing of members' algorithms, circuit breakers, order-to-trade ratios, tick sizes, market making schemes and clock synchronisation.
• Provide compliance oversight of pre- and post-trade transparency, waivers and deferrals, transaction reporting, reference data and the accuracy and completeness controls behind them.
• Advise the business on the interaction between the MTF and OKX's wider European footprint: the MiFID derivatives business, MiCA-authorised activity in OKX Europe Ltd, and the DLT Pilot Regime where a DLT MTF is in scope.
• Deliver the annual compliance risk assessment, the compliance monitoring plan and the compliance report to senior management and the Board.
• Build, lead and develop the MTF compliance team, and set the compliance training curriculum for venue-facing staff, trading operations and technology.
• Give day-to-day advice to product, engineering, trading operations, legal and market operations in a fast-moving regulatory environment, including sign-off on venue changes, launches and marketing where required.
• Oversee compliance aspects of outsourcing, critical third parties and operational resilience, including DORA obligations relevant to the venue.
• Prepare Board, committee and matrix stakeholder reporting, and represent OKX with the MFSA, ESMA consultations, industry bodies and peer venue forums.

What We Look For in You
• 10 years plus in regulatory compliance within financial services, market infrastructure, fintech or crypto, including time at a senior or head-of-function level.
• Direct experience of trading venue compliance: MTF, OTF, regulated market, SI or an equivalent execution venue. This is the core requirement.
• Working knowledge of MiFID II and MiFIR as they apply to venue operators: Articles 18–20 and 31 (MTF operating requirements and rule monitoring), Articles 48–50 (orderly trading), MiFIR transparency and transaction reporting, and the associated RTS.
• Practical experience of market abuse surveillance and MAR obligations for a venue operator, including STOR decision-making.
• Experience developing and owning a compliance framework that has stood up to regulatory examination, and a track record of engaging supervisors directly.
• Experience preparing and defending compliance reporting to a board or regulator.
• Familiarity with MFSA Investment Services Rules and Malta's regulatory environment, or a demonstrable ability to get there quickly from another EEA jurisdiction.
• Strong project management skills and the ability to run several regulatory workstreams to deadline.
• Comfortable working independently and in a dispersed, cross-border team across multiple varied tasks.
• Highly ethical, intuitive, and willing to question and challenge at every level of the business.
• Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain venue regulation to engineers and commercial teams.
• Eligible for MFSA approval as the holder of the compliance function.
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to Haves
• Prior experience in the crypto industry, particularly tokenised instruments, crypto derivatives or a MiCA-authorised trading platform.
• Experience with the DLT Pilot Regime or another distributed ledger market infrastructure.
• Experience of a trading venue authorisation or a licence variation to add MTF operation.
• Familiarity with surveillance platforms (Nasdaq Trade Surveillance, Eventus, Scila, Steeleye or similar) and with transaction reporting tooling.
• International Compliance Association, ACAMS, CISI or equivalent compliance certification.

Perks Benefits
• Competitive total compensation package
• L D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
• Various team building programs and company events
• Wellness and meal allowances
• Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants
• More that we love to tell you along the process!

jobs.title: Business Resilience Specialist
jobs.description:
Trust is the first of a new breed of banks in Singapore – digitally native and focused on delivering a delightful customer experience. You will work in a fast-paced and collaborative environment to solve new and interesting challenges each day. Together with our Trust team, you will help shape the future of our bank.

Role Purpose

The Business Resilience Specialist is responsible for executing and continuously enhancing the Bank's Business Resilience programme to ensure the resilience of critical business services, operational capabilities, and supporting dependencies.

The role serves as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) on Business Continuity Management (BCM), Operational Resilience, Crisis Management, Operational Continuity in Resolution (OCIR), Technology Resilience, and Third-Party Resilience. The incumbent will work closely with Business, Operations, Technology, Risk, Finance, Product, and external parties to strengthen the Bank's ability to withstand, respond to, recover from, and adapt to disruptions while meeting regulatory and business expectations.

Key Responsibilities

Business Continuity Management (BCM)
• Execute and maintain the Bank's BCM programme in accordance with regulatory requirements, internal standards, and industry best practices.
• Coordinate annual Business Impact Analysis (BIA) reviews for Critical Business Services (CBS) and Critical Business Functions (CBF), including dependency mapping, concentration risk assessments, and recovery objective reviews.
• Facilitate identification and assessment of people, process, technology, facilities, and third-party dependencies supporting critical services.
• Review and challenge Business Continuity Plans (BCPs) to ensure recovery strategies remain fit for purpose and aligned to business recovery objectives.
• Monitor BCM programme deliverables, remediation actions, and compliance obligations.
• Prepare BCM governance materials, management reporting, and attestation submissions.
• Maintain BCM standards, procedures, frameworks, and supporting documentation.

 

Operational Resilience
• Support the implementation and ongoing maturity of the Bank's Operational Resilience framework.
• Maintain the inventory of Critical Business Services and supporting dependency maps.
• Assess resilience vulnerabilities, concentration risks, and single points of failure across critical services.
• Facilitate severe-but-plausible scenario development, resilience assessments, and scenario testing exercises.
• Support resilience metrics, dashboards, and reporting for management and risk committees.
• Partner with business and technology stakeholders to ensure resilience considerations are incorporated into strategic initiatives and change programmes.

 

Operational Continuity in Resolution (OCIR)
• Support the Bank's Operational Continuity in Resolution (OCIR) framework and annual review processes.
• Coordinate Group OCIR submissions and support regulatory reporting requirements, including MAS 654 submissions.
• Maintain documentation relating to Critical Economic Functions (CEFs), critical shared services, and operational dependencies required to support resolution planning.
• Collaborate with Finance, Product, Strategy, Risk, and senior management stakeholders during OCIR reviews and submissions.

 

Crisis Management
• Maintain and enhance the Crisis Management Framework, supporting procedures, crisis playbooks, and crisis runbooks.
• Coordinate Crisis Management Team (CMT) exercises, tabletop simulations, and call-tree testing activities.
• Support crisis activation, coordination, and stakeholder communications during major disruptions.
• Drive lessons learnt reviews following incidents, exercises, and crisis events.
• Consolidate resilience and incident management processes across business and technology teams to strengthen enterprise crisis response capability.

 

Technology and Third-Party Resilience
• Partner with Technology teams to assess resilience of critical systems, technology platforms, disaster recovery capabilities, and service recovery arrangements.
• Review system recovery objectives, resilience gaps, and technology dependency assessments.
• Support Critical Business Service change management reviews involving new systems, applications, or technology changes.
• Assess resilience risks arising from outsourcing arrangements and critical third-party service providers.
• Review and challenge Third-Party Continuity Plans (TPCPs) and contingency arrangements for both technology and non-technology vendors.
• Collaborate with Vendor Management and Technology Risk teams to strengthen third-party resilience oversight.

 

Exercising, Testing and Assurance
• Develop and coordinate annual BCM testing and exercising programmes.
• Facilitate desktop walkthroughs, BCP exercises, end-to-end recovery testing, crisis simulations, and call-tree exercises.
• Maintain the Bank's resilience scenario library and testing methodologies.
• Prepare post-exercise reports, lessons learnt documentation, and remediation tracking.
• Monitor closure of resilience-related findings, actions, and improvement opportunities.

 

Governance, Reporting and Stakeholder Management
• Serve as the primary advisor and SME on business resilience matters across the Bank.
• Prepare reports and updates for risk forums, governance committees, and senior management.
• Support policy and standard reviews relating to BCM, operational resilience, crisis management, and third-party resilience.
• Coordinate regulatory reviews, audits, independent assessments, and assurance activities.
• Promote resilience awareness and conduct training sessions for Business Continuity Coordinators, business stakeholders, and employees.
• Foster strong working relationships across Business, Technology, Risk, Operations, and external partners to strengthen organisational resilience outcomes.

 

Qualifications Experience
• Bachelor's degree in Business, Risk Management, Finance, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline.
• Extensive years of experience in Business Continuity Management, Operational Resilience, Technology Resilience, Recovery Resolution Planning, Operational Risk, or related disciplines within financial services.
• Strong understanding of Critical Business Services, Business Impact Analysis, recovery strategies, continuity planning, and resilience testing.
• Experience working with Technology, Operations, Risk, and Third-Party Risk Management functions.
• Experience facilitating workshops, resilience exercises, crisis simulations, and stakeholder engagements..
• Experience within banking, digital banking, fintech, or other highly regulated financial institutions.
• Knowledge of MAS BCM Guidelines, MAS Operational Resilience requirements, MAS Technology Risk Management Guidelines, Outsourcing Guidelines, and Recovery Resolution Planning expectations.
• Professional certifications such as CBCI, DRI, ISO 22301 Lead Implementer/Auditor or equivalent.
• Experience supporting regulatory submissions, OCIR programmes, Critical Economic Function assessments, or enterprise resilience transformation initiatives.

Success Measures

The successful candidate will:
• Deliver the annual BCM programme and testing roadmap on time.
• Maintain accurate and current Critical Business Service inventories, BIAs, BCPs, and dependency mappings.
• Ensure effective crisis readiness through regular exercising and testing.
• Strengthen resilience oversight of critical technology services and third-party providers.
• Coordinate successful OCIR and regulatory submissions.
• Drive continuous improvement of the Bank's operational resilience capability and resilience culture.

jobs.title: Associate Data Product Manager
jobs.description:
YouTrip is the leading and fastest-growing multi-currency payment platform in Asia Pacific. In 2018, we pioneered the region's first multi-currency digital wallet. Now, YouTrip is the #1 multi-currency digital wallet trusted by millions across the region, processing over US$15 billion in total payment value annually. 

Our consumer and business propositions – YouTrip and YouBiz – empower individuals and businesses with inclusive, accessible, and affordable financial solutions. YouTrip has raised over US$110 million to date, including its recent Series B round led by global venture capital firm Lightspeed Venture Partners—underscoring strong investor confidence in its mission to transform digital financial services across the Asia Pacific. 

Recognised as World Economic Forum’s Global Innovator 2025, CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies (2025, 2024), and LinkedIn’s Top Startup (2024, 2023), YouTrip is dedicated to creating the next generation of digital finance services for consumers and businesses.

Valuing an entrepreneurial culture of diversity and inclusion, we are seeking driven individuals to join our fast-growing regional team as we push the boundaries of innovative fintech solutions. 

About The Role

We are looking for an Associate Data Product Manager to join YouTrip's Data & Analytics team, building and running the data products the company relies on: AI agents, decision-support products, metrics and analytics services. 

A Data Product Manager designs, builds, ships and then runs the product. You will write production code alongside AI coding agents, and you will own what the product achieves in the business, not just its launch. You'll partner with AI coding agents to build production systems, and once something's live, it's still yours: you monitor it, fix it, improve it, and drive its adoption. 

This role reports to the Director of Data & Analytics and works closely with business, operations, engineering and country teams.

You Will:
• Own and drive product initiatives, features, and workstreams end to end, from problem definition, data requirements, build, evaluation, launch, and running the product after launch
• Write and ship production code with AI coding agents to our engineering standard, and review what the agent produces before it ships
• Build the evaluation suites that gate releases: accuracy, guardrails, regression sets
• Monitor your live products daily: watch accuracy, usage and failures, fix what breaks, and continue to improve the product
• Drive adoption of what you build and measure it, from training users, chasing usage, and changing the product when required
• Own and report the business impact of your products in numbers: e.g. tickets resolved, hours saved, decisions made faster, errors avoided
• Translate business questions into executable specifications, such as data definitions, user stories, acceptance criteria with a measurable bar
• Collaborate closely with the people who use what you build — CS agents, finance analysts, and country teams to turn real operational pain points into working solutions
• Write the documentation that lets someone else run it: runbooks, design notes, evaluation reports, training materials, etc.

You Are:
• 1–3 years of hands-on experience building products, software, or data/AI systems
• Solid programming fundamentals, comfortable writing and understanding production code
• Clear communicator in writing and in person, and the ability to work closely with both technical and non-technical teams
• Strong problem-solving skills, comfortable working with AI coding agents, and the judgment to know when AI-generated code is right and when it isn't — you use AI for speed and stay responsible for the result
• Structured thinker who can determine works that matter, and break down messy problems into practical, executable solutions before building
• Define and track product and operational metrics such as conversion rates, campaign performance, engagement rates, and operational SLAs
• Having an ownership mentality, comfortable owning outcomes, not just deliverables, and accountable for what the product does after it ships
• Curious, fast learner, comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities 

Good to Have:
• Shipped or evaluated LLM-powered features in production
• Exposure to fintech, payments or another regulated environment
• Warehouse experience (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar), dashboards, or metrics-layer work
• A genuine interest in travel and overseas spending — you think like our users

jobs.description:
Summary - About KUDA

Kuda, which means ‘love’ in Shona, is more than a fintech - it’s a movement to make financial services accessible, affordable, and truly rewarding for every African.

Backed by over $100 million from some of the world’s most respected investors, we’re building a smarter alternative to traditional banking - offering seamless money transfers, business banking, and instant access to credit, all through your device.

At Kuda, we don’t just build products - we build people. We share the love in how we collaborate, carry everyone along as we grow, break boundaries to challenge what’s possible, and show up every day committed to doing better.

If you’re driven by purpose, excited by impact, and ready to help redefine the future of finance in Africa, you’ll feel right at home here.

Role Overview

At Kuda, we are dedicated to delivering a seamless, reliable, and highly secure digital financial experience for our customers. As a Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET), you will be the ultimate guardian of our platform’s quality and reliability. You won’t just be writing scripts; you will be writing robust code to build the automated infrastructure that ensures our customers' money and data are always safe and accessible.

You will sit at the critical intersection of software engineering and quality assurance. Your mission is to architect comprehensive test automation frameworks, champion a "shift-left" testing culture, and integrate quality gates seamlessly into our CI/CD pipelines.

Responsibilities
• Test Architecture & Frameworks: Design, build, and scale robust, maintainable test automation frameworks from the ground up for our backend microservices (APIs), web platforms, and mobile applications (iOS and Android).
• Comprehensive Automation: Drive functional, integration, and end-to-end automation testing. Write clean, high-quality code (e.g., in Java, Python, C#, or JavaScript/TypeScript) to automate complex financial user journeys.
• Pipeline Integration (CI/CD): Embed continuous testing into our DevOps pipelines. Ensure that every code commit is rigorously and automatically tested for functionality and stability before reaching production.
• Performance & Security Testing: Design and execute automated performance, load, and security tests to proactively identify bottlenecks and vulnerabilities, ensuring our systems can handle massive transaction volumes securely.
• Shift-Left Quality & Collaboration: Partner closely with software engineers, product managers, and QA analysts during the design phase. Define testability requirements and ensure quality is built-in from day one rather than tested-in later.
• Defect Triage & Root Cause Analysis: Investigate complex issues, debug code, and work alongside developers to trace defects down to the root cause, implementing preventative automation to stop regressions.
• Mentorship & Best Practices: Continuously evaluate modern testing tools and methodologies (e.g., Appium, Playwright, JMeter, Axios/RestAssured, MySql). Mentor junior team members and cultivate a culture where quality is a shared engineering responsibility.
• 5+ years of experience in a dedicated SDET or Software Automation role.
• Advanced proficiency in Java and JavaScript, with working knowledge of C# and Groovy.
• Hands-on experience with web and mobile automation tools including:
• Selenium
• Playwright
• Cypress
• Appium
• Strong experience with API and data testing, including making API/HTTP requests using:
• Rest Assured
• Axios
• Jest
• OkHttp
• Apache HttpClient
• Experience managing database connections using HikariCP or JDBC.
• Proficiency in automation framework design patterns, particularly:
• Keyword-Driven Testing
• Page Object Model (POM)
• Familiarity with build and CI/CD tools including:
• Maven
• TestNG
• Jest
• Jenkins
• Azure DevOps Pipelines
• Experience with test reporting and test management tools such as:
• Extent Reports
• Azure/Assure Reports
• Jira
• Test management integrations

Soft Skills & Professional Attributes
• Independent Ownership: Proactively identify improvements and fix issues without constant supervision.
• Knowledge Sharing: A "share the love" mentality—mentoring peers and documenting findings to elevate the team's technical bar.
• Collaborative Leadership: Aligning developers and Product Owners with the automation strategy to ensure collective success.
• Continuous Improvement: A "do things better every day" mindset focused on optimizing execution time and simplifying workflows.
• Strong Communication: Translating complex technical failures into clear, actionable insights for all stakeholders.

Why join Kuda?

At Kuda, our people are the heart of our business, so we prioritise your welfare. We offer a wide range of competitive benefits in areas including but not limited to:

👴Pension

jobs.title: Indirect and Direct Tax Compliance and Reporting Manager
jobs.description:
Hello, we’re Starling. We built a new kind of bank because we knew technology had the power to help people save, spend and manage their money in a new and transformative way. We’re a fully licensed UK bank with the culture and spirit of a fast-moving, disruptive tech company. We’re a bank, but better: fairer, easier to use and designed to demystify money for everyone. Starling Bank is powered by Engine, the banking platform we built ourselves and which we are now rolling out to other banks around the world. We employ more than 3,500 people across our London, Southampton, Cardiff and Manchester offices.

We are looking for a Tax Manager to join our growing tax team. Alongside the Head of Indirect Tax, Senior Corporation Tax Manager and the finance, payroll and HR teams, you will assist with the group’s UK and international VAT/GST and corporation tax affairs. This will include supporting a wide range of tax projects, international expansion projects, and managing tax compliance and tax risk.

This is an exciting time to be joining Starling Bank given its growth trajectory to date and its ambitious expansion plans in both the UK and internationally. You will support these plans from a tax compliance and reporting perspective.

Responsibilities
• Assist with the Group’s UK and international VAT/GST compliance, including quarterly VAT returns, monthly GST returns, partial exemption calculations, optimising input VAT recovery and working collaboratively with advisors.
• Support cross-border expansion by advising on international VAT/GST and corporation tax registration triggers, and place-of-supply rules.
• Assist in managing the Group’s UK and international corporation tax compliance including quarterly tax provisions, quarterly instalment payments and corporation tax returns.
• Support the organisation and wider tax team by taking a leading role in tax risk management and governance, including overseeing and improving the VAT and corporation tax control frameworks.
• Liaison between the finance and tax teams, as required across the taxes.
• A strong indirect and direct tax compliance and accounting background, gained in practice and/or industry.
• Experience of international taxes and banking taxes would be an advantage.
• Enthusiasm and a drive to expand your knowledge in new areas is as important as experience.
• Professional Qualification: ACA, ACCA, CTA with at least five years professional experience.
• A self-starter and independent worker with strong interpersonal skills.
• Well organised with the ability to plan and deliver on tight deadlines with attention to detail.
• A practical and commercial approach to problem solving, and the ability to communicate complex tax matters to both a tax and non-tax audience.

Interview Process

Interviewing is a two way process and we want you to have the time and opportunity to get to know us, as much as we are getting to know you! Our interviews are conversational and we want to get the best from you, so come with questions and be curious. In general you can expect the below, following a chat with one of our Talent Team:
• Step 1; interview with Head of Indirect Tax and Senior Corporation Tax Manager
• Step 2; complete tax case study and discuss answers with Head of Indirect Tax and Senior Corporation Tax Manager
• Step 3; interview with the Head of Tax.
• 25 days holiday (plus take your public holiday allowance whenever works best for you)

• Generous family-friendly policies
• Perkbox membership giving access to retail discounts, a wellness platform for physical and mental health, and weekly free and boosted perks
• Access to initiatives like Cycle to Work and Salary Sacrificed Gym partnerships

 About Us

You may be put off applying for a role because you don't tick every box. Forget that! While we can’t accommodate every flexible working request, we're always open to discussion. So, if you're excited about working with us, but aren’t sure if you're 100% there yet, get in touch anyway.

jobs.title: Quality Assurance Specialist
jobs.description:
Join Wise’s Quality Assurance team and help us build world-class, scalable operations that keep customers safe and deliver great experiences. In this role, you’ll provide independent, expert assurance over how work is done—spotting risk, identifying control gaps, and turning insights into clear, practical improvements. You’ll balance attention to detail with strong judgement, using data and tools to form well-reasoned conclusions that stand up to scrutiny.

You’ll work closely with partners across the business, sharing themes and trends, contributing to consistent decision-making, and helping raise the bar on quality—while keeping pace in a fast-moving environment aligned to our mission of Money Without Borders.

We are looking for candidates with extensive experience in AML Investigation, SAR Reporting, Fraud, Sanctions or KYC (EDD/CDD).

Key

Responsibilities:
• Conduct holistic, risk-based reviews using test scripts and scorecards to assess risk outcomes, compliance with global and regional policies, relevant guidance and risk appetite.
• Assess risk, materiality and root causes for each finding, providing clear and robust reasons aligned to policy compliance and/or risk mitigation.
• Participate in calibration exercises to share findings, best practice and ensure consistent, correct decisions are made across the team.
• Clearly communicate outcomes to stakeholders covering key risks, issues, root causes, and recommendations, maintaining robust records and audit trails.
• Analyse, assess and communicate emerging themes and trends, recommending opportunities for continuous improvement.
• When assigned, scope, plan, and execute root cause analysis or targeted investigations.
• Contributes to team collaboration and knowledge sharing to enhance team capabilities.
• Take a proactive approach to consistently achieving individual and team targets (KPIs, SLAs), demonstrating a strong commitment to both quality and speed. Meet deadlines, optimise processing times and take full ownership and accountability to deliver results.
• Perform additional tasks as assigned by your lead, demonstrating adaptability and a proactive approach. This includes actively participating in meetings, training, and internal events to support broader team and company objectives.
• Embody and uphold Wise’s values in daily interactions.

jobs.title: Deputy BSA/AML Officer
jobs.description:
Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world's money. Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money.

Your Mission

As the Deputy covering the broader financial crime needs of our function, your core responsibilities will include:
• Operational Leadership: Lead and empower the financial crimes team, guiding day-to-day operations, allocating resources effectively, and fostering a culture of high performance and continuous learning.
• Strategic Execution: Act as a central, strategic partner to the BSA/AML Officer, connecting the dots across various compliance domains, streamlining department operations, and driving the delivery of programmatic enhancements cross-functionally.
• Audit & Exam Coordination: Serve as the primary focal point for all financial crime-related internal audits and regulatory exams, proactively managing readiness, coordinating stakeholder responses, and ensuring the execution of remediation plans.
• Control Environment Oversight: Maintain rigorous oversight of our financial crime controls, ensuring they are continuously monitored, tested, and optimized so our defensive framework remains robust and scalable.
• Supervising appropriate measures to ensure that financial crime risks are taken into account in our day-to-day operations.
• Providing advice and guidance to other teams and key stakeholders—regionally and globally—on BSA, AML/CTF, and OFAC sanctions regulations, as well as related Wise policies and procedures.
• Challenging first-line teams on the development of controls and providing approvals on any control changes, new products, or features.
• Representing financial crime compliance oversight both internally and externally to regulators, auditors, and partners as required, showcasing Wise's strong compliance framework.

jobs.title: Fraud Operations Associate
jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Operations at Brex

Operations is the backbone of Brex’s mission to power businesses through our Intelligent Finance Platform. We own credit, fraud, money movement, and payments, protecting our customers and our company. From product operations that ensure flawless launches to scalable systems that drive innovation and precision, we operate at the intersection of product, design, engineering, and customer success. If you want to work at the heart of the business, Operations is where you belong.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our Vancouver office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week - Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

What you’ll do

As a Fraud Operations Associate, you will be working with some of the industry’s brightest minds to manage the operations aspects of fraud. Specifically, you will manage daily workflows related to transaction fraud, first-party fraud, and account takeovers and work towards improving the business’s ability to scale and make risk-based and customer-focused decisions. In this role, you will be the company expert in fraud operations and have the autonomy to drive down losses and improve internal efficiencies. You will also be critical in containing fraud losses and improving operational efficiencies by contributing to the evolution of our AI tools, thus ensuring Brex scales safely and sustainably. As Brex scales, the pressure of fraud increases as well.

Responsibilities

Case Management:
• Own and work associate level queues that are assigned to the Fraud Operations team
• Develop and implement scalable operational processes for fraud management
• Make risk-based, subjective decisions on high-value/risk transactions account offboardings
• Achieve company-level goals around financial fraud losses

Case Escalations Incident Handling
• Respond to cross-functional partners on escalations related to fraud in a diligent way that balances risk and provides customer love
• Participating and helping in streamlining fraud operational workflows around transaction review and account investigations
• Ability to take ownership of Fraud Incident handling and be able to conduct the root cause analysis close inefficiency gaps

Project Roadmap Ownership
• Ability to own ship projects that are on Fraud Ops roadmap with full autonomy
• Able to use AI tools to elevate enhance queues and projects
• Partner with Policy, Data Science, and Engineering to improve tooling to scale internal operations for fraud. 

Requirements
• 3+ years of experience in a fraud, risk or related operations role
• 1+ year of experience leading projects or workstreams end to end
• Demonstrated ability to use data to investigate issues, spot trends, and support decisions
• Strong verbal and written communication skills, including with cross-functional partners
• Excellent interpersonal, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage competing priorities
• Ability to collaborate and work with a team on projects and process improvements. 

Bonus points
• Familiarity with SQL or other data query tools
• People management or team lead experience
• Experience using AI tools to improve operational workflows
• Experience in fintech, payments, or banking industries

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $76,800-$96,000 CAD. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors, including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package

jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Legal at Brex

The Legal team helps the company grow responsibly, advocating for Brex and for the thousands of growing businesses we serve. We provide strategic advice and guidance to all Brex teams, protect Brex, advise on risk, and represent the company externally, negotiating with partners and interacting with regulators. Reimagining the financial system in a highly regulated environment requires creativity and resourcefulness, and we welcome the challenge.

What you’ll do

As Product and Privacy Counsel at Brex, you will be a critical strategic leader helping the company navigate the complex regulatory landscape at the intersection of financial services and technology. You will scale our privacy program and monitoring and assessment of legal and regulatory developments affecting Brex and its products. Together with cross-functional partners, you will be responsible for developing and scaling the privacy program, and providing strategic guidance that protects and advances Brex's business objectives. You will collaborate closely with internal teams, bank partners, and industry groups to ensure Brex maintains a robust, forward-looking approach to privacy. 

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our Salt Lake City office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities
• Scale Data Privacy and Security Programs: Work with engineering and business teams to expand and enhance data security, access, and privacy programs, optimizing for Brex's evolving data landscape.
• Implement Global Privacy Compliance: Develop and implement processes for strict adherence to domestic and international privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA), establishing monitoring and testing frameworks with the Compliance team.
• Negotiate Data-Related Contracts: Lead drafting and negotiation of external agreements, focusing on data protection, sharing, and data product legalities, safeguarding Brex's interests.
• Provide Product and Regulatory Advice: Offer comprehensive legal oversight and actionable regulatory/compliance advice for all products, from scoping design to go-to-market entry and marketing, while mitigating risks.
• Represent Brex Externally: Act as Brex's key representative with financial partners and regulatory bodies, building relationships and addressing inquiries.
• Integrate Innovation Compliance: Collaborate with compliance, engineering, and business teams to identify innovation opportunities within strict regulatory compliance, assessing and mitigating risks.
• Manage Outside Counsel: Strategically manage external legal counsel for regulatory, privacy, and data matters, overseeing strategies and ensuring cost-effective advice.

Requirements
• 4+ years working experience in a combination of law firm, technology and fintech companies, with a track record of working on privacy-related and financial regulatory issues.
• Deep understanding of CCPA, GDPR, and financial regulatory regulations.
• Exceptional judgment and integrity, ability to handle complex matters independently, and product-minded approach to lawyering.
• Entrepreneurial mindset and ability to work across various modes of communication; thrives in dynamic, fast-paced environments.
• Capacity to translate complex legal and regulatory concepts into clear, actionable guidance for non-legal stakeholders.
• Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives and manage time-sensitive projects.
• J.D. from an accredited law school, with a demonstrated track record of excellence in privacy and financial regulatory law. Bar admission and active standing in at least one U.S. state.

Bonus Points
• Experience in fintech or adjacent innovative financial services sectors is strongly preferred, with a nuanced understanding of emerging regulatory challenges.
• International privacy experience, with proven expertise in navigating cross-border regulatory complexities, including familiarity with international regulations.

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $189,000 - $230,000 USD. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

Greenlight is a family technology company on a mission to help families raise financially smart kids and navigate life together. Its suite of products — including the Greenlight app, debit card, Safe Family GPS trackers, and Family Hub — brings together financial tools, safety features, and everyday family management in one connected experience. It takes a talented team to aim for a mission like ours. We're looking for people who ask "is it bold enough?" You will join a smart, collaborative and passionate team of Recruiters. We take pride in the art of hiring and retaining talent across different functions. As a recruiter, you will partner directly with hiring managers and own end-to-end recruitment. The ideal candidate for this role should have a good understanding of different business functions, good communication skills, good interpersonal skills, strategic thinking, and good organizational skills. 

If you thrive in a collaborative team setting, enjoy ownership of your work, and take pride in providing exceptional candidate experience, this might be the role for you, and we would like to hear from you!

What you’ll get to do
• Managing end-to-end recruitment process: from job intake, sourcing, scheduling to interviewing, offer negotiation, hiring and onboarding.
• Engaging in proactive recruitment strategies to generate pipelines of qualified candidates for current and future needs.
• Working closely with hiring managers at all levels to identify current and upcoming staffing needs and build long-lasting working relationships.
• Assist in implementing various HR initiatives, including providing recommendations on process and program improvements
• Facilitate day to day employee relations, including complaint resolution
• Coordinate, administer and facilitate the performance management and talent management for employees
• Support the execution of HR strategies, policies, procedures, and programs to sustain continued growth and retention

To succeed in this role, we think you should have:
• An educational background in human resources and/or a relevant technical program is required.
• Minimum 5 years relevant work experience including experience in full life-cycle recruitment, working closely with hiring managers and candidates.
• Experience as both an agency recruiter and as an In-house recruiter
• Out-of-the-box thinking when it comes to sourcing, candidate management and candidate experience.
• Experience hiring for both Technical and Non-Technical roles (Engineering, Business and Commercial positions)
• Highly self-motivated and directed; ability to execute tasks in a fast-paced environment.
• Experience working with Human Resources Information Systems and Applicant Tracking Systems.
• Strong relationship-building skills with stakeholders, team members and candidates.
• Strong negotiation and persuasion skills.
• Exceptional organization skills and a keen attention to detail.
• High business acumen with the ability to align departmental projects key business objectives.

What we can offer you
• Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human.
• Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks.
• Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits.

What to expect in the hiring process
• A preliminary phone call with the recruiter
• A technical interview with the talent acquisition team
• A take-home assignment
• A behavioural and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.

The Payouts team specifically serves high-volume enterprise clients—such as creator economy platforms, content licensing firms, and gig-economy businesses—that rely on Wise’s API infrastructure to send funds globally at scale.

As one of the first three hires on this newly formed team, you will own the entire post-sale lifecycle for North American enterprise accounts. You will be responsible for driving partner onboarding, ensuring smooth API integrations, maintaining account health, and proactively driving net revenue expansion through corridor, currency, and volume growth. In addition to client-facing duties, you will build the foundational account management playbook, escalation paths, and partner health frameworks for this business line.

Responsibilities:

jobs.title: Scrum Master
jobs.description:
About Kuda 

Kuda, which means ‘love’ in Shona, is more than a fintech - it’s a movement to make financial services accessible, affordable, and truly rewarding for every African.

Backed by over $100 million from some of the world’s most respected investors, we’re building a smarter alternative to traditional banking - offering seamless money transfers, business banking, and instant access to credit, all through your device.

At Kuda, we don’t just build products - we build people. We share the love in how we collaborate, carry everyone along as we grow, break boundaries to challenge what’s possible, and show up every day committed to doing better.

If you’re driven by purpose, excited by impact, and ready to help redefine the future of finance in Africa, you’ll feel right at home here.

Role Overview

As a Scrum Master at Kuda, you will play a pivotal role in driving delivery velocity, operational excellence, and agile maturity across our engineering organization. Operating within a high-growth scale-up environment, you will be embedded with large cross-functional teams of 15 to 20 engineers, product managers, and designers.

Your mission is to champion agile principles, eliminate delivery friction, and foster a high-trust, safe environment where teams consistently produce high-quality financial software. You will serve as the bridge between high-level delivery milestones and day-to-day execution, ensuring squads stay aligned with organizational objectives while navigating the dynamic complexities of the FinTech space.

Key Responsibilities
1. Agile Facilitation & Team Coaching
• Facilitate core Scrum ceremonies—including Daily Stand-ups, Sprint Planning, Backlog Refinement, Sprint Reviews, and Retrospectives—for larger cross-functional teams.
• Coach squad members and product owners on agile best practices, backlog prioritization, user story splitting, and effective capacity estimation.
• Cultivate a team culture grounded in psychological safety, active accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration.
2. Operational & Delivery Excellence
• Proactively identify and resolve delivery blockers, dependencies, and cross-team bottlenecks to maintain high execution velocity.
• Partner with engineering leads to optimize squad workflows and reduce delivery friction across sprint cycles.
• Utilize delivery metrics (such as velocity, burn-down trends, lead time, cycle time, and DORA metrics) to drive data-informed continuous improvement.
3. Stakeholder Alignment & Scale-Up Execution
• Work closely with Product Managers and Engineering Leadership to ensure sprint goals directly map to high-level product roadmaps.
• Maintain transparent, real-time visibility into sprint progress, risks, and dependencies for key business stakeholders.
• Guide teams through the rapid pace and shifting priorities characteristic of a fast-growing FinTech scale-up.
4. Compliance & Quality Governance
• Support squads in maintaining technical excellence and security-first engineering practices without sacrificing delivery momentum.
• Ensure agile processes account for necessary regulatory, compliance, and quality standard checks typical of high-throughput financial systems.
• Proven Agile Expertise: 5+ years of hands-on experience as a Scrum Master or Agile Coach in dynamic technology environments.
• Scale-Up & FinTech Background: Demonstrable track record of delivering value within high-growth scale-up companies, preferably in the FinTech sector.
• Large Tribe Leadership: Deep experience facilitating and guiding multi-disciplinary squads (Engineers, QA, Designers, Product Managers).

Hard Skills
• Deep expertise in Scrum, Kanban, and modern scaling frameworks.
• Advanced proficiency with Jira, Confluence, and delivery tracking tools.
• Strong grasp of software delivery metrics (e.g., flow metrics, DORA metrics) to measure squad health and output.
• Practical understanding of modern software delivery practices (e.g., CI/CD, GitOps, automated testing).

Soft Skills
• Empathetic Leadership: A dedication to empowering teams, removing obstacles, and nurturing an inclusive environment.
• Clear Communication: Ability to articulate project status, risks, and process optimizations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders alike.
• Conflict Resolution & Adaptability: Skillful at navigating team dynamics, resolving friction, and pivoting gracefully in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.title: KYC Operations Senior Analyst - SMA (Night shifts)
jobs.description:
Wise is looking for a KYC Operations Senior Analyst to join the Tallinn Senior Management Approval team to cover our night shifts. You will play a critical role in ensuring that Wise adheres to regulatory and compliance requirements. You will be responsible for conducting enhanced due diligence, analysing customer activities, behaviour patterns, and ensuring that our KYC records are kept up to date according to our internal standards. You will be responsible for assessing and approving onboarding customers in AML High Risk state and customers with touch points with High Risk 3rd Countries and Low Tax Jurisdictions according to regulatory standards.

As a KYC Operations Senior Analyst, you will play a key role in supporting a financial crime program that is driven by Wise's mission for money without borders, transparency, and protecting customers. We are looking for someone with experience in enhanced due diligence, an excitement and desire to learn and grow with this new team, and strong organisational and communication skills.

Job Responsibilities
• Review and assess high risk customer reports to provide analysis and approval as per the set policies and procedures.
• Review customer transaction history and provide insights into customer behaviour patterns that may indicate risks. Conduct periodic reviews and analyse changes in customers history and account usage.
• Exercise discretion in setting priorities, identifying customer records that require further review and taking action to obtain and follow-up on the information and/or documentation requested.
• Ensure that information and documentation provided by customers meet our risk appetite for onboarding and maintaining High Risk customers.
• Conduct in depth analysis, using provided documentation or external sources (e.g. websites and company registries) ensuring that only customers within risk appetite are onboarded. Perform searches utilising Internet sources and/or third-party vendors to obtain information on prospects and new/existing customers.
• Communicate with other internal teams when required to handle escalated or complicated cases.
• Provide guidance and responses to daily inquiries from peers, front-line and management regarding high risk approval matters and case analysis, when appropriate.
• Maintain high understanding of AML/CFT Regulations and how these impact the business, as well as Wise products and Services;
• When warranted, be capable of drafting SAR narratives to report activity deemed unusual.
• Taking part in and leading projects related to SMA Team processes and guidelines. Assist in identifying improvement opportunities and contribute to policy updates, training materials, and standard operating procedures.
• Draft reports to internal and external stakeholders, periodically and when requested.
• Have a deep understanding of different business models, customer types, country risks and regulatory requirements across multiple geographies;
• Support Wise in internal and external audits and regulatory process related queries reviews.
• Mentor, and support Senior Management Approval Analyst, by providing training and coaching to enhance team capabilities.
• Effective communication with customers by the relevant communication channels that Wise operates with (e.g. phone, email, and chat).
• Perform your tasks and responsibilities within the expected key performance indicators set by the leadership team.
• Tasks that are related to the position and are assigned to you by your lead. Participating in meetings, training, internal and external events.

jobs.title: Finance Manager, Settlement and Reconciliation
jobs.description:
We Are

YouTrip is the leading and fastest-growing multi-currency payment platform in Asia Pacific. In 2018, we pioneered the region's first multi-currency digital wallet. Now, YouTrip is the #1 multi-currency digital wallet trusted by millions across the region, processing over US$15 billion in total payment value annually. 

Our consumer and business propositions – YouTrip and YouBiz – empower individuals and businesses with inclusive, accessible, and affordable financial solutions. YouTrip has raised over US$110 million to date, including its recent Series B round led by global venture capital firm Lightspeed Venture Partners—underscoring strong investor confidence in its mission to transform digital financial services across the Asia Pacific. 

Recognised as World Economic Forum’s Global Innovator 2025, CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies (2025, 2024), and LinkedIn’s Top Startup (2024, 2023), YouTrip is dedicated to creating the next generation of digital finance services for consumers and businesses.

Valuing an entrepreneurial culture of diversity and inclusion, we are seeking driven individuals to join our fast-growing regional team as we push the boundaries of innovative fintech solutions. 

About the Role

Settlement & Reconciliation is the operational and regulatory core of our business — the function that moves and reconciles customer money across every product and partner, and ensures we always have the funds in place to settle. As Finance Manager, you will own settlement, reconciliation, cash-flow forecasting and exception management end to end, partner with Product and Engineering as we build, and handle our regulatory and partner reporting. You will build and lead a team and play a central role in scaling our finance operations — a rare opportunity to own a function at the heart of how the business moves and safeguards money. 

You Will

Settlement
• Settle with card networks, FX, and remittance partners, ensuring funds reach partners accurately and on time
• Validate, and approve user refunds and cashback disbursements

Reconciliation
• Own daily reconciliation across all products and flows - topup, withdrawals, purchases, etc., - against bank statements, partner data, and internal records
• Review and approve balance adjustments and user compensation

Cash flow & liquidity
• Forecast settlement inflows and outflows to ensure sufficient prefunding and liquidity to meet settlement obligations and regulatory requirements

Continuous improvement
• Investigate reconciliation variances, partnering with Product and Engineering to identify the root causes, refine systems, and strengthen processes

Reporting & accounting support
• Prepare and submit regulatory and partner reporting
• Provide settlement journals, accruals, and reconciliation support for month-end and year-end close

Business partnering & leadership
• Partner with Product, Data and Engineering on new features and enhancements — to assess the impact on revenue and cost recognition, define data and reporting requirements for reconciliations, evaluate settlement cut-off times and their impact on safeguarded balances, identify tax implications, and support product testing and implementation
• Drive process improvement and automation, including adopting AI tools
• Build, lead and develop a team of 3+

You Are
• A proactive, detail-oriented finance professional with 10+ years across finance operations, settlement, treasury or financial control — ideally gained in fintech, payments or banking.
• Proven people manager, having led teams of 5 or more
• Strong grasp of payment flows, reconciliation, card networks, and multi-currency operations
• Experience with settlement, prefunding, liquidity, and regulatory and partner reporting (e.g. MAS or equivalent)
• Strong controls mindset and attention to detail, with the analytical skill to resolve complex breaks
• Possess excellent communication skills and business acumen
• Comfortable in a fast-paced, high-growth, and regulated environment
• Degree in Accounting or Finance; CA / CPA / ACCA an advantage

jobs.title: Independent Non-Executive Director (Resident), Seychelles
jobs.description:
Independent Non-Executive Director (Resident), Seychelles

 

About OKX

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

Our Seychelles business has operated since 2017 and now sits within the licensing regime established by the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act of Seychelles 2024 (the VASP Act). We are seeking an Independent Non-Executive Director, resident in Seychelles, to join the board of our Seychelles entity to supplement its board of governance with an independent resident non-executive director.

About the Role

As an Independent Non-Executive Director and Resident Director of our Seychelles entity, you will bring independent challenge to strategy, risk and conduct, hold management to account on behalf of shareholders and stakeholders, and provide the resident board presence that the licence and the entity's governance arrangements require. The role exists to do three things at once: provide independent challenge; satisfy the Seychelles Financial Services Authority (the FSA) that the board of the Company meets its expectations on composition, competence and fitness and propriety under the VASP Act; and provide local substance in Seychelles.

The entity operates within the group's global governance, risk and compliance framework while remaining separately accountable to its own board and to its regulator. The Board comprises a mix of executive and independent non-executive directors. This is a genuinely resident role. The appointee must be physically present in Seychelles, attend board and management meetings in person, and be available to engage with the FSA and the entity's advisers in Seychelles.

A non-executive director carries the same general legal responsibilities to the entity as any other director, and must perform those duties faithfully, efficiently and diligently to a standard commensurate with the role and with their own knowledge, skills and experience.

What You’ll Be Doing

Independentally Challenge
• Bring an external and independent perspective to strategy, risk and conduct, and hold management to account on behalf of shareholders and stakeholders.
• Provide constructive challenge and strategic guidance, and offer specialist advice to the Board.
• Scrutinise the performance of management and of individual executive directors against agreed goals, and monitor how that performance is reported.
• Act in good faith, honestly and responsibly, and make decisions objectively in what you consider to be the interests of the entity.

Regulatory Standing Local Substance
• Satisfy the FSA that the board of the Company meets its expectations on composition, competence and fitness and propriety under the VASP Act.
• Provide the physical, resident board presence in Seychelles that the licence and the entity's governance arrangements require.
• Attend board and management meetings in person, and engage with the FSA and the entity's advisers in Seychelles as required.

Collective Board Responsibilities
• Promote the long term sustainable success of the entity, generating value for shareholders and contributing to wider society.
• Establish the entity's purpose, values and strategy, and satisfy the Board that its culture is aligned to them.
• Provide effective, prudent and ethical oversight, act with integrity, lead by example and promote the desired culture.
• Ensure the resources needed to meet the entity's objectives are in place, and measure performance against them.
• Establish and lead within a framework of prudent and effective controls that allows risk to be assessed and managed.
• Ensure effective engagement with shareholders and stakeholders.
• Ensure workforce policies and practices are consistent with the entity's values.

Individual Director Responsibilities
• Satisfy yourself on the integrity of the entity's financial information, its financial controls, and whether its risk management systems are robust and defensible.
• Determine appropriate remuneration for executive directors, and play a leading part in appointing and, where necessary, removing them.
• Contribute to the entity's succession planning.
• Uphold the highest standards of integrity, and support the chairperson in setting the values, behaviours and culture of the boardroom and beyond.

Committee Service

Serve on one or more board committees where required. The relevant terms of reference will be provided on appointment.

What We Look for in You
• Resident in Seychelles, and currently holding the right to reside and work there.
• Able to satisfy the FSA's fitness and propriety assessment.
• Board level or senior governance experience in a regulated financial services, banking, insurance, fiduciary or corporate services business.
• Working knowledge of anti-money laundering and counter terrorist financing obligations, and of the Seychelles regulatory environment.
• Financial literacy sufficient to interrogate financial statements, controls and risk reporting without support.
• Demonstrable independence of mind, and the willingness to challenge management and record dissent.
• Fluent in English, with excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.

What Will Make You Stand Out
• Experience of virtual assets, fintech, payments or capital markets.
• Prior regulatory experience.
• Experience chairing an audit, risk or compliance committee.
• Experience of a group structure where much of the operating activity sits outside the licensed entity's jurisdiction, and of the oversight challenge that creates.
• An established local network among Seychelles regulators, professional advisers and the financial services community.

 

Why Join OKX?
• Play a pivotal role in the governance of a successful virtual asset business.
• Bring independent oversight to a global crypto platform operating at scale across multiple jurisdictions.
• Work alongside an experienced board and a global leadership team in a high-growth industry.
• A defined, time-bounded commitment with genuine influence over strategy, risk and conduct.

 

Ready to Reshape Finance?

At OKX, we’re on a mission to make crypto accessible, secure, and transformative for the next billion users. Join us and help set the governance standard for virtual assets globally.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

 

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. 

 

Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

 

About The Opportunity

P2P Marketplace sits within the Core Platform team where we serve as the backbone of OKX Central Exchange. • Strong knowledge of payment processing, settlement flows, and compliance frameworks (e.g., AML, KYC).
• Excellent project management and cross-functional collaboration skills; able to lead complex integration projects independently.
• Proficient in English, with strong communication and negotiation skills for working with international partners.

Nice-To-Have

• Familiarity with payment landscapes in Southeast Asia, LATAM, the Middle East, or Africa.
• Experience working with global card schemes (Visa, Mastercard) or major local payment networks.
