jobs.description:
At bunq, we're not just building a banking app, we are reshaping how people experience financial freedom globally. To sustain that mission while protecting our users and our business, we need an Internal Auditor focused on Regulatory Compliance to ensure we meet every regulatory requirement, manage compliance risks, and keep our operations audit-ready at all times.

As an Internal Auditor - Regulatory Compliance, your mission is to safeguard bunq's regulatory standing by identifying and mitigating compliance gaps, ensuring adherence to evolving regulations across all markets we operate in, and building the audit infrastructure that keeps our business resilient.

As an Internal Auditor - Regulatory Compliance, you will own:

Conduct compliance audits across all business lines (AML, KYC, data protection, market conduct) and identify gaps with concrete remediation recommendations.

Build and execute the audit roadmap, prioritizing high-risk regulatory domains and ensuring systematic coverage across our markets.

Drive remediation tracking with business teams, ensuring findings are addressed and root causes fixed, not just symptoms.

Compliance Audit Program: Design and execute the first multi-domain compliance audit program, covering AML/KYC, data protection, market conduct, and operational risk, delivering findings and a forward remediation roadmap.

High-Risk Compliance Assessment: Conduct a deep-dive audit into bunq's highest-risk regulatory areas (likely payment services directives, data governance, or market-specific regulations depending on your markets), identifying systemic gaps and building a remediation plan.

Regulatory Change Impact Assessment: Analyze recently enacted or upcoming regulations across our markets and assess operational readiness, working with stakeholders to ensure bunq remains compliant before enforcement deadlines.

Regulatory audit expertise: Proven experience auditing AML/KYC, data protection (GDPR/similar), or market conduct in financial services/fintech.

Audit methodology: Risk-based audit planning, workpaper development, sampling techniques, and presenting findings to executives and regulators.

Regulatory knowledge: You understand banking regulators, interpret guidance, and can navigate regulatory inquiries or examinations.

Communication: Translate complex regulations into clear actions for business teams; credible voice with regulators and leadership.

jobs.title: Deputy AML Manager - Belgium
jobs.description:
At bunq, we're more than just a bank, we're transforming how people experience banking across Europe. Our users deserve to bank like locals, no matter where they are. We started Belgium with local IBANs, but we're now upgrading to full-branch status, which means taking on direct regulatory standing, deeper compliance obligations, and new accountability to Belgium's NBB (National Bank of Belgium) and financial regulators.

As AML Manager Belgium, your mission is to lead Belgium through this compliance transition, ensuring we move seamlessly from our lighter vIBAN model to full-branch operations while maintaining regulatory trust and operational excellence. You'll be the accountable person who owns Belgium's entire compliance footprint, AML/CFT operational readiness, integrity-risk assessment (SIRA), and financial-crime reporting (FIU), all operating at full-branch regulatory standards.

Transition Belgium to full-branch compliance model, migrate from vIBAN-era compliance systems to full-branch operations, ensuring seamless readiness for NBB oversight and maintaining zero regulatory findings during the upgrade.

Own Belgium's SIRA, AML/CFT, and FIU obligations end-to-end, establish Belgium-localized SIRA integrity-risk assessments, AML/CFT gap analysis, and FIU financial-crime reporting, using AI-first mechanisms to deliver what traditional banks staff with a local team.

Prepare Belgium's AML program for regulatory inspection readiness, maintain audit trails, evidence documentation, and control testing for NBB oversight.

Full-Branch Compliance Readiness Audit : Conduct a comprehensive audit of Belgium's current compliance posture under vIBAN model, identify gaps for full-branch requirements (NBB, FSMA, Ombudsfin), and deliver a remediation roadmap with specific AI-driven solutions.

Belgium-Localized SIRA & FIU Systems : Design and implement Belgium-specific SIRA integrity-risk controls and FIU financial-crime reporting mechanisms, using AI tooling to automate what possible and keeping humans in the loop for judgment calls and escalations.

Deep Belgian AML/CFT & regulatory expertise - You understand NBB requirements, FSMA rules, local banking regulations, and their practical application; you can translate Belgian regulatory language into operational compliance controls.

Proven ownership of compliance programs end-to-end - You've built or scaled a compliance program (not just supported one), managing operational readiness, risk assessment, and regulatory reporting as the accountable person.

Proven ability to manage AML inspections and regulatory audits, preparing evidence, audit trails, and control documentation for regulator scrutiny.

AI-first operating mindset - You're comfortable building compliance operations using AI and automation (not traditional local headcount), and you can design mechanisms that let AI handle routine workflows while you focus on exceptions and regulatory judgment.

Fluency in Dutch, French, or both + English - You can navigate Belgian regulatory communication and engage with local stakeholders in their language; English fluency for bunq-wide collaboration.

ABOUT US

Dakota is a stablecoin infrastructure platform powering modern financial products through regulated money movement, stablecoin orchestration, and cross-border settlement. We serve institutional clients — fintechs, payment service providers, marketplaces, and enterprises — through an API-first platform that abstracts the complexity of custody, compliance, settlement, and banking partnerships. Dakota has raised $16.5M from CoinFund, 6th Man Ventures, and Triton Ventures.

We are a remote first team across North America and Europe. We value high quality work, clear thinking and ownership.

Please note: Dakota is a remote-only, equal-opportunity employer. At this time, we are able to hire within the U.S., United Kingdom, Spain and Portugal.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Dakota is at a stage where how we explain the product and how it shows up in real customer conversations matters as much as what we build. This role exists to make that repeatable.

We’re hiring a Head of Marketing to take ownership of how Dakota goes to market — defining positioning, shaping messaging, and building the foundations of a GTM motion that works in practice, not just on paper.

This is a founding marketing leadership role. You’ll work closely with the CEO and GTM leadership to set direction, make tradeoffs, and execute in a hands-on way. We’re not looking for someone to manage a large team or scale channels immediately. We’re looking for a leader who can decide what matters, test it, refine it, and then scale what’s working over time.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Define how Dakota is explained to customers

 - Define and evolve positioning, messaging and use cases that stand up in real sales conversations.

 - Clarify how Dakota’s products are differentiated and when they’re the right solution for a customer.

Build a content led GTM engine

 - Own what content is worth producing, why it exists, and how it supports customer understanding and conversion.

 - Create and iterate key assets while also using leverage- AI, contractors and partners- to increase speed and quality.

 - Set the bar for quality and relevance rather than sheer output volume.

Improve conversion and GTM effectiveness

 - Partner closely with sales and product to understand objections, stalled deals and increase buyer clarity.

 - Adjust messaging, use cases, and campaigns based on feedback from the field.

 - Scale activity once fundamentals are working, prioritizing signal before volume.

Lay foundations for scale

 - Establish lightweight workflows, metrics, and operating cadence so marketing can scale responsibly over time.

 - Use modern tools, including AI, to increase leverage without adding unnecessary processes.

WHO YOU ARE

You’re a strategic builder with strong judgment.

You likely:

 - Have been the first or early marketing hire at a startup, or owned a 0–1 GTM effort inside a larger company.

 - Have strong product marketing instincts and can operate across content, messaging, and GTM execution.

 - Are comfortable making decisions without perfect information and adjusting quickly when something isn’t working.

 - Have worked closely with sales and understand how marketing impacts real conversations and outcomes.

 - Can balance hands-on execution with setting direction and leading through influence.

 - Have managed a small team or led others before and can see yourself growing and developing people over time, without needing a large org or heavy process.

You don’t need fintech experience, but you should be comfortable marketing complex, trust sensitive, or regulated products.

HOW WE WORK

At Dakota, we value people who:

 - Strive for excellence

 - Practice extreme ownership.

 - Experiment fearlessly and learn quickly.

 - Stay close to customers.

 - Communicate clearly and directly.

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Engaging problems that increase economic freedom globally

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Employee-friendly equity terms (extended exercise)

 - Remote work, no commuting to the office

 - Paid co-working space/desk at an office

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Regular team events and off-sites

jobs.title: Sr. Member Experience Manager
jobs.description:
DAVE VS. GOLIATH. WE’RE DAVE.

Dave is a financial app on a mission to build products that level the financial playing field. It is redefining the financial landscape by leveraging technology to create an affordable, transparent, and user-centric access to liquidity for millions of Americans. As a leading innovator in the U.S. financial services sector, Dave’s digital financial platform offers products designed to meet the credit needs of those underserved by traditional financial institutions. Dave’s offerings include its flagship ExtraCash product, providing members up to $500 within minutes. The company is on track to launch several new product offerings in 2026, including a Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) option.

Dave is focused on serving Americans who are financially vulnerable or living paycheck to paycheck. Dave is leading the charge in creating a new era of credit products that prioritizes speed, affordability, and accessibility, making it the go-to financial partner for those who need it most.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Dave is growing fast and the member base is growing with it. As more people choose Dave over traditional banking, the feedback loop that helps us understand their experience needs to be sharper, more structured, and more connected to the decisions that drive the business. That's what this role builds.

As Sr. Member Experience Manager, you'll own the Voice of Customer program and shape how Dave listens to, understands, and acts on member signals across every touchpoint. This isn't a "compile the feedback" role. You'll be the person translating what millions of members are experiencing into the structured, data backed case that gets in front of Product and Leadership and actually changes things.

The work sits at a real intersection. You'll tie member sentiment to business outcomes like retention, engagement, and revenue, and make the argument that doing right by the member and growing the business are the same goal. At Dave they are. This role is how we make sure that case gets made consistently, on a regular cadence, with the numbers to back it up.

If you want a high-visibility IC role where your work shapes product decisions and your voice carries weight across the org, this is it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Voice of Customer Program

You are the voice of the customer within Dave. You own how member signals get turned into something the Dave team can act on. That means pulling input from every customer contact support data, app reviews, social conversations, community feedback, and surveys, including App Store and Google Play reviews and public social conversations. You decide what gets tracked, how it's measured, and when something is significant enough to escalate, including routing anything with reputational or policy circumvention risk to Complaints/Resolve so they can move fast.

You'll build a structured, recurring rhythm for surfacing what matters: real-time visibility into issues and trend shifts as they happen, a monthly deep dive with Research into one specific friction area affecting members, and a periodic review of the biggest unresolved issues that you bring to Product and use to keep Leadership current. Each cycle produces a clear problem statement, not just a data dump, and you keep a running backlog so patterns don't disappear just because they miss a cycle.

The readouts you deliver aren't a complaints list. They're a business case. A spike in a friction category is a churn signal. A recurring drop-off in a core flow means members are transacting less or leaving. You'll tie what you're hearing to the metrics that matter, retention, engagement, revenue, and member growth, and you'll partner with Member Insights and Data Analytics so the signal you're surfacing feeds the classifiers and dashboards the rest of MS&O relies on, not just your own readouts.

When member signals point to a product gap, you build the case and bring it to Product in a way PMs can prioritize: a clear problem statement written from the member's perspective, backed by data, with a recommendation behind it.

You're not there to report back. You're there to move the outcome.

jobs.description:

the Role:

You'll own security operations end-to-end, embedded directly into the engineering team and working closely with infrastructure, protocol and platform.

If you treat threat modeling as a design conversation and not a compliance exercise, you're our kind of person. You should only apply for this role if you are ready to come into the office every day and work in person with our team!

What You'll Do:

Security Operations

 - Own day-to-day security operations: monitoring, alerting, triage, and response

 - Manage and monitor endpoint security via an EDR system - tune detections, investigate alerts, and drive incidents to resolution

 - Lead identity lifecycle management, including employee onboarding and off boarding (access provisioning, key rotation, deprovisioning)

Bug Bounty & Vulnerability Management

 - Prioritize and track vulnerabilities through to remediation in close collaboration with protocol and engineering teams

 - Develop internal tooling and processes to make the bounty workflow faster and more consistent

DevSecOps & Pipeline Hardening

 - Audit and harden CI/CD pipelines - secrets management, supply chain integrity, SAST/DAST integration, build provenance

 - Own dependency security: identify and remediate vulnerable packages across repositories (yes, including the npm dependency hell)

 - Establish and enforce security standards across the SDLC

Infrastructure Security

 - Partner with the infrastructure team to review and harden cloud environments (access controls, network segmentation, least privilege, logging)

 - Contribute to threat modeling for new systems and architectural changes

 - Drive implementation of security tooling across the stack

Vendor & External Partner Management

 - Own relationships with external security vendors and service providers — holding them accountable toSLAs, managing scope, and ensuring findings are actioned

 - Evaluate and onboard new security tooling as the team and threat landscape evolve

What We're Looking For:

- 5+ years of experience in software and security engineering, with meaningful time in a DevSecOps or security operations context

 - Hands-on experience hardening CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, CircleCI, or similar) and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or equivalent)

 - Proficiency with endpoint security tooling (CrowdStrike or equivalent EDR)

 - Comfort owning identity and access management processes, including onboarding/offboarding workflows

 - Strong communication skills - you can write a clear triage report, give direct feedback to a developer and explain risk to a non-technical stakeholder

Nice to Have:

- You were a traditional software engineer before specializing in security

 - Prior experience at a DeFi protocol, crypto exchange, or blockchain infrastructure company

 - CTF/security competition background

 - Contributions to open-source security tooling

What Success Looks Like:

In your first 90 days, you've mapped our attack surface, established a daily rhythm on ImmuneFi, and shipped at least a few meaningful PRs across the full stack. Within six months, you've built enough trust in the team that engineers come to you before shipping sensitive PRs, not after.

experience:

jobs.title: Blockchain Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

ether.fi http://ether.fi is a fast-growing crypto-native financial platform on a mission to put users in control of their wealth, making it easy to save, earn, and spend crypto. As a leading decentralized finance (DeFi) bank, ether.fi http://ether.fi offers a fully integrated, non-custodial suite of products (Stake, Liquid, and Cash) that bridge crypto utility with real-world convenience.

Nonce is the team behind ether.fi http://ether.fi's DeFi yield vaults, the products that take user deposits and put them to work across DeFi. A depositor gets a single position and a yield-bearing token. Behind it sits a mandate, a set of whitelisted protocols and strategies, live NAV accounting, and a redemption path that has to stay honest whether the market is calm or not. The whole job is deploying into lending markets, LSTs and LRTs, basis and funding trades, stablecoin strategies, and whatever comes next, safely, with the risk understood before the capital moves.

It's a small team with a lot of autonomy. Every vault, every rebalance, and every new protocol integration goes through this team.

Learn more at ether.fi http://ether.fi.

POSITION OVERVIEW

We're hiring a smart contract / backend engineer to help build and operate ether.fi http://ether.fi's DeFi yield vaults. You'll write the contracts that allocate user capital, build the tooling/systems that runs 365/24/7 to safely monitor and manage the capital.

The immediate focus is the next generation of Nonce's vault product to power one of the largest DeFi yield vaults products in the industry. Getting that right, and keeping it secure, is the main thing this role is here to do.

This is a build-and-operate role. You'll ship Solidity and backend services, and you'll also share the day-to-day of running live vaults: discussing new yield opportunities, reviewing transactions, signing them, and deciding whether a new protocol is safe to allocate into. The team is small, so the people who write the vaults are the people who run them.

This role is onsite 4 days per week at one of our global offices: NYC, Denver, or the Cayman Islands.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

Vaults

 - Design, write, deploy, and configure yield vault smart contracts alongside the rest of the vault team

 - Build vault tooling: putting on trades, rebalancing across strategies, updating vault policies and whitelists, admin configuration

 - Extend the vault architecture as new yield strategies, assets, and chains come online

 - Review teammates' contracts and tooling, and get reviewed in turn

 - Prove the contracts do what they claim: unit and fuzz tests, invariants, and formal verification where it earns its keep

 - Work with external auditors through review cycles, and write contracts that are straightforward to audit in the first place

Backend services

 - Build and maintain the critical systems that run 365/24/7 without failure: the solver powering redemption flows, including the liquidity buffer, report NAV changes, security concerns and unwind logic behind them

 - Build and maintain the NAV service, pricing every position a vault holds, and the accuracy guarantees behind the share price

 - Automate on-chain operations so allocation, harvesting, and rebalancing run reliably without a human in the loop

Risk and protocol operations

 - Own the new-protocol review pipeline: given a new protocol, read the docs and contracts, assess the risk, and decide whether and on what terms we allocate

 - Review and sign vault rebalancing transactions as a multisig signer

 - Build monitoring and automation that catches a broken oracle, a depeg, a stuck withdrawal, or a bad allocation before users do

 - Participate as a security guardian across ether.fi http://ether.fi's web3 stack and operations

YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU

 - Write strong production Solidity: clean, secure, and designed around edge cases and failure modes

 - Are equally strong on the backend: services, automation, and tooling that hold up when they're running against real money

 - Know DeFi deeply enough to read a protocol's docs and contracts, understand where the yield actually comes from, and form your own view on where it breaks

 - Have 4+ years of industry engineering experience

 - Have shipped a real yield vault (ERC-4626, BoringVault-style, or your own architecture) and operated it after launch

 - Thrive in fast-moving environments where the best idea wins

Bonus

 - Experience at a vault platform, asset curator, or yield product with real TVL, either building the vaults or curating what goes into them

 - Hands-on with the strategies themselves: lending markets, LSTs and LRTs, basis and funding trades, stablecoin yield

 - Audit or security review background

 - You've hacked on this for fun: your own contracts, protocol audits, MEV bots, or just a lot of hours across DeFi protocols

jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
About ether.fi http://ether.fi

ether.fi http://ether.fi is one of the largest DeFi protocols on Ethereum. We started with weETH, a liquid staking token that now secures billions of dollars of staked ETH, and built outward from there: the Liquid vault range, which runs automated yield strategies across ETH, stablecoins and BTC, and ether.fi http://ether.fi Cash, a Visa card and neobank product that lets users spend directly against their on-chain balances.

Behind the protocol is a group of operating companies in Cayman, Brazil, the US, Canada and the UAE, including a regulated investment manager and a licensed VASP. We are continuing to open new markets and add additional regulated products, with finance playing a key role in this expansion.

The role

We're hiring a Head of Finance to run the finance function. Today finance sits with the COO/CFO and financial controller. We are looking for someone to own the following: month end, audits, budget, tax, treasury operations, fund NAV, payments and payroll. The CFO will set policy and sign off. You own everything else.

It's a small team. You'll have one accountant reporting to you and can hire as we grow, but you need to be comfortable doing the work yourself. We're based across several time zones and you'll be working with legal, compliance, ops and the product teams every week.

What you'll do

 - Run month end across all entities. Management accounts within 15 business days, quarterly reporting within 45 days.

 - Balance sheet recs, including wallets, exchange and custody balances against the ledger.

 - Revenue recognition for protocol fees, vault fees, card interchange and treasury income.

 - Lead our statutory audits.

 - Own the annual budget and monthly budget vs actuals. Every material assumption needs to be documented and something you can defend.

 - Cash forecasting.

 - Daily liquidity monitoring across fiat, stables and crypto. Weekly portfolio review and rebalancing to targets set by the CFO. Moving funds for payroll and payments.

 - Put intercompany agreements and a transfer pricing model in place with our advisers.

 - Tax and regulatory finance filings across Cayman, Brazil, US, Canada and UAE (economic substance, US information returns, CRA).

 - Weekly payment run, vendors, payroll and contractors in several countries, token vesting and payouts, expenses.

 - Card inventory and cost tracking with Ops.

 - Own the finance systems (QuickBooks, crypto sub-ledger, AP tool, payroll, cap table) and cut down the manual recs.

 - Work with Compliance, Ecosystem and Product on fee models and new launches. Help HR with comp budgets, relocations and payroll.

What we're looking for

 - Qualified accountant (CA, CPA, ACCA). Big 4 audit background preferred.

 - 8+ years post-qualification, at least 4 of them in-house at a crypto, fintech or asset management business.

 - Has run a finance function before, as controller or head of finance, across multiple entities and currencies.

 - Has owned audits end to end.

 - Hands-on with intercompany agreements and transfer pricing.

 - Comfortable with crypto: wallet recs, token accounting, staking rewards, NAV for crypto funds.

 - Organised and direct. Flags problems early rather than at month end.

 - Able to work in Cayman (right to work or eligible for a permit). Relocation support is available.

Nice to have

 - Cayman funds: CIMA registration, investment manager entities, working with administrators.

 - VASP, payments or card program experience, including interchange.

 - US and Canadian tax.

 - Multi-country payroll and token compensation.

 - QuickBooks Online, a crypto sub-ledger, AP automation.

What we offer

 - Competitive salary plus ETHFI tokens.

 - Relocation support to Cayman.

 - Direct line to the CFO and a finance function you get to shape, in a business with real revenue across staking, vaults and payments.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description:
ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.

ABOUT THE ROLE

At KOHO, Product Design is key to our brand identity and product differentiation. As a Senior Product Designer, you will be involved in every aspect of the product development process. You will be using your skills in UI and UX design, product design, interaction design, visual / audio / motion design and prototyping to create product experiences that wow and deliver measurable value.

We’re looking for someone who embraces innovation, including the use of Generative AI and other AI-powered tools to speed up workflows, explore creative solutions, and enhance design decision-making. Our dream candidate has a passion for understanding users and enjoys working closely with other designers, engineers, data analysts, and product managers to build the best banking experience for Canadians.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Work with Product Managers to develop and refine product strategy and vision (not just ‘how it works, looks’ but ‘why it should be built’)

 - Prepare wireframes, user flows, process flows, customer journeys and other artifacts to effectively communicate interactions and design ideas

 - Work within an iterative design process: rapid prototyping, initiating user experience research, incorporating feedback, launching quickly and testing hypotheses in an agile environment

 - Work as a part of an end-to-end product development team: collaborating early with and providing design direction to engineers, understanding technical requirements of what it takes to implement your designs

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to influence all aspects of the product from copywriting to lifecycle marketing

 - Evangelize our Design-centric product development process, and act as a design mentor to other designers and cross-functional partners

 - Leverage AI tools to streamline the design process, and uncover user insights

WHO YOU ARE

 - You bring 5+ years of experience on Consumer-facing products, with a focus on Mobile, thriving in fast-paced environments.

 - You communicate clearly and confidently, presenting your designs to a variety of audiences and articulating the rationale behind your decisions.

 - You apply user-centric design principles with ease, following web and mobile design standards and best practices, whilst challenging the status-quo.

 - You have a sharp eye for design and a deep understanding of how to craft intuitive, impactful user workflows.

 - You enjoy collaborating with others and are passionate about solving real user problems together.

 - You take initiative and navigate ambiguity with confidence, using your creativity and resourcefulness to find solutions.

 - You excel at solving complex problems and pride yourself on being highly self-sufficient.

 - You’re proficient in modern design tools like Figma.

 - You incorporate GenAI into your design workflows to boost creativity and efficiency.

 - You come prepared with a strong portfolio that showcases your product design skills and relevant experience.

 - You’re well-versed in designing for consumer-facing products, particularly in the social, financial, or broader B2C space.

The budgeted salary range for this role is $135,000-175,000 CAD / year. 

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS

À PROPOS DU POSTE

Chez KOHO, le design de produit est au cœur de notre identité de marque et de notre différenciation sur le marché. En tant que designer principal(e) de produit, vous participerez à toutes les étapes du processus de développement de produit. Vous mettrez à profit vos compétences en design UI et UX, en design de produit, en design d’interaction, en design visuel, audio et motion, ainsi qu’en prototypage, afin de créer des expériences produit marquantes qui génèrent une valeur mesurable.

Nous recherchons une personne qui adopte l’innovation, y compris l’utilisation de l’IA générative et d’autres outils propulsés par l’IA, pour accélérer les flux de travail, explorer des solutions créatives et améliorer la prise de décision en design. La personne idéale est passionnée par la compréhension des utilisateurs et utilisatrices et aime collaborer étroitement avec d’autres designers, ingénieur(e)s, analystes de données et chef(fe)s de produit afin de bâtir la meilleure expérience bancaire pour les Canadien(ne)s.

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

 - Collaborer avec les chef(fe)s de produit afin de développer et d’affiner la stratégie et la vision produit, en réfléchissant non seulement à la façon dont le produit fonctionne et se présente, mais aussi aux raisons pour lesquelles il devrait être conçu

 - Préparer des maquettes, parcours utilisateurs, flux de processus, parcours clients et autres livrables afin de communiquer efficacement les interactions et les idées de design

 - Travailler dans un processus de design itératif : prototypage rapide, lancement de recherches sur l’expérience utilisateur, intégration de la rétroaction, lancement rapide et validation d’hypothèses dans un environnement agile

 - Faire partie d’une équipe de développement de produit de bout en bout : collaborer tôt avec les ingénieur(e)s, leur fournir une orientation en design et comprendre les exigences techniques nécessaires à la mise en œuvre de vos conceptions

 - Collaborer avec des équipes multidisciplinaires afin d’influencer tous les aspects du produit, de la rédaction à la commercialisation du cycle de vie

 - Promouvoir notre approche de développement de produit centrée sur le design et agir à titre de mentor en design auprès d’autres designers et partenaires interfonctionnels

 - Tirer parti des outils d’IA afin d’optimiser le processus de design et de faire émerger des insights utilisateurs

QUI VOUS ÊTES

 - Vous possédez plus de 5 ans d’expérience dans la conception de produits destinés aux consommateurs, avec un accent sur le mobile, et vous évoluez avec aisance dans des environnements rapides

 - Vous communiquez avec clarté et assurance, présentez vos designs à divers publics et expliquez le raisonnement derrière vos décisions

 - Vous appliquez facilement les principes de design centrés sur l’utilisateur, en respectant les standards et les meilleures pratiques du design web et mobile, tout en remettant le statu quo en question

 - Vous avez un œil aiguisé pour le design et une compréhension approfondie de la façon de créer des parcours utilisateurs intuitifs et percutants

 - Vous aimez collaborer et vous êtes passionné(e) par la résolution collective de problèmes réels vécus par les utilisateurs

 - Vous faites preuve d’initiative et naviguez avec confiance dans l’ambiguïté, en misant sur votre créativité et votre débrouillardise pour trouver des solutions

 - Vous excellez dans la résolution de problèmes complexes et êtes fier(-ère) de votre grande autonomie

 - Vous maîtrisez des outils de design modernes comme Figma

 - Vous intégrez l’IA générative à vos méthodes de travail en design afin d’accroître votre créativité et votre efficacité

 - Vous présentez un portfolio solide qui met en valeur vos compétences en design de produit ainsi que votre expérience pertinente

 - Vous avez une bonne expérience en conception de produits destinés aux consommateurs, particulièrement dans les secteurs social, financier ou, plus largement, B2C

KOHO is for builders.

If you’re energized by challenge, motivated by mission, and want to be part of a team that punches above its weight - we want to hear from you.

 

The KOHO culture is one of collaboration, creativity, and diverse perspectives. We are committed to building and fostering an inclusive, accessible environment for everyone. If you have any questions, concerns, or requests regarding accessibility needs, please contact peopleaccessibility@koho.ca and the People and Culture team will be happy to help.

 - Hands-on experience planning and executing adversarial simulations, including scoping engagements, defining rules of engagement, and delivering post-engagement reporting.

Votre rôle consistera à préparer l’ensemble de l’entreprise à faire face aux cyberincidents, en commençant par l’équipe de sécurité pour ensuite étendre cette culture à tout KOHO. Lorsqu’un incident survient, vous faites partie de l’équipe d'intervention en agissant comme commandant d'incident ou en offrant votre soutien, selon le contexte et les exigences de la situation.

En plus de la réponse aux incidents, vous serez responsable de bâtir entièrement le programme d’ingénierie de la déception (deception engineering) de KOHO. Ce volet englobe à la fois les actifs de détection internes (pots de miel/honeypots, jetons canaris/canary tokens, utilisateurs leurres, miettes de pain/breadcrumbs) et la déception externe (identifiants fictifs, jetons canaris intégrés dans les interfaces clients et infrastructures leurres placées dans des zones accessibles aux attaquants). Ce programme génère des renseignements sur les menaces (threat intelligence) qui viennent alimenter nos logiques de détection, nos scénarios de réponse (playbooks) et le modèle global de menaces de KOHO.

 - Animer des simulations théoriques avec la haute direction (C-level) afin de tester la tolérance aux risques et les limites organisationnelles.

 - Documenter les leçons apprises, les améliorations opérationnelles et les mises à jour des scénarios de réponse. Mettre en œuvre l'ensemble de ces améliorations.

 - Diriger la réponse aux incidents et l'analyse informatique légale (DFIR) lors d'un cyberincident.

 - Prendre en charge la documentation post-incident afin de déterminer les facteurs contributifs et les leçons apprises.

 - Concevoir et déployer des actifs de déception internes pour détecter les mouvements latéraux, les menaces internes et les accès non autorisés au sein de l'environnement de KOHO.

 - Bâtir des capacités de déception externes, incluant de faux identifiants, des jetons canaris intégrés aux interfaces clients et des infrastructures leurres injectées dans des bases de données compromises ou d'autres surfaces accessibles aux attaquants.

 - Configurer les outils et actifs de déception afin de générer des renseignements exploitables sur les menaces et intégrer ces résultats dans la logique de détection, les scénarios de réponse et le modèle de menaces global.

 - Intégrer le flux de travail de triage et de réponse lié aux alertes de déception au sein des opérations existantes du SOC (du signal initial à l'enquête, jusqu'aux leçons apprises).

jobs.description:
ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a seasoned Director - Privacy Office (Deputy Chief Privacy Officer); Head of Advisory and RCM to lead the advisory heart of KOHO’s Compliance function and to own our Privacy Office end to end. Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer, you will be the trusted advisor to our business partners, such as product (lending, core banking, growth & onboarding), marketing, and user success, and before they build — translating a dense regulatory landscape into clear and useful guidance. You will also own KOHO’s privacy program, from Privacy Impact Assessments and consent design through to breach response.

 

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is energized by ambiguity, comfortable being the decision-maker in the room, and motivated by building durable programs rather than inheriting them. If you believe compliance should make good products possible rather than merely permissible, you’ll do your best work here.

 

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

COMPLIANCE ADVISORY

 - Act as the primary compliance advisor to business partners such as Product (lending, core banking, growth & onboarding), Marketing, Technology, Payments, Partnerships, and User Success, providing timely, practical, risk-based guidance on new products, features, campaigns, and business arrangements.

 - Own the regulatory advisory and interpretation function, resolving novel questions with clear written positions and a defensible rationale that stands up to regulatory and audit scrutiny.

 - Lead compliance review and sign-off of marketing materials, disclosures, and customer communications, and embed obligations into product development early.

 - Own the Whistleblower and Ethics programs, including intake, investigation oversight, non-retaliation, and ethics reporting to the Board.

REGULATORY COMPLIANCE MANAGEMENT

 - In collaboration with Legal, own the regulatory compliance management program: horizon scanning, impact assessment, and coordinated implementation of new and amended regulatory requirements.

 - Maintain KOHO’s regulatory obligations inventory and the mapping of obligations to responsible business owners, policies, and controls.

 - Lead the development, refresh, and governance of compliance policies, standards, and procedures, including annual approval cycles.

PRIVACY OFFICE (DEPUTY CHIEF PRIVACY OFFICER)

 - Own and mature KOHO’s enterprise privacy program, aligned to privacy legislation, and act as KOHO’s designated privacy lead.

 - Establish and run the Privacy Impact Assessment process for new products, vendors, data uses, and technology changes, and govern consent, collection, use, disclosure, retention, and cross-border transfer of personal information on a privacy-by-design basis.

 - Lead privacy incident and breach response, including containment coordination, real-risk-of-significant-harm assessments, regulatory and individual notification, and root cause remediation.

 - Own privacy complaints and access and correction requests, the data inventory and privacy notices, and privacy training and awareness across the organization.

TEAM LEADERSHIP AND INDUSTRY ENGAGEMENT

 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of compliance and privacy professionals, setting clear priorities and raising the technical bar of the function.

 - Partner closely with Financial Crime, Compliance Testing, Operational Risk, Internal Audit, Legal, and Tech/Cyber to ensure integrated coverage and no gaps between mandates.

 - Represent KOHO externally with industry associations, peer forums, and regulator outreach, staying ahead of emerging compliance, privacy, and conduct risk trends.

 - Prepare and present clear, decision-ready materials for senior management and applicable Board-level committees.

AI, AUTOMATION AND INNOVATION

 - Apply AI, automation, and data analytics to advisory intake, regulatory horizon scanning, marketing review, and privacy assessments.

 - Advise the business on the responsible use of AI, including model transparency, fairness, explainability, and personal information use.

 - Evaluate and implement RegTech and privacy technology that improves speed and consistency without diluting rigour.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 10+ years of progressive compliance, privacy, or regulatory legal experience in financial services, with meaningful time spent in an advisory capacity.

 - You have deep working knowledge of Canadian consumer protection, retail banking or payments, and privacy legislation.

 - You have built or substantially matured a privacy program or regulatory change program, not just operated one someone else designed.

 - You are a strong people leader and a clear writer — you can give a straight answer to a hard question and explain the reasoning behind it.

 - You’ve worked in regulated fintech, neobank, or direct-to-consumer financial institutions, you’re passionate about empowering financial wellness, and a relevant designation (CIPP/C, CAMS, CRCM, LL.B/JD, or equivalent) is an asset.

The budgeted salary range for this role is $190,000-230,000 CAD / year. 

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS

À PROPOS DU POSTE

Nous sommes à la recherche d’une personne chevronnée pour diriger les services-conseils — le cœur de la fonction Conformité de KOHO — et prendre en charge l’ensemble de notre Bureau de la protection des renseignements personnels. Relevant de la cheffe ou du chef de la conformité, vous serez la personne-ressource de confiance de nos partenaires d’affaires, notamment les équipes Produits (prêts, services bancaires de base, croissance et intégration), Marketing et Expérience utilisateur. Votre rôle consistera à traduire un environnement réglementaire complexe en conseils clairs et utiles, en amont de la conception de leurs produits et initiatives.

Vous serez également responsable du programme de protection des renseignements personnels de KOHO, de bout en bout : évaluations des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée, conception des mécanismes de consentement, gestion des incidents et intervention en cas d’atteinte à la protection des renseignements personnels.

Il s’agit d’un rôle de leadership très concret, pour une personne qui aime évoluer dans l’ambiguïté, qui est à l’aise de prendre des décisions et qui souhaite bâtir des programmes durables plutôt que de simplement assurer le maintien de programmes existants. Si vous croyez que la conformité doit rendre possibles de bons produits — et pas seulement les rendre permis —, vous pourrez vous épanouir pleinement dans ce rôle.

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

SERVICES-CONSEILS EN CONFORMITÉ

 - Agir comme principale personne-conseil en conformité auprès des partenaires d’affaires, notamment les équipes Produits (prêts, services bancaires de base, croissance et intégration), Marketing, Technologie, Paiements, Partenariats et Expérience utilisateur, en fournissant des conseils rapides, pratiques et fondés sur les risques pour les nouveaux produits, les fonctionnalités, les campagnes et les ententes commerciales.

 - Diriger la fonction de conseil et d’interprétation réglementaires, résoudre les questions inédites et formuler des positions claires, écrites et appuyées par une analyse défendable qui résiste à l’examen des organismes de réglementation et de l’audit.

 - Diriger l’examen et l’approbation de conformité des documents marketing, des communications aux clients et des informations à fournir, et intégrer les exigences réglementaires dès les premières étapes du développement des produits.

 - Être responsable des programmes de dénonciation et d’éthique, notamment la réception des signalements, la supervision des enquêtes, la protection contre les représailles et la présentation de rapports sur l’éthique au conseil d’administration.

GESTION DE LA CONFORMITÉ RÉGLEMENTAIRE

 - En collaboration avec le service juridique, être responsable du programme de gestion de la conformité réglementaire : veille réglementaire, évaluation des répercussions et mise en œuvre coordonnée des exigences nouvelles ou modifiées.

 - Tenir à jour l’inventaire des obligations réglementaires de KOHO et établir la correspondance entre ces obligations, les responsables d’affaires, les politiques et les contrôles en place.

 - Diriger l’élaboration, la mise à jour et la gouvernance des politiques, normes et procédures de conformité, y compris les cycles annuels d’approbation.

BUREAU DE LA PROTECTION DES RENSEIGNEMENTS PERSONNELS

 - Prendre en charge et faire évoluer le programme d’entreprise de protection des renseignements personnels de KOHO, conformément aux lois applicables, et agir à titre de personne responsable de la protection des renseignements personnels désignée par KOHO.

 - Mettre en place et administrer le processus d’évaluation des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée (EFVP) pour les nouveaux produits, les fournisseurs, les utilisations de données et les changements technologiques. Encadrer le consentement ainsi que la collecte, l’utilisation, la communication, la conservation et le transfert transfrontalier de renseignements personnels selon une approche de protection de la vie privée dès la conception.

 - Diriger la réponse aux incidents et aux atteintes à la protection des renseignements personnels, notamment la coordination du confinement, l’évaluation du risque de préjudice sérieux, les avis aux organismes de réglementation et aux personnes concernées, ainsi que la mise en œuvre des mesures correctives visant à éliminer les causes profondes.

 - Être responsable des plaintes en matière de protection des renseignements personnels, des demandes d’accès et de rectification, de l’inventaire des données, des avis de confidentialité ainsi que de la formation et de la sensibilisation à l’échelle de l’organisation.

LEADERSHIP D’ÉQUIPE ET RAYONNEMENT DANS LE SECTEUR

 - Diriger, accompagner et faire progresser une équipe de spécialistes de la conformité et de la protection des renseignements personnels, en établissant des priorités claires et en rehaussant le niveau d’expertise technique de la fonction.

 - Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Crimes financiers, Tests de conformité, Risques opérationnels, Audit interne, Affaires juridiques et Technologie/Cybersécurité afin d’assurer une couverture intégrée et d’éviter les angles morts entre les différents mandats.

 - Représenter KOHO auprès d’associations sectorielles, de groupes de pairs et d’organismes de réglementation, et demeurer au fait des tendances émergentes en matière de conformité, de protection des renseignements personnels et de risques liés aux pratiques commerciales.

 - Préparer et présenter des documents clairs, axés sur la prise de décision, à la haute direction et aux comités pertinents du conseil d’administration.

INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE, AUTOMATISATION ET INNOVATION

 - Utiliser l’intelligence artificielle, l’automatisation et l’analytique des données pour améliorer la gestion des demandes de conseil, la veille réglementaire, l’examen du matériel marketing et les évaluations des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée.

 - Conseiller l’entreprise sur l’utilisation responsable de l’intelligence artificielle, notamment en matière de transparence des modèles, d’équité, d’explicabilité et d’utilisation des renseignements personnels.

 - Évaluer et mettre en œuvre des solutions de technologie réglementaire et de protection des renseignements personnels qui améliorent la rapidité et la cohérence des processus sans en réduire la rigueur.

PROFIL RECHERCHÉ

 - Vous possédez au moins 10 ans d’expérience progressive en conformité, en protection des renseignements personnels ou en droit réglementaire dans le secteur des services financiers, dont une expérience substantielle en services-conseils.

 - Vous avez une connaissance approfondie de la protection des consommateurs au Canada, des services bancaires de détail ou des paiements, ainsi que des lois relatives à la protection des renseignements personnels.

 - Vous avez bâti ou fait évoluer de façon importante un programme de protection des renseignements personnels ou de gestion des changements réglementaires — vous n’avez pas uniquement assuré l’exploitation d’un programme conçu par quelqu’un d’autre.

 - Vous êtes une personne gestionnaire solide et une excellente rédactrice ou un excellent rédacteur : vous savez donner une réponse claire à une question difficile et en expliquer le raisonnement.

 - Vous avez travaillé dans une entreprise de technologie financière réglementée, une néobanque ou une institution financière s’adressant directement aux consommateurs. Vous avez à cœur de favoriser la santé financière et une certification pertinente — CIPP/C, CAMS

jobs.title: Director - Financial Crime Office (Deputy AML Officer); Head of Regulatory Relations and Testing
jobs.description:
ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.

ABOUT THE ROLE

 

We’re looking for an accomplished Director to lead four connected pillars of KOHO’s Compliance function: the Financial Crime Office, Regulatory Relations, Complaints Management, and second-line Compliance Testing. Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer, you will own how KOHO detects and disrupts financial crime, how we show up in front of our regulators, how we resolve customer complaints fairly, and how we independently test that our compliance controls actually work.

It is a broad mandate, and deliberately so — these are the areas where evidence matters most. You will bring the discipline, documentation quality, and executive presence to make KOHO’s control environment demonstrably effective, while keeping the customer experience in view.

 

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

FINANCIAL CRIME OFFICE (DEPUTY CHIEF AML OFFICER)

 - Lead KOHO’s AML/ATF and sanctions compliance program in accordance with the PCMLTFA and its regulations, and own the enterprise money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions risk assessment.

 - Oversee transaction monitoring, alert and case management, enhanced due diligence, sanctions screening, and suspicious transaction reporting, including the quality and timeliness of regulatory reporting to FINTRAC.

 - Direct KYC and customer risk rating standards, and partner with the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) to close typology gaps between fraud and financial crime detection.

 - Own the two-year AML effectiveness review, resulting remediation, and financial crime training.

REGULATORY RELATIONS

 - Serve as the central point of coordination for regulators, owning the cadence, quality, and consistency of KOHO’s regulatory correspondence and submissions.

 - Lead the end-to-end management of regulatory examinations, reviews, and information requests, including planning, evidence collection, response quality control, and issue tracking.

 - Own the regulatory findings and commitments register, driving remediation to validated closure.

 - Maintain the inventory of regulatory filings and the record of regulatory engagement, and prepare executives and subject matter experts for regulatory meetings.

COMPLAINTS MANAGEMENT

 - Own KOHO’s enterprise complaints management program, including policy, procedures, escalation pathways, and service standards.

 - Oversee handling of escalated and designated complaints, ensuring fair, timely, well-reasoned outcomes and clear written responses to customers.

 - Manage case flow with the external complaints body and oversee reporting to the FCAC and other applicable authorities.

 - Deliver complaints reporting and root cause analysis, converting complaint themes into product, process, and disclosure improvements that advance fair treatment of customers.

COMPLIANCE TESTING

 - Own the design and delivery of KOHO’s independent Compliance Testing Program, including methodology, quality standards, and reporting.

 - Develop the annual risk-based testing plan, scoped and prioritized from the regulatory obligations inventory and known risk concentrations; Collaborate with Operational Risk Management (ORM) on the selection of compliance controls.

 - Maintain a quality assurance process over testing outputs, including work performed by co-source or business process outsourcing partners, and report results and thematic conclusions into senior management and/or Board-level reporting.

TEAM LEADERSHIP AND INDUSTRY ENGAGEMENT

 - Lead, coach, and develop a multi-disciplinary team across financial crime, testing, and complaints, building bench strength and clear career paths.

 - Partner with Compliance Advisory and Privacy, Operational Risk, Internal Audit, Legal, and FIU to ensure integrated risk oversight.

 - Represent KOHO externally in industry associations, peer forums, and financial crime intelligence networks, staying ahead of emerging typologies, fraud trends, and regulatory developments.

 - Prepare and present decision-ready reporting to senior management and applicable Board-level committees.

AI, AUTOMATION AND INNOVATION

 - Apply AI, machine learning, RPA, and advanced analytics to transaction monitoring tuning, alert triage, complaints classification, and compliance testing.

 - Lead the development of automated testing scripts, intelligent workflows, and advanced reporting to increase coverage.

 - Evaluate and implement emerging RegTech and financial crime technology, and maintain model governance and tuning documentation for detection systems.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 10+ years of experience across AML and financial crime, compliance testing or audit, regulatory relations, or complaints within financial services.

 - You have deep working knowledge of Canadian consumer protection, AML, retail banking or payments, and privacy legislation.

 - You have direct experience managing regulatory examinations or information requests, and you’re composed under that kind of scrutiny.

 - You bring rigour to evidence and documentation — you believe a control that cannot be demonstrated has not been performed — and you deliver unwelcome findings constructively.

 - You’ve worked in regulated fintech, neobank, or direct-to-consumer financial institutions, you’re passionate about empowering financial wellness, and a relevant designation (CAMS, CFE, CIA, CPA, CRCM, or equivalent) is an asset.

The budgeted salary range for this role is $190,000-230,000 CAD / year. 

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS

À PROPOS DU POSTE

Nous sommes à la recherche d’une directrice ou d’un directeur chevronné pour diriger quatre piliers interconnectés de la fonction Conformité de KOHO : le Bureau de la criminalité financière, les relations avec les organismes de réglementation, la gestion des plaintes et les tests de conformité de deuxième ligne. Relevant de la cheffe ou du chef de la conformité, vous serez responsable de la façon dont KOHO détecte et perturbe les activités criminelles financières, interagit avec les organismes de réglementation, traite équitablement les plaintes des clients et vérifie de façon indépendante l’efficacité réelle de ses contrôles de conformité.

Il s’agit volontairement d’un mandat vaste : ce sont les domaines où les faits et les preuves sont les plus importants. Vous apporterez la rigueur, la qualité documentaire et la présence exécutive nécessaires pour démontrer l’efficacité de l’environnement de contrôle de KOHO, tout en gardant l’expérience client au cœur de vos décisions.

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

BUREAU DE LA CRIMINALITÉ FINANCIÈRE

 - Diriger le programme de KOHO en matière de lutte contre le blanchiment d’argent et le financement des activités terroristes (LBA/FT), ainsi que de conformité aux sanctions, conformément à la Loi sur le recyclage des produits de la criminalité et le financement des activités terroristes (LRPCFAT) et à ses règlements. Être responsable de l’évaluation à l’échelle de l’entreprise des risques liés au blanchiment d’argent, au financement des activités terroristes et aux sanctions.

 - Superviser la surveillance des transactions, la gestion des alertes et des dossiers, les mesures de vigilance renforcées, le filtrage des sanctions et la déclaration des opérations douteuses, notamment la qualité et la ponctualité des déclarations réglementaires auprès du Centre d’analyse des opérations et déclarations financières du Canada (CANAFE).

 - Diriger les normes relatives à la connaissance du client (KYC) et à l’évaluation du niveau de risque des clients, et collaborer avec l’Unité du renseignement financier (URF) afin de combler les écarts entre la détection de la fraude et celle des activités criminelles financières.

 - Être responsable de l’examen biennal de l’efficacité du programme de LBA/FT, du suivi des mesures correctives qui en découlent et de la formation en matière de criminalité financière.

RELATIONS AVEC LES ORGANISMES DE RÉGLEMENTATION

 - Agir comme point de coordination central auprès des organismes de réglementation et être responsable de la fréquence, de la qualité et de la cohérence de la correspondance et des déclarations réglementaires de KOHO.

 - Diriger la gestion de bout en bout des examens réglementaires, des évaluations et des demandes de renseignements, notamment la planification, la collecte des éléments probants, le contrôle de la qualité des réponses et le suivi des enjeux.

 - Être responsable du registre des constats réglementaires et des engagements, et piloter les mesures correctives jusqu’à leur résolution confirmée.

 - Tenir à jour l’inventaire des déclarations réglementaires et le registre des interactions avec les organismes de réglementation, et préparer la direction ainsi que les spécialistes concernés aux rencontres réglementaires.

GESTION DES PLAINTES

 - Être responsable du programme de gestion des plaintes à l’échelle de KOHO, notamment des politiques, des procédures, des mécanismes d’escalade et des normes de service.

 - Superviser le traitement des plaintes transmises à un niveau supérieur et des plaintes désignées, en veillant à ce que les décisions soient équitables, rendues en temps opportun et bien motivées, et que les réponses écrites aux clients soient claires.

 - Gérer le cheminement des dossiers auprès de l’organisme externe de traitement des plaintes et superviser les déclarations à l’Agence de la consommation en matière financière du Canada (ACFC) ainsi qu’aux autres autorités compétentes.

 - Produire les rapports sur les plaintes et les analyses des causes profondes, et transformer les tendances observées en améliorations aux produits, aux processus et aux communications, afin de favoriser un traitement équitable des clients.

TESTS DE CONFORMITÉ

 - Être responsable de la conception et de la réalisation du programme indépendant de tests de conformité de KOHO, notamment de la méthodologie, des normes de qualité et de la production de rapports.

 - Élaborer le plan annuel de tests fondé sur les risques, en établissant sa portée et ses priorités à partir de l’inventaire des obligations réglementaires et des concentrations de risques connues. Collaborer avec la gestion des risques opérationnels (GRO) à la sélection des contrôles de conformité.

 - Maintenir un processus d’assurance qualité pour les résultats des tests, y compris les travaux réalisés par des partenaires de co-impartition ou d’impartition de processus opérationnels, et présenter les résultats ainsi que les conclusions thématiques à la haute direction ou dans les rapports destinés au conseil d’administration.

LEADERSHIP D’ÉQUIPE ET RAYONNEMENT DANS LE SECTEUR

 - Diriger, accompagner et faire progresser une équipe multidisciplinaire en criminalité financière, en tests de conformité et en gestion des plaintes, en développant la relève et des parcours professionnels clairs.

 - Collaborer avec les équipes Services-conseils en conformité et Protection des renseignements personnels, Risques opérationnels, Audit interne, Affaires juridiques et URF afin d’assurer une surveillance intégrée des risques.

 - Représenter KOHO auprès d’associations sectorielles, de groupes de pairs et de réseaux de renseignement sur la criminalité financière, et demeurer au fait des nouvelles typologies, des tendances en matière de fraude et de l’évolution de la réglementation.

 - Préparer et présenter des rapports axés sur la prise de décision à la haute direction et aux comités pertinents du conseil d’administration.

INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE, AUTOMATISATION ET INNOVATION

 - Utiliser l’intelligence artificielle, l’apprentissage automatique, l’automatisation robotisée des processus (ARP) et l’analytique avancée pour optimiser le paramétrage de la surveillance des transactions, le triage des alertes, la classification des plaintes et les tests de conformité.

 - Diriger l’élaboration de scripts automatisés de tests, de flux de travail intelligents et de rapports avancés afin d’accroître la couverture des contrôles.

 - Évaluer et mettre en œuvre des solutions émergentes de technologie réglementaire et de technologie de lutte contre la criminalité financière, et maintenir la documentation relative à la gouvernance des modèles et au paramétrage des systèmes de détection.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Platform
jobs.description:
ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ready to Shape the Platform Behind KOHO's Products? 🚀

As Engineering Manager, Platform, you'll lead a full-stack platform team that owns KOHO's mobile and web platform (how our mobile app gets released and our frontend developer tooling), internal tooling and the risk domain. This is a unique opportunity to lead a team that spans platform and feature development, building the foundations other teams rely on while supporting user-facing functionality such as login and access management.

This is a role for someone who thrives in high-impact technical environments, turns ambiguous requirements into concrete solutions, and builds high-performing teams.

You'll report directly to the Senior Manager, Platform Engineering, collaborate closely with peer platform and feature teams, and manage key stakeholders including Risk, Product, and Security. Your team will also share ownership of our authentication and authorization systems, working hand in hand with the team that leads that space.

YOUR MISSION 🎯

Make it fast, safe, and easy for KOHO to build and ship great products, on mobile, on the web, and behind the scenes.

 - Build and lead a high-performing platform team: Manage a team of full-stack engineers (employees and partner contractors), set clear expectations, create real career growth paths, and maintain a culture of ownership and continuous improvement

 - Own the Mobile and Web platform: Lead how our mobile app gets released, from build pipelines and release trains to app store submissions, phased rollouts, and feature flagging, and keep our web platform healthy and scalable

 - Raise frontend developer experience, with AI at the core: Invest in frontend tooling, shared components, CI/CD, testing, and AI-assisted workflows so engineers across KOHO can build, test, and release with confidence

 - Own internal tooling for the organization: Deliver and maintain the internal tools our operations, support, and business teams rely on, treating them as products with real users and clear quality bars

 - Own the risk domain: Lead your team's ownership of risk-related systems and experiences, partnering with Risk and Compliance stakeholders to balance user experience, operational efficiency, and regulatory expectations

 - Manage key vendors: Own relationships with third-party vendors in your domain, from evaluation and integration through performance, cost, contract renewals, and migrations when needed

 - Own stability & production health: Keep your team's systems reliable through strong observability, a healthy support rotation, effective incident response, and steady reduction of tech debt

 - Collaborate across the platform: Work closely with the authentication and authorization team on initiatives that touch the mobile and web experience, and translate Platform OKRs into a focused quarterly roadmap

WHAT YOU'LL BRING 💡

We're looking for someone who:

 - Has strong full-stack engineering roots: 5+ years building and operating production software across web or mobile frontends and backend services, with enough hands-on depth to review designs, unblock engineers, and make sound architectural calls

 - Is a proven people leader: 1-3 years managing an engineering team (3-6 people), with demonstrated success coaching engineers, managing performance, hiring, and building an inclusive, high-trust team culture

 - Owns production outcomes: A track record of owning critical customer-facing or business-critical systems, setting and holding quality and reliability bars, and leading the team calmly through incidents

 - Manages vendors effectively: Experience owning third-party vendor relationships, holding partners accountable to outcomes, and making clear build-versus-buy decisions

 - Thrives in ambiguity: You can take high-level business objectives, structure the problem, and turn it into an actionable plan when requirements are not clearly defined

 - Balances strategy with execution: You can shape a roadmap and improve team process, then dive deep to unblock a tricky implementation or production issue

 - Communicates with exceptional clarity: You explain technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders, write clear docs, and build strong relationships with Product, Design, Risk, and peer engineering teams

WHAT SETS YOU APART 🌟

This role is best suited for someone who wants real growth - not just more tasks, but more scope, more impact, and more trust, and wants to make a real impact in the financial lives of Canadians.

 - You've owned mobile release and platform engineering: Experience with mobile CI/CD, release automation, app store processes, and frontend build tooling at consumer scale

 - You've built internal tools people love: You've delivered internal platforms or admin tooling that measurably improved how operations, support, or business teams work

 - You've worked in risk, identity, or auth domains: Experience in financial services, payments, fraud, identity verification, or authentication and authorization (e.g., OAuth/OIDC, SSO, MFA), where risk, security, and auditability shape product decisions. Nice-to-have: hands-on experience with vendors such as Onfido or Auth0

 - You're passionate about developer

experience:

You treat the platform as a product for internal engineers and invest in tooling, shared components, CI/CD, and self-service that make their lives better

 - You embrace AI-enabled workflows: You're excited about using AI to accelerate development, testing, and code review, and you help your team adopt it thoughtfully

 - You understand "you build it, you run it": You've built teams that own their systems end to end, from design through on-call, with strong observability and feature-flagged releases

The posted salary range for this role is $160,000 – $190,000 CAD / year.

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS

À PROPOS DU POSTE

Prêt à façonner la plateforme derrière les produits de KOHO? 🚀

En tant que gestionnaire en ingénierie, Plateforme, vous dirigerez une équipe plateforme full-stack responsable de la plateforme mobile et Web de KOHO (la façon dont notre application mobile est publiée et nos outils de développement frontend), des outils internes et du domaine du risque. Il s'agit d'une occasion unique de diriger une équipe qui couvre à la fois la plateforme et le développement de fonctionnalités, en bâtissant les fondations sur lesquelles reposent les autres équipes tout en soutenant des fonctionnalités destinées aux utilisateurs, comme la connexion et la gestion des accès.

Ce poste s'adresse à une personne qui s'épanouit dans des environnements techniques à fort impact, qui transforme des exigences ambiguës en solutions concrètes et qui bâtit des équipes performantes.

Vous relèverez directement du gestionnaire principal, Ingénierie de plateforme, collaborerez étroitement avec les équipes plateforme et fonctionnalités homologues, et gérerez des parties prenantes clés, notamment les équipes Risque, Produit et Sécurité. Votre équipe partagera également la responsabilité de nos systèmes d'authentification et d'autorisation, en travaillant main dans la main avec l'équipe qui dirige ce domaine.

VOTRE MISSION 🎯

Permettre à KOHO de concevoir et de livrer d'excellents produits rapidement, en toute sécurité et facilement, sur mobile, sur le Web et en coulisses.

 - Bâtir et diriger une équipe plateforme performante : gérer une équipe d'ingénieurs full-stack (employés et contractuels partenaires), fixer des attentes claires, créer de véritables parcours de croissance et entretenir une culture de responsabilisation et d'amélioration continue

 - Prendre en charge la plateforme mobile et Web : diriger le processus de publication de notre application mobile, des pipelines de compilation et des cycles de publication jusqu'aux soumissions aux boutiques d'applications, aux déploiements progressifs et aux indicateurs de fonctionnalités, et maintenir notre plateforme Web saine et évolutive

 - Améliorer l'expérience des développeurs frontend, avec l'IA au cœur : investir dans les outils frontend, les composants partagés, l'intégration et le déploiement continus (CI/CD), les tests et les flux de travail assistés par l'IA afin que les ingénieurs de KOHO puissent concevoir, tester et publier en toute confiance

 - Prendre en charge les outils internes de l'organisation : livrer et maintenir les outils internes sur lesquels comptent nos équipes des opérations, du soutien et des affaires, en les traitant comme des produits ayant de vrais utilisateurs et des normes de qualité claires

 - Prendre en charge le domaine du risque : diriger la responsabilité de votre équipe à l'égard des systèmes et des expériences liés au risque, en partenariat avec les parties prenantes Risque et Conformité, afin d'équilibrer l'expérience utilisateur, l'efficacité opérationnelle et les attentes réglementaires

 - Gérer les fournisseurs clés : gérer les relations avec les fournisseurs tiers de votre domaine, de l'évaluation et l'intégration jusqu'au rendement, aux coûts, aux renouvellements de contrats et aux migrations au besoin

 - Assurer la stabilité et la santé de la production : maintenir la fiabilité des systèmes de votre équipe grâce à une observabilité solide, une rotation de soutien saine, une réponse efficace aux incidents et une réduction constante de la dette technique

 - Collaborer à l'échelle de la plateforme : travailler étroitement avec l'équipe d'authentification et d'autorisation sur les initiatives touchant l'expérience mobile et Web, et traduire les OKR de la plateforme en une feuille de route trimestrielle ciblée

CE QUE VOUS APPORTEREZ 💡

Nous recherchons une personne qui :

 - Possède de solides bases en ingénierie full-stack : plus de 5 ans d'expérience en conception et en exploitation de logiciels en production, couvrant des interfaces Web ou mobiles et des services backend, avec une profondeur technique suffisante pour réviser des conceptions, débloquer les ingénieurs et prendre des décisions architecturales judicieuses
