jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

About the Role

Nubank Mexico operates as a regulated financial institution under CNBV oversight, processing millions of transactions daily for millions of customers. Preventing money laundering and terrorism financing is not only a regulatory obligation — it is central to our license to operate and to the trust our customers place in us.

The Senior Expert AML is the foremost domain expert in Mexico's PLD/FT compliance. This role owns the design and ongoing improvement of Nubank Mexico's AML program and ensures full adherence to the Disposiciones de Carácter General (DCG) referidas en el Artículo 115 de la LIC and its 2024 amendments, the FATF 40 Recommendations, and the Evaluación Nacional de Riesgos.

Beyond regulatory compliance, this person shapes how AML controls are embedded into product development, automated monitoring systems, and risk models — making Nubank Mexico both a safe and efficient financial institution. They influence across Engineering, Product, Legal, and Data teams, and represent Nubank before the CNBV and SHCP/UIF in regulatory interactions.

You'll be responsible for

Program Ownership & Regulatory Compliance

 - Design, maintain, and continuously improve the Nubank Mexico AML/PLD-FT compliance program, including the Manual de Cumplimiento, in line with DCG115 (Art. 115 LIC) and its August 2024 amendments.

 - Own the enfoque basado en riesgos (risk-based approach) methodology: develop risk indicators for ML and TF separately, maintain the customer risk segmentation model, and submit the annual Reporte de Operatividad to CNBV.

 - Ensure CNBV PLD/FT certification is current for yourself and all audit personnel; coordinate timely notifications to CNBV upon designations or revocations of compliance officers (within 10 business days).

 - Lead preparation and response for CNBV annual audits and ad hoc inspections; manage remediation plans and track implementation of regulatory findings.

 - Monitor FATF grey/black list updates, GAFI-flagged jurisdictions, and emerging typologies; adjust controls accordingly and apply reforzada due diligence to affected transactions and correspondents.

Transaction Monitoring & Reporting

 - Oversee the design and tuning of automated transaction monitoring (ATM) systems, including differentiated monitoring rules for persons físicas, morales, and fideicomisos.

 - Ensure ATM systems embed risk model execution and client classification as required by DCG115; lead biennial independent system evaluations.

 - Supervise the alert-to-SAR pipeline: manage the investigation process for unusual operations, escalation criteria, and timely filing of Reportes de Operaciones Inusuales (ROU), Reportes de Operaciones Relevantes (ROR), and Reportes de Operaciones con Dólares (ROED) to SHCP/UIF via goAML.

 - Define and maintain the reporting cadence for international fund transfer reports, including new requirements for concentrator accounts under the 2024 resolution.

KYC / Customer Due Diligence

 - Own the KYC/CDD framework: set standards for client identification, expediente integration, transactional profile construction, and the enhanced due diligence process for PEPs, high-risk clients, and foreign correspondents.

 - Oversee the dual-review process for customer files (reviewer independent from the person who integrated or updated the expediente) as mandated by DCG115.

 - Define EDD protocols for customers exceeding low-risk transactional thresholds and ensure mandatory interviews (presencial o remota) are conducted.

 - Manage PEPs and sanctions screening program (OFAC SDN, UN Security Council, SHCP blocked persons list); ensure real-time and periodic screening coverage.

Cross-functional Leadership & Product Compliance

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to embed AML controls by design in new product features, account types, and onboarding flows — particularly for non-presential account opening and digital identity validation (INE/SRE verification, Firma Electrónica Avanzada).

 - Advise on compliance implications of new product launches, partnerships, and geographic expansion in Mexico.

 - Design and deliver the annual AML training program for all relevant personnel, including board-level awareness and role-specific modules.

 - Represent the AML function internally and externally — including in product committees, risk forums, and regulatory interactions with CNBV and UIF.

We are looking for a person who has

Required experience & knowledge

 - 7+ years of AML/PLD-FT compliance experience in regulated financial institutions, banks, or fintech companies operating in Mexico.

 - Deep working knowledge of DCG referidas en el Artículo 115 de la LIC (including 2024 amendments), LFPIORPI, LGOAAC, and the SHCP/CNBV/UIF regulatory ecosystem.

 - CNBV PLD/FT certification (vigente), or willingness to obtain within the regulatory deadline. High proficiency in the certification exam topics: KYC, transactional profiling, ROU/ROR/ROED filing, PEPs, and national/international AML regimes.

 - Track record of building, scaling, or materially improving AML/compliance programs — especially in digital or high-volume transaction environments.

 - Hands-on experience managing transaction monitoring platforms: rule creation, threshold calibration, alert queue management, and model validation.

 - Experience managing or supporting CNBV PLD/FT audits end-to-end, including pre-audit readiness, fieldwork support, and findings remediation.

 - Strong analytical skills with experience working with large transaction datasets; comfort with SQL or Python for ad hoc investigations and reporting.

 - Experience with PEPs screening, OFAC/UN/SHCP sanctions list management, and enhanced due diligence processes.

 - Bilingual: Spanish (native) / English (professional working proficiency).

Nice to have

 - CAMS (Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist) or equivalent international certification.

 - Experience contributing to FATF mutual evaluations, national risk assessments, or GAFI working groups.

 - Background with RegTech / compliance automation tools (e.g., automated screening, AI-based transaction monitoring).

 - Experience at a high-growth tech company, neobank, or digital payments platform.

 - Familiarity with virtual asset regulations and FATF Recommendation 15 (Travel Rule, VASPs).

Key Regulatory Framework

This role operates within — and must demonstrate mastery of — the following frameworks:

 - Artículo 115 de la Ley de Instituciones de Crédito (LIC) and its Disposiciones de Carácter General (DCG), including the August 2024 resolution published in the DOF.

 - Ley Federal para la Prevención e Identificación de Operaciones con Recursos de Procedencia Ilícita (LFPIORPI).

 - Ley General de Organizaciones y Actividades Auxiliares del Crédito (LGOAAC).

 - FATF 40 Recommendations — particularly R.10 (CDD), R.12 (PEPs), R.15 (New Technologies), R.20 (Suspicious Transaction Reporting), and R.26–R.28 (Regulation, Supervision, FIU).

 - Evaluación Nacional de Riesgos 2023 and sectoral risk typologies published by UIF/SHCP.

 - NOM-151-SCFI (digitalization and preservation of data messages).

 

Benefits 

 - 17 days paid vacation per year. 

 - Life insurance. 

 - Health insurance. 

 - NuLanguage Program 

 - NuCare Program 

 - Extended Parental Leave

Hybrid — Our hybrid work model brings us to the office at least twice a week, on strategic days designed to maximize team connection and collaboration. For more details, visit building.nubank.com/nu-hybrid-work-model/

jobs.title: Consumer Compliance and CRA Analyst
jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE TEAM

At Nubank, Compliance is a strategic partner—not a tollgate. We view effective Risk Management & Compliance as the engine that maintains agility and empowers rapid, responsible growth across multiple global markets. Our team partners directly with internal clients using a targeted friction approach: we focus on the most relevant regulatory risks and embed compliance directly into product design rather than distributing rules after the fact.

The Global Compliance function serves as the Second Line of Defense, responsible for the full regulatory lifecycle: tracking new regulations, advising product and technology teams, testing controls, coordinating regulatory inspections, and monitoring remediation of regulatory issues.

This role is positioned at a pivotal moment. Nubank has received conditional approval for a US National Bank Charter. Should the charter be approved, this person will help build and operationalize the compliance and Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) infrastructure for a de novo national bank. In the near term, the role focuses on charter readiness—including supporting the development of the organizing bank's proposed CRA strategy—and on strengthening Nubank's consumer compliance posture under its current US operating model. The role requires someone who can build from scratch, own outcomes, and operate with an entrepreneurial mindset in a highly regulated environment.

JOB SUMMARY

We are seeking an experienced Compliance Analyst with dedicated compliance, risk, or audit experience at a regulated US financial institution or bank. This role carries primary ownership of Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) support and consumer protection compliance across Nubank's US deposit and unsecured lending products (personal loans and credit cards).

The CRA dimension of this role is central. Working within the Second Line of Defense, this person supports the oversight of CRA program execution and engages directly with community stakeholders to help assess local credit and community development needs. In the near term, and as part of charter readiness, this person will help drive the development of the proposed CRA Strategic Plan for the organizing bank.

This person reports to the Head of US Compliance, who is expected to serve as the bank's CRA Officer upon charter approval. The role provides direct support to that function.

The ideal candidate independently interprets and applies complex regulatory frameworks, translates regulatory requirements for cross-functional and business audiences, and develops proactive strategies to mitigate compliance risk. This person does not wait for direction—they identify issues, propose solutions, and drive them to completion.

Please note: This is a consumer compliance and CRA role. It is not a BSA/AML role. While a general awareness of the broader regulatory environment is useful, this position does not focus on anti-money laundering, sanctions, or financial crimes compliance. Candidates whose primary experience is in BSA/AML should review the focus areas below carefully before applying.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Community Reinvestment Act (CRA)

 - Support the development of the proposed CRA Strategic Plan for the organizing bank as part of charter readiness, including helping define assessment areas, measurable performance goals, and community development objectives appropriate to a digital banking model.

 - Engage directly with community organizations, nonprofits, local stakeholders, and community development practitioners to assess local credit and community development needs, and document those needs to inform the bank's CRA strategy.

 - Support the Second Line oversight of CRA program execution, including monitoring and providing effective challenge to the First Line on the adequacy of CRA-related activities, controls, and documentation.

 - Support the public engagement and comment process associated with the CRA Strategic Plan, should the bank pursue the strategic plan evaluation option.

 - Establish and maintain CRA records, data, and documentation to support performance evaluation readiness and examination preparedness.

 - Monitor CRA-related regulatory developments and supervisory expectations, and advise on implications for the bank's strategy and operations.

Compliance Advisory

 - Independently advise business partners on new product initiatives, marketing campaigns, servicing processes, and system implementations to identify and mitigate compliance risk before deployment.

 - Provide effective challenge to the First Line of Defense (Business Operations, Marketing, Product) on the design and adequacy of compliance controls, policies, and procedures.

 - Interpret and apply federal and state consumer protection laws to diverse and complex business scenarios, offering actionable compliance solutions—not just risk flags.

 - Assess the compliance and regulatory impact of internal operational events, audit findings, and external regulatory changes; develop and drive remediation plans in coordination with the First and Third Lines of Defense.

 - Translate complex regulatory requirements into plain-language guidance for cross-functional teams, business leadership, and where applicable, external stakeholders (e.g., partner banks, regulators).

 - Monitor emerging consumer banking trends, proposed rulemaking, and enforcement actions to proactively identify risks and advise the business on implications.

Charter Readiness & Compliance Infrastructure

 - Support the build-out of compliance and CRA infrastructure appropriate for a de novo national bank under OCC supervision, including policies, procedures, monitoring, testing, training, and recordkeeping. Activities are conducted in preparation for potential operations as a national bank, subject to charter approval.

 - Identify gaps in current compliance processes that would require enhancement or replacement under direct charter operations.

 - Conduct and contribute to compliance gap analyses comparing current processes, policies, and controls against OCC supervisory expectations for a de novo national bank; support the development of remediation roadmaps to close identified gaps.

 - Partner with Legal, Risk, and Operations to support readiness for potential OCC examinations and supervisory expectations, as well as potential examinations or inquiries from other regulators (e.g., CFPB, state regulators).

 - Execute compliance activities in alignment with Nubank's Global Compliance standards, frameworks, and methodologies, adapting them as needed for US regulatory requirements.

Mentoring & Knowledge Sharing

 - Mentor junior compliance team members and cross-functional partners on evolving regulatory landscapes, sharing insights and best practices.

 - Create and maintain compliance training materials, reference guides, and knowledge-base documentation to build institutional regulatory knowledge.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

REQUIRED

 - Dedicated compliance, risk, or audit experience within a US financial institution or bank.

 - Direct working experience with the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA), including familiarity with assessment area definition, community development activities, performance evaluation, recordkeeping, and—ideally—the CRA strategic plan option.

 - Experience engaging with community organizations, community development practitioners, or local stakeholders to identify and respond to community credit needs.

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Law, Business Administration, or a related field.

 - Deep working knowledge of US consumer compliance regulations, including ECOA/Reg B, TILA/Reg Z, UDAAP (Section 5 FTC Act / Dodd-Frank §1031), and EFTA/Reg E. Familiarity with FCRA/Reg V, GLBA/Reg P, and broader US banking regulations is a plus.

 - Demonstrated ability to independently interpret regulatory requirements and apply them to complex, ambiguous business scenarios—not just follow established playbooks.

 - Experience providing compliance advisory to product, technology, or business teams in a fast-paced environment.

 - Track record of building or materially improving compliance processes, controls, or monitoring programs (not just operating within existing ones).

 - Strong judgment, integrity, and discretion in handling sensitive and confidential matters.

 - Ability to communicate complex regulatory topics clearly to non-compliance audiences.

jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Regulatory Solutions Analytics at Nubank

As a company at the forefront of the financial revolution in Latin America, Nubank has grown exponentially since its inception — and keeping that growth healthy and people-centered depends on making critical, data-informed decisions every day. Regulatory Solutions Analytics is at the heart of that process: our analysts work across teams to structure and analyze data, challenge assumptions, and translate findings into real improvements for our customers.

You bring the depth, autonomy, and technical fluency to lead that work on the most demanding problems — and to raise the bar for the analysts around you. We’re looking for people who are curious, proactive, and energized by solving complex problems: not necessarily those with all the answers, but those who know how to find them.

About the Role

This role sits in Pack Analytics within Regulatory Solutions (Ops Defense). You’ll turn the analytical demands of our regulatory processes — KYC, AML, Judicial Orders, and others — into advanced analytics, models, and AI-powered solutions, while keeping the highest standard of quality for customer data and due diligence, in line with regulators and internal policies.

You will operate with growing autonomy: you solve well-defined problems independently and take on harder, more ambiguous challenges with the support of your team and manager, beginning to build deep expertise in your domain. Above all, you are excellent with data and genuinely passionate about artificial intelligence, proactively keeping yourself at the frontier of what these tools can do.

As a Sr Analyst in Regulatory Solutions Analytics, you’re expected to

 - Lead investigative, data-first work end to end: decide which data makes the most sense in each situation and, when it isn’t there yet, design the right tests or approaches to generate it.

 - Own advanced data analysis — run root-cause analysis, formulate and test hypotheses, and deliver effective solutions to challenging (though typically well-defined) problems with limited supervision.

 - Apply data science and statistical methods (e.g., anomaly detection, classification, segmentation, forecasting) to strengthen, scale, and automate regulatory decisions.

 - Use artificial intelligence as a core tool: leverage GenAI/LLMs and modern AI tooling to accelerate analysis, prototype solutions, and automate manual work — and proactively stay at the frontier of AI, bringing new techniques back to the team.

 - Work with large volumes of data using SQL, Python, and Scala — writing optimized queries and code to build a solid foundation for decision-making, knowing that not all answers live in the data, and that’s okay.

 - Build dashboards and visualizations (e.g., QuickSight, BigQuery) that go beyond the descriptive, surfacing trends, deviations, and forward-looking signals across historical and future horizons.

 - Apply solid, practical knowledge of data architecture and modeling (Data Mart, Data Lake, Data Warehouse) for analytical purposes, and manage dataset dependencies.

 - Understand our products and how they interact with other areas of the business, translating business, legal, and customer needs into quantitative metrics (KPIs, OKRs).

 - Support data-based decisions across your team, making calculated risk-taking comfortable despite uncertainty while keeping project flow.

 - Apply data governance fundamentals — data classification, secure access to PII, lineage, quality monitoring, and cost optimization.

 - Learn continuously and share knowledge generously, beginning to act as a reference in your area.

What we’re looking for

 - Strong analytical capacity: comfort with numbers and calculations, and the ability to solve problems methodically.

 - Excellent with data — advanced data analysis and/or data science — with the appetite to go deep on large, ambiguous transactional datasets.

 - Hands-on fluency with SQL and at least one general-purpose language (Python and/or Scala).

 - A real passion for artificial intelligence and machine learning, with a proactive habit of keeping up to date and applying new tools to real problems.

 - Business basics: understanding the dynamics between risks and opportunities, and how business and technical areas (product/engineering) interact.

 - Problem solving: creativity and practicality in tackling day-to-day challenges, with awareness of how your work impacts our customers’ experience and aligns with our purpose.

 - Proactive, autonomous, and curious — comfortable solving well-defined problems on your own and escalating the harder, ambiguous ones at the right time.

 - Clear, succinct, and effective communication in English and Spanish.

 - Openness to feedback and adaptability to a multifunctional, fast-changing environment.

It will be a differential if you…

 - Have data engineering experience — building and maintaining data pipelines, working with massive parallel processing (e.g., Spark / MPP), and using lineage and orchestration tools. (Data engineering is a strong plus.)

 - Hold a degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Finance, or Physics) with a solid statistical modeling and analysis background.

 - Have hands-on experience taking machine learning or AI / GenAI solutions to production.

 - Are familiar with “Know Your Customer” and AML / regulatory topics, applicable not only for Mexico but also for Brazil and other Latin American countries.

 

Location for this opportunity

Mexico City, Mexico

Work Model for this Role

This role is based full-time, on-site, at our Mexico City office.

Guided by our mission to fight complexity and empower people, we are redefining financial services in Latin America - and this is still just the beginning of the purple future we're building.

Our impact has been recognized by global rankings such as Time 100 Companies, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, and Forbes World's Best Bank.

About the AI Private Banker

The AI Private Banker is Nubank's intelligent financial partner - an AI-powered advisor that helps millions of customers understand their finances, make confident decisions, and take action seamlessly. It is built on Nubank's proprietary foundation models and data infrastructure, developed by the AI Core team that joined Nubank through the Hyperplane acquisition. This is not a chatbot bolted onto a banking app. It is a fundamental reimagining of how people relate to their money, powered by conversational AI, recommendation engines, and real-time personalization across mobile and web.

The AI Private Banker represents Nubank's next chapter and one of the company's highest-priority strategic bets. It sits at the intersection of banking and frontier AI, and every design decision here directly shapes how millions of people experience financial guidance.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Design Manager (M4) to lead the design organization for the AI Private Banker team in Palo Alto.

As Sr Design Manager, you will lead a multidisciplinary team of product designers and content designers (6+) crafting the AI Private Banker experience - shaping how customers interact with our AI advisor, how trust is earned, and how complex insights become simple, actionable, and human.

But you are no longer just building for the AI Private Banker vertical. You are establishing the foundational experience systems that will power AI across all of Nubank, while ensuring alignment with the broader Magic App vision (Nubank's next-generation unified app experience). In this context, you will help define the design vision, systems, cultural anchors, and rituals that make this product feel unmistakably Nubank: clear, kind, and empowering - bridging product-specific excellence with company-wide coherence.

You will partner closely with Rohan Ramanath (GM, AI Core) and the broader product, data science, and engineering leadership to translate AI capabilities into trusted, explainable human experiences. This is a high-visibility role with senior stakeholder exposure across the US and Brazil, requiring someone who can navigate ambiguity, align teams across borders and time zones, and find structure in an emerging space.

What You'll Do

- Lead and inspire a multidisciplinary team of product designers and content designers (6+) working on conversational, visual, and systemic layers of the AI experience
- Define and evolve the design north star for the AI Private Banker - how it looks, feels, and behaves across touchpoints
- Partner with product, data science, and engineering to translate AI capabilities into trusted, explainable human experiences
- Build and scale design systems for AI interaction patterns (voice, confidence levels, error recovery, transparency)
- Coach and grow the team - helping them balance craft excellence with experimentation and speed
- Drive cross-functional alignment, ensuring the design voice stays consistent from early prototypes to production
- Create frameworks for evaluating AI experience quality - usability, emotion, trust, and value perception
- Establish the cultural anchors and rituals that make the design team operate with clarity, purpose, and velocity
- Represent design to senior leadership across the US and Brazil, navigating complex cross-functional and cross-cultural dynamics

What Great Looks Like

- You have built or led design teams working on AI- or data-powered experiences (e.g., personalization, recommendations, chat, insights)
- You think systemically but care deeply about detail and tone
- You are a natural coach - you know how to elevate others' craft and clarity
- You balance strategic thinking with the ability to dive deep into design problems
- You are comfortable working with uncertainty and helping teams find structure in emerging spaces
- You advocate for human values in AI - fairness, clarity, empathy - not as slogans but as design principles
- You thrive in high-growth, high-change environments and can adapt as the company, team structures, and priorities evolve
- Experience in fintech, banking, or regulated industries is a plus but not required

Why This Role Matters

The AI Private Banker represents Nubank's next chapter: helping people feel in control of their financial journey through intelligence that listens, learns, and guides. Design leadership here means more than building interfaces - it means shaping how AI meets humanity, every day, at the scale of 100 million+ customers.

We are hiring a Staff Software Engineer to be the foundational technical lead on the newly established Product Workflow Reinvention team inside Global Products. Product Workflow Reinvention aims to replace the current, human-centric approach with an AI-native workflow. As the foundational engineer on this team, you will own the end-to-end technical architecture and build the initial internal platforms that ship weekly improvements to how Nubank builds products.

 

Mission

Design and operationalize the foundational technical strategy for Product Workflow Reinvention so that:

 - Intent becomes execution: Product requirements, research, and technical specs flow seamlessly into AI agents and domain execution tools with complete legibility and provenance.

 - Platform primitives are built for AI-native engineering: Product and platform teams consume well-architected workflows, state machines, and event systems designed specifically for agentic execution.

 - Every slow step in the life cycle has a tool: Product and engineering teams get first-class tooling for technical discovery, prototype-to-code experimentation, self-serve customer data, service health, and ops automation.

 - Agentic workflows scale safely, deterministically, and economically: Evaluation harnesses and integration patterns let LLM agents perform complex build tasks reliably, at a defensible cost per outcome, while keeping humans in the loop at strategic decision gates.

 - The workflow encodes what good looks like, so speed does not come at the cost of rigor.

 

Core Responsibilities

 - Lead the architecture of the orchestration layer: Own the end-to-end architecture of the single system of record, including data models, work legibility, and spec delivery to domain agents.

 - Design AI-native platform primitives: Build new platform abstractions from scratch, applying deep backend expertise to workflows, state management, event orchestration, and agent integrations.

 - Make agents reliable and affordable: Design agentic workflows, evaluation harnesses, and integration patterns that turn frontier models into practical velocity multipliers. Own the cost side of that equation through context design, model selection, and knowing when a deterministic component beats an inference call.

 - Ship the first-generation workflow tools: Build and iterate on the internal products that remove the slowest steps in the life cycle, from research and requirements generation to technical discovery, design-to-code experimentation, self-serve customer data, service health, and ops automation. Pick the sequence based on where teams actually lose the most time.

 - Operate in a high-autonomy, greenfield environment: Translate broad product vision and monthly milestones into concrete architectural decisions, implementation roadmaps, and sequencing.

CORE QUALIFICATIONS

 - Senior Staff-Level Engineering

Experience:

Proven track record designing, building, and operating complex backend or platform systems at scale.

 - End-to-End Architectural Ownership: Demonstrated ability to set technical direction, write comprehensive design docs/RFCs, and establish primitives that other engineers build against. Expertise in data modeling, workflow engines, state machines, and event-driven architecture.

 - 0-to-1 Platform Delivery: Experience leading ambiguous platform initiatives from early discovery to launch and rapid iteration. Comfort operating in small, fast-moving environments by creatively combining APIs, open-source tools, and AI models rather than over-engineering.

 - Built for other builders: Experience building internal tools or platforms whose users were other product creators, with evidence you drove real adoption rather than only shipping capability. You understand why teams abandon an internal tool in week two. Bonus: you have worked on a customer-facing product that also became a platform other products were built on.

 - AI and agentic conviction: Strong, well-reasoned conviction around LLM agents, agentic systems, or spec-driven development, with real examples of using AI tools, automation, or decision-support mechanisms to accelerate development workflows. jobs.title: Head of Design, Digital Assets
jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

HEAD OF DESIGN (HANDS-ON), DIGITAL ASSETS

We are building open money and open financial services — not "crypto."

The Digital Assets team at Nubank is reimagining how a financial services platform can use blockchain technology to solve real problems for real people — without ever making customers think about the blockchain at all. We have deliberately renamed ourselves from Crypto to Digital Assets, and we have effectively banned the word "crypto" internally. We do not do crypto for crypto's sake. We do blockchain banking.

The reference point is Apple Pay. It runs on cryptography, public and private keys, and secure tokenization inside a secure enclave. Apple never says any of that. It says "on device," and "it just works." That is the standard for everything we ship.

THE ROLE

We are looking for a hands-on design leader to join the Digital Assets team in Palo Alto. You will be the lead design voice for a genuinely new category: making digital assets — Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and stablecoins — as simple, accessible, and trusted as a debit card swipe.

This role sits at the intersection of consumer product design, financial innovation, and zero-to-one invention. Much of what you will design has never existed in consumer form before. You will not be asked to study what the incumbents did; the explicit instruction is to carve a new path.

WHAT YOU WILL DESIGN

 - The buy, hold, and sell experience for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Digital Dollars, etc. — designed to feel intuitive, familiar, and clear from the first interaction.

 - Earning, also known as staking: an experience that lets customers put eligible digital assets to work and earn rewards with clarity, control, and trust — without exposing the protocol mechanics underneath.

 - Onchain transfers and payments: sending, receiving, and using digital assets in ways that feel as simple and dependable as moving money today, while the underlying blockchain complexity stays out of the customer’s way.

 - The invisible infrastructure layer that powers core functionality across the entire company, including the US build.

 - Both the customer experience and the platform that other teams will draw on for future launches.

 - New ways for people to own, move, use, and grow value across financial products and borders — shaping a flexible foundation for what open money can become without being constrained by today’s conventions.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Consumer instincts over crypto fluency. Deep domain experience in crypto is not the point here — and can even work against you. If your instinct is to explain custody models or gas fees to a customer, this is not the seat.

 - Mobile expertise is a must-have. There is no desktop app in Brazil; effectively no web. Strong recent mobile work is non-negotiable, and a primarily B2B or enterprise background is a hard fit.

 - Zero-to-one experience. You have designed products that did not exist before, where there were no references to copy, and you thrived in the ambiguity.

 - A product marketing mindset. You care about the words, the positioning, and how it feels — not just the design elements. Our touchstone is "a thousand songs in your pocket," decided before the product was designed.

 - The ability to hide complexity. You have made something complicated feel obvious and delightful. Products that resonate with us: Cash App, Apple, the Tesla app, Duolingo, Wise, Revolut.

 - Fintech experience is a plus, never a requirement. We will teach you the compliance, legal, and regulatory ropes. What we cannot teach is the instinct to dream a magical experience first.

 - A short line to the business. The design team reports directly to the GM of the business unit. For a senior designer, that means unusual room to shape strategy rather than receive it.

HOW WE WORK

 - Dream first. The hiring manager's framing is: "Dream the magical experience first. We'll tell you afterwards what's not allowed."

 - No desktop-first. Everything is mobile-first, consumer-first.

 - No copy-and-paste. No copying from Coinbase or Robinhood. We are deliberately different.

 - The US is part of the trajectory. You will be shaping work that serves the next phase of global growth.

THE TEAM

You will report directly to Michael Rihani, GM of the Digital Assets business unit. Michael is a product leader with close to twenty years of experience, including four years at Apple on Apple Pay, leading Bitcoin and consumer financial services at Cash App and Coinbase, and directing Supercharging UX and Bitcoin payments at Tesla. He believes the biggest thing the industry is missing is storytellers and design people who can make the technology disappear.

INTERVIEW PROCESS
1. Portfolio review with Ethan Eismann (CDO, Nubank) — asynchronous
2. Live portfolio presentation with 2-3 design leaders and/or senior designers (~1 hour)
3. Hiring manager interview with Michael Rihani
4. Possible additional interviews. This interview process is subject to change, and may evolve with the hiring process. We appreciate your flexibility.

You will propose, build, implement, optimize, and measure paid media campaigns end to end, operating in a test-and-learn model to find the most efficient paths to reach and convert audiences — with particular focus on the mass affluent target, reaching them in the key demographic and geographic areas aligned to Nu's product offerings, from national brand campaigns down to regional, state, and city-level activation.

jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Location: U.S./Canada East Coast, including New York City, or Brazil (Eastern timezone for Europe-compatibility)

---

THE ROLE

We're launching a brand-new global account into dozens of markets at once — multi-currency holdings, yield, diversification across digital assets, and a suite of debit cards, built for people whose work and family span borders. The infrastructure underneath is powered by stablecoins and open financial services, but that complexity is fully abstracted. What the customer feels is a delightful, magical consumer product — as simple and effortless as anything Apple makes.

This is the project where every new thing at Nu lands first: the Magic App, the next evolution of the design system, new components and patterns. You'd have unusual room to experiment, iterate, and push the system forward rather than just consume it. The benchmark isn't the domestic market — it's global leaders like Revolut and Wise, and we're building to raise the bar past them.

As Head of Design for this initiative, you'll own the design function for the entire project. This is a player-coach role: you'll manage a team, but you'll also stay deeply in the craft — prototyping, refining, and setting the standard by doing, not just by directing. We need someone whose work itself is the bar.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

* Lead the design function for Nubank's most ambitious global expansion — a multi-currency account allowing transfers to 35+ countries.

* Set and hold the craft bar at a global standard, benchmarking against the best fintech products in the world (Revolut, Wise, and beyond).

* Stay hands-on. You manage people, but you're also in the work — shipping design, prototyping, and elevating every surface and interaction.

* Push the design system forward. This product is the proving ground for new components and patterns that flow back into Nu's global design system. You don't just use the system; you evolve it.

* Navigate the balance between creative freedom and organizational maturity — earning autonomy by influencing and persuading the central design organization, contributing patterns back to the system, and building bridges rather than working in isolation.

* Collaborate closely with engineering, product, and the broader design organization to ship experiences that feel magical and effortless to customers across China, Italy, Spain, and dozens of other markets.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

* Craft first. Extreme attention to detail and a portfolio that demonstrates world-class product design — the kind of work that stands out against Revolut, Wise, or Apple.

* A hands-on manager. You've led teams, but you still design. You set the bar by doing, not just by directing.

* Fintech-adjacent domain experience. You've worked in or around financial products — payments, cards, banking, digital assets, consumer finance. If you come from outside finance, you should have extraordinary craft and a track record of making complex products feel dead simple.

* A system-level collaborator. You know how to operate within a mature design organization — influencing the global system, contributing patterns, and partnering with central teams rather than working around them.

* A bar-raiser. You're not satisfied with "good enough." You push your team and yourself to the next level, especially when competing against the best in the world.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT

A global account designed for people with cross-border lives — those who work across markets, have family in different countries, or need to move money internationally with ease. It offers multi-currency holdings, yield, diversification across digital assets, and a set of debit cards. The underlying technology is powered by stablecoins and open financial services, but that's invisible to the user. What they experience is a consumer product that feels as simple and delightful as anything Apple makes.

The product is launching nonlinearly into 35+ countries simultaneously — customers in China, Italy, Spain, and beyond. This is Nubank's most ambitious global expansion to date, and the design bar must match the ambition.

INTERVIEW PROCESS
1. Async portfolio review with Ethan Eismann (CDO).
2. Live portfolio presentation (1 hour) — walkthrough of your best work with the design leadership team.
3. Hiring manager interview (45 min) with Thomaz Fortes and Thais Burin.
4. Final conversation with Ethan if needed.

jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE ROLE

Every Nubank office runs on an IT Room that most people never see. Power distribution, cooling, structured cabling and fiber are the layer that keeps thousands of Nubankers connected and working — and when that layer fails, entire sites stop.

Nubank's office portfolio is growing across countries, and today each site has been built to its own standard. The ETS team owns the physical layer of these environments — structured cabling, optical fiber and, in partnership with other teams, power distribution, HVAC, fire protection and physical security systems. This role exists to bring one engineering standard to all of them.

As Lead Infrastructure Engineer for Global Office IT Physical Infra, you are the technical reference for IT Room infrastructure across Nubank's global office portfolio. You assess and size environments, define the technical specifications new sites and expansions must meet, and coordinate the vendors and construction teams who build them — so that an IT Room in Miami, São Paulo or Mexico City is built, documented and operated the same way.

This is a senior individual contributor role with technical authority rather than direct reports. You set the standard, you review the projects against it, and you catch the gaps before they become outages.

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Assessing and sizing IT Rooms for expansion and improvement projects, defining the technical and physical specifications that meet real capacity needs, optimize resource use, and hold to operational standards.

 - Executing deployment projects for new environments and expansions in compliance with established technical specifications, and coordinating deployment logistics end to end while ensuring quality standards throughout.

 - Acting as the interface between internal teams and external vendors — translating business needs into infrastructure requirements, work orders and technical specifications — and managing those vendors and service providers to quality, deadline and compliance with Nubank's standards.

 - Coordinating with construction and engineering teams during the build-out of new offices, ensuring IT Room specifications are met from the earliest project phases rather than retrofitted later.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

The Operational Risk Specialist, plays a vital role within the operational risk management function at Nu Mexico. The main duties involve identifying, assessing, monitoring, and mitigating operational risks that may hinder the company from reaching its objectives. This is accomplished by developing methodologies and ensuring their implementation and execution within the first line of defense. This process includes training, review and challenge, monitoring key risk indicators, and escalating issues in appropriate Risk Forums. This role involves close collaboration with different departments and teams to execute various Operational Risk programs aimed at reducing and controlling the likelihood and impact of adverse operational risk events.

YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR
1. Lead the oversight and continuous improvement of the Op Risk Management System, ensuring that policies, methodologies, procedures, governance practices, and supporting documentation remain aligned with local regulation and global standards.
2. Lead and coordinate the annual and continuous RCSA process, maintaining high-quality risk and control matrices by ensuring that operational risks are properly identified, documented, classified, assigned to processes and business lines, and linked to accountable owners and controls.
3. Perform independent 2LoD review and challenge of 1LoD risk assessments and controls, including the evaluation of inherent risk, residual risk, control design, control execution, supporting evidence, and overall control effectiveness.
4. Own the governance and periodic maintenance of risk matrices across macroprocesses, ensuring that changes in products, processes, regulations, systems, incidents, control gaps, and organizational priorities are properly reflected, documented, and traceable in the institutional risk inventory.

6. Monitor operational loss events, incidents, and control gaps; lead or support root cause analysis; ensure accurate and timely registration; and define corrective, preventive, and improvement actions to reduce the likelihood of recurrence.
7. Design, manage, and enhance the Key Risk Indicator program for priority operational risks, ensuring that each applicable risk in the RCM has measurable indicators, defined amber and red thresholds, reliable data sources, periodic monitoring, documented analysis, and appropriate escalation.
8. Evaluate operational risks associated with new products, features, processes, operational changes, and other initiatives, ensuring that potential control gaps are identified, mitigation plans are defined, and required actions are completed before launch or formal implementation.
9. Prepare and present accurate, well-structured risk reports, dashboards, and management materials for senior leadership, the Non-Financial Risk Technical Forum, the Risk Committee, and other governance bodies, ensuring consistency and traceability to the RCM, loss-event database, KRI inventory, and control-gap management tools.

ABOUT THE TEAM

This is a build role. Nubank is standing up its first Global Creative & Brand Foundations Center of Excellence (CoE): a central hub sets best practices, capacity planning, and quality measurement, while markets retain execution. You'll be defining the operating model as you go, in close partnership with Senior Leadership and the regional creative leadership.

The mandate is specific: Brand Foundations and the Creative Center of Excellence. Own the craft and brand disciplines globally and Execution stays local. Brand Foundations is a small, Brazil-based team (currently three to four people) that has owned Nubank's brand refresh, sonic identity, and institutional design system; Nubank's institutional brand work globally is also moving into this role's remit. Your job is to build the system, standards, career paths, hiring bar, tooling, and review cadence, that lets creative and brand quality hold as Nubank multiplies markets and headcount.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This role owns Brand and Creative globally for Nubank — not an advisory function reviewing guidelines from the sidelines, but full, end-to-end accountability for how the brand shows up everywhere Nubank operates.

The mandate centers on two things:

 - Setting the creative and brand bar. Define what "great" looks like concretely enough that regional teams can hold themselves to it, rather than relying on a single senior reviewer to catch problems after the fact.

 - Building the infrastructure behind great creative work — tooling, review cadence, and governance — so quality can scale without linear headcount growth.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Hiring bar & talent. Set and protect the hiring bar for creative talent in every market where Nubank hires. Recruit senior creative leaders and stay closely involved in senior creative hires as the Center of Excellence builds out. Coach and seniorize existing creative talent over time, particularly in Brazil.

 - Scalable tooling. Build the tools and workflows — including AI-assisted ones — that let creative quality scale without linear headcount growth.

 - Review cadence & governance. Run a structured, content-focused creative review cadence that replaces today's ad hoc, adversarial feedback loops between markets and leadership.

 - Creative direction beyond the traditional campaign. Push the creative product past efficiency-driven, format-first advertising toward earned media and content built to be genuinely watched, not just placed.

Core Workstreams
1. Brand Foundations — Own brand refresh, sonic identity, and the institutional design system, plus Nubank's institutional brand presence company-wide, in close partnership with Cristina Junqueira.
2. Creative Center of Excellence — Own creative output company-wide: campaigns, social content, influencer marketing, and marketing stunts. Set the creative and brand bar that lets regional teams hold themselves to a consistent standard — distinct from media planning and channel measurement, which remain with regional teams.
3. Creative Production & Agency Management — Build an in-house production capability and direct the roster of external creative agencies.

QUALIFICATIONS

Professional Experience & Education

 - 10+ years in creative or brand leadership, with a track record of setting standards across multiple markets or business units — not just producing work for one.

 - Demonstrated experience building the infrastructure behind good creative (career ladders, review processes, hiring bars), not only a portfolio of campaigns.

 - Agency or in-house creative director background; strong agency-side creative leadership experience is a plus.

 - Fintech or financial services experience is useful context, though not required.

 - A clear point of view on how AI tools change the economics of creative production at scale, with genuine appetite to build with them rather than bolt them on.

Competencies & Attributes

 - Comfortable operating inside a matrixed, multi-market organization, with the judgment to raise the craft bar without steamrolling the local teams who own execution.

 - Experience developing junior and mid-level creative talent into senior roles, including hands-on coaching of raw talent toward more refined execution.

 - Strong systems-thinking orientation: able to build the structure behind creative work (leveling, tooling, governance), not only produce it personally.

 - Comfortable working across English- and Portuguese-speaking teams, given close, regular collaboration with Brazil-based creative talent and leadership.

About the role

In this role, you will sit at the strategic intersection of high-scale distributed backend systems, foreign exchange (FX) engines, international payment rails, and global compliance platforms. You won't just maintain existing pipelines, you will architect the foundation that enables instant, low-cost, multi-currency money movement for millions of users across borders.Your mission: maintain and grow a resilient, multi-country remittance engine that abstracts away complex global payment rails and regulatory requirements into simple, reliable platform capabilities.

What You Will Own & Build

 - Core Remittance Platform Architecture: Design and evolve the long-term technical vision for multi-currency money movement, FX rate locking, payout routing, and ledgering across international corridors.

 - Global Rail Integration Strategy: Architect plug-and-play integrations with global payout partners, banking networks, and local clearing rails (e.g., PIX, SPEI, FedNow, SWIFT) with ultra-high reliability and low latencies.

 - Resilient Ledgering & FX Management: Build transaction execution engines that guarantee exact-once delivery, deterministic ledger balancing, real-time liquidity management, and auditability under massive concurrency.

 - Compliance & Risk System Abstractions: Partner with AML, KYC, Sanctions Screening, and Regulatory Engineering teams to embed real-time screening seamlessly into payment paths without degrading user experience or throughput.

 - Technical RFC Leadership: Drive cross-organizational consensus on high-impact architectural decisions through detailed RFCs, design reviews, and technical documentation.

 - Engineering Mentorship: Multiply organizational velocity by mentoring senior engineers across payments squads in distributed systems principles, resilience engineering, and payment domain knowledge.

What We Are Looking For

 - Tenure in Backend Software Engineering: Proven track record of designing, operating, and scaling highly available, mission-critical backend distributed platforms in demanding environments (e.g., fintech, payments, banking, or cloud platform infrastructure).

 - Deep Payments Domain Expertise: Hands-on experience building remittance systems, cross-border payments, multi-currency ledger engines, FX execution services, or integrations with international payment clearing systems.

We value small, independent teams that move fast, own their decisions end-to-end, and hold themselves to a high bar for quality and craft.

Increasingly, that work also includes Generative AI and Agentic Engineering. Depending on the problem, our engineers design and build systems that combine models, tools, workflows, evaluation loops, and human oversight to solve real business tasks reliably in production.

Role Summary

The Global Head of Sanctions owns the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of Nubank's global sanctions compliance program across every market the company serves or plans to enter. This includes compliance with U.S. sanctions administered by OFAC, as well as EU, UN, UK OFSI, and other applicable regimes. Based in Tysons, VA — close to Washington, D.C.— this leader is Nubank's principal voice on sanctions matters with U.S. regulators and acts as the central point of accountability for sanctions risk as the company expands beyond Latin America. The role combines deep technical sanctions expertise with the people leadership and stakeholder management needed to run a program across multiple countries, languages, and regulatory regimes.

Key Responsibilities

 - Design, own, and continuously enhance Nubank's global sanctions policy framework, ensuring alignment with OFAC, EU, UN, and other relevant sanctions regimes across all current and future markets.

 - Direct the end-to-end sanctions screening program, including customer (onboarding and ongoing) screening, transaction and payments screening, and the systems, vendors, and models that power them.

 - Oversee watchlist and reference data management, including list ingestion, update cadence, and screening logic tuning to balance detection effectiveness against false-positive rates.

 - Lead investigation and escalation of potential and true sanctions hits, including disposition decisions, blocked and rejected transaction handling, and required regulatory filings and reporting.

 - Serve as Nubank's primary interface with OFAC, Treasury, and other regulators on sanctions matters, including managing examinations, inquiries, and voluntary self-disclosures where applicable.

 - Advise business, product, and partnerships teams on sanctions risk in new products, markets, customer segments, and third-party relationships before launch.

 - Monitor geopolitical and regulatory developments and translate them into timely program updates.

 - Coordinate independent testing, internal audit, and regulatory examinations of the sanctions program, and drive remediation of identified gaps.

 - Own sanctions training and awareness programs for employees, contractors, and relevant third parties across the organization.

Qualifications

Required Professional Experience & Education:

 - 10+ years of progressive experience in sanctions compliance or broader financial crimes compliance within financial services.

 - Deep, current knowledge of OFAC regulations and sanctions programs, with working familiarity with EU, UN, and UK OFSI regimes.

 - Experience building, scaling, or materially uplifting a sanctions program in a high-growth, regulated, or fintech environment.

 - Demonstrated people leadership, including managing distributed or multi-country teams.

 - Strong track record of stakeholder management with regulators, executives, and the Board.

 - Bachelor's degree required.

 - Willingness to be based in or relocate to Virginia with periodic travel to Brazil and other Latin American offices.

Prefered Professional

Experience:

- Experience at a global or multi-jurisdictional bank, payments company, or fintech operating across multiple regulatory regimes.

 - CAMS or equivalent financial crimes compliance certification.

 - Direct experience managing OFAC examinations, voluntary self-disclosures, or sanctions-related enforcement matters.

 - Familiarity with sanctions screening technology vendors and model tuning/validation practices.

From day one, Product Marketing is at the table — shaping roadmaps with customer and market insight, defining full‑funnel marketing strategy, and keeping us aligned with long‑term business priorities and product success metrics. This is a high‑ownership role, building something new from the ground up.

jobs.description:
ABOUT US
At OakNorth, we're on a mission to empower the UK's most ambitious businesses. Since 2015, we've lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers — all while fuelling the UK economy. This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic, fast-growing bank known for challenging the status quo. We're not looking for just another cog in the wheel — we want bold thinkers and proactive self-starters who are eager to shape their own careers while supporting the UK's most driven business leaders.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Our Debt Finance team sits at the heart of OakNorth's front-office lending activity. We work directly with entrepreneurs, sponsors, and intermediaries to originate and execute high-quality transactions across trading businesses (cashflow lending), real estate, and operational real estate. The team is fast-paced, collaborative, and deeply commercial — driven by a shared belief that ambitious businesses deserve better banking.

ABOUT THE ROLE
This is a high-impact, front-office Director role focused on originating, structuring, and executing lending transactions across trading businesses and real estate. jobs.title: Manager - Treasury, Capital Markets / Front Office
jobs.description:
The role

OakNorth runs an £8bn balance sheet with a small, senior Treasury team. Reporting to the Head of Treasury, you will own the execution of the bank's derivatives and FX activity and its investment portfolio, the sizing of its FX funding and liquidity positions, and support for capital and wholesale funding issuance — building the analytics behind those decisions. Treasury here is run as a measurable profit contributor rather than a cost centre, and the decisions taken on this desk are a material part of that.

This is a hands-on execution role rather than an oversight one. You will be pricing, trading, sizing and building the analysis behind your own recommendations, and presenting that work in senior forums including ALCO and to the CFO.

The role is deliberately front-office weighted, but the team is small and the remit is broad. There is genuine scope to build depth in the wider Treasury agenda — funds transfer pricing, liquidity and interest rate risk frameworks, and Board and regulatory work — for someone who wants it.

Principal responsibilities

Derivatives and FX

 - Execute interest rate swaps, cross-currency swaps and FX forwards across the bank's hedging programme. This is the most frequent trading activity on the desk and the centre of the role

 - Price, negotiate and execute with dealers across the counterparty panel, and evidence best execution

 - Own the FX risk position — including the USD lending book and intragroup exposures — and produce the exposure and hedging analysis that supports ALCO and Board reporting

 - Monitor collateral and margin flows under CSA arrangements, including the liquidity consequences of adverse mark-to-market moves. Supports expansion and onboarding with additional counterparts

 - Work with Finance on hedge designation and supporting documentation
 
 

Investment portfolio

 - Execute the gilt and HQLA investment programme against Board-approved mandates, using asset-swap spread and relative-value analysis to inform selection

 - Maintain and extend the portfolio construction tooling, including duration, maturity-ladder and concentration constraints

 - Size and roll the Treasury bill programme against deposit deployment windows

 - Support oversight of the externally managed AAA CLO portfolio, including trend and spread analytics and preparation for quarterly manager review

 - Support expansion of the investment instruments to develop the liquidity portfolio
 
 

Capital and funding issuance

 - Support the origination and execution of capital instrument issuance — Tier 2 and AT1 — working alongside the Treasurer, CFO and external advisers

 - Build and maintain the analysis behind issuance decisions, including sizing, pricing benchmarks and comparable market levels

 - Contribute to the development of wholesale funding options as the balance sheet grows, potentially spanning senior unsecured and secured issuance and securitisation
 
 

Funding and liquidity sizing

This part of the role is about sizing and direction. Operational execution and settlement sit with Treasury Operations; you set the strategy, size the transaction and steer the team.

 - Own USD liquidity end to end — determining how much liquidity is required in currency, and executing the cross-currency swaps that deliver it within Risk Appetite Limits

 - Set the sizing and collateral strategy for Bank of England repo facilities (ILTR and STR), instructing and reviewing rather than operating them

 - Steer the wider team on the analytical basis for funding and liquidity decisions, and review their output
 
 

Analytics and automation

We work extensively with AI-assisted development — Claude and Claude Code — inside a GitHub-controlled workflow. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you do need to be able to build a working analytical tool this way, or to learn to do so quickly.

 - Build, maintain and extend the desk's Python toolkit — pricing, sizing, limit monitoring and income attribution

 - Replace manual spreadsheet processes with repeatable, auditable and documented ones

 - Contribute to the Treasury Management System implementation and the Bloomberg data integration
 
 

Control, governance and reporting

 - Ensure trades are captured, confirmed and reported in line with the Treasury Trading Policy and supporting procedures

 - Monitor Risk Appetite Limits and Key Risk Indicators for front-office activity, and escalate promptly and clearly

 - Prepare and present front-office inputs to ALCO

 - Support regulatory deliverables — ILAAP, ICAAP and PRA information requests — from a front-office perspective
 
 

Essential experience and skills

 - Relevant execution experience — typically three to six years in a bank treasury front office, money markets or ALM desk, or a markets and rates role with clearly transferable execution skills.

 - Well-honed Bloomberg skills.. You should be fast and self-sufficient across money market and fixed income pricing, curve and relative-value analysis, swap and FX pricing, and the day-to-day ticket and blotter workflow.

 - Instrument knowledge — interest rate and cross-currency swaps and FX forwards first and foremost, together with gilts, Treasury bills and repo including Bank of England facilities.

 - Regulatory mechanics — a sound working understanding of LCR, NSFR and HQLA classification, as well as Capital regulation and how execution decisions move them.

 - Python literacy — sufficient to build, read and debug analytical tooling (pandas, numpy), together with real enthusiasm for AI-assisted development.

 - Communication — the ability to explain a trade, a number or a risk clearly and briefly to a senior, non-specialist audience.

Desirable

 - CFA, FRM, BTRM in progress or complete

 - Exposure to Clearing, CSA and margining mechanics, SA-CCR, or hedge accounting

 - Securitisation, CLO or structured credit experience

 - Exposure to debt capital markets — capital instrument or senior debt issuance, or securitisation — from a bank treasury, DCM or advisory seat

 - Experience in a challenger bank or another small team where breadth was required rather than optional
 
 

Who will do well here

 - You get things moving. Pace matters more than polish, and you are comfortable forming a view, making a call and owning the outcome.

 - You learn quickly and want to. The technical range here is wide, and we would rather hire someone visibly capable and eager to grow into the full breadth of it than someone with a narrow and finished skill set.

 - You are helpful by default. The team is small and nobody's job description is treated as a boundary.

 - You are comfortable being challenged, and challenging back.

You thrive in a global team. The finance team is spread across the UK and India and you're good at building trust across time zones and you don't need to be in the same room to stay aligned.

jobs.title: Principal, Talent Intelligence – US Lending
jobs.description:
We want to know the US lending talent market better than anyone else.

OakNorth is building its US lending business, and we are looking for someone to build the talent intelligence capability behind that growth.

Your job is to know where the exceptional people are before we need to hire them.

You'll map the market, understand how the best lending teams are built, develop relationships with outstanding people across the industry and give our leadership real-time intelligence on where talent, teams and opportunities are moving.

This isn't a traditional recruiting role focused on filling vacancies.

It's a strategic, external-facing role for someone who loves understanding markets, finding people others don't know about and building relationships long before there is a job to discuss.

You'll work directly with senior leaders across our US Lending business while being part of OakNorth's Global Talent Acquisition team.

You'll have the opportunity to build this capability from the ground up.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

KNOW THE MARKET

Become our expert on talent across the US commercial lending ecosystem, including:

 - Commercial and middle-market banking

 - Private credit and direct lending

 - Specialty finance

 - Sponsor finance

 - Asset-based lending

 - Corporate banking

You'll understand the firms, teams and individuals shaping these markets — who's growing, who's moving, where teams are being built and where the next generation of talent is emerging.

FIND EXCEPTIONAL PEOPLE BEFORE WE NEED THEM

We don't want to start searching when a vacancy opens.

You'll continuously identify and build relationships with exceptional people who could become important to OakNorth in the future.

You'll find them through:

 - Market mapping and original research

 - Industry relationships and referrals

 - Conferences and professional networks

 - Deal and transaction activity

 - Industry publications and awards

 - Leadership moves and team changes

 - AI-powered research and intelligence tools

You'll be curious enough to look beyond LinkedIn and creative enough to uncover people our competitors haven't found.

BUILD TRUSTED RELATIONSHIPS

You'll develop a powerful network across the US lending market.

These won't always be recruitment conversations.

You'll build long-term relationships with senior lenders, emerging leaders and market influencers — understanding their careers, ambitions and views on the market.

Over time, we want OakNorth to be one of the first calls exceptional lending professionals make when they're thinking about their careers.

TURN INTELLIGENCE INTO BUSINESS INSIGHT

You'll turn what you're seeing in the market into useful intelligence for our leadership team.

That could include:

 - Talent and competitor heatmaps

 - Team and leadership movements

 - Compensation intelligence

 - Emerging talent

 - Competitor hiring activity

 - New market entrants

 - Team stability and succession risk

 - Geographic talent pools

 - Market opportunities

The goal isn't research for the sake of research.

Your insight should help OakNorth make better decisions about where, when and who we hire.

BUILD OUR TALENT INTELLIGENCE PLATFORM

You'll use Ashby as our Talent CRM and create a living picture of the US lending talent market.

You'll build and maintain:

 - Talent communities

 - Executive relationships

 - Competitor maps

 - Market intelligence

 - Future hiring pipelines

 - Relationship history

 - Talent dashboards

You'll help us move from traditional recruiting pipelines towards a long-term talent ecosystem.

EXPERIMENT WITH AI

We want to rethink how talent intelligence is built.

You'll experiment with AI and emerging technology to improve research, market mapping, relationship management, workflow automation and reporting.

You'll have the freedom to test new approaches rather than simply follow an established recruiting playbook.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Within your first year, we want you to have built a talent intelligence capability that our US Lending leaders actively use to make decisions.

We should have:

 - A clear map of the most important firms, teams and talent across our priority lending markets

 - Strong relationships with exceptional people before vacancies exist

 - Live intelligence on competitor teams and market movements

 - High-quality future talent pipelines

 - Better visibility of compensation and talent trends

 - A growing network of emerging and established lending leaders

 - An Ashby Talent CRM that contains genuinely valuable market intelligence

Most importantly, when we decide to enter a market, build a team or make a critical hire, we should already know who we want to speak to.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're deliberately open-minded about where you've built your career.

You might currently work in:

 - Executive search

 - Talent intelligence or strategic sourcing

 - Commercial banking or private credit

 - Lending-focused research or market intelligence

 - Strategy or competitive intelligence

 - Another environment where you've developed deep knowledge of the US lending market

We're more interested in how you think and operate than whether you've previously held this exact title.

You'll likely be someone who:

 - Understands the US commercial lending landscape and can quickly build credibility with senior professionals

 - Loves researching markets and finding people others miss

 - Is naturally curious about firms, teams, deals and people

 - Builds relationships without needing an immediate transaction

 - Can turn fragmented market information into useful commercial insight

 - Is comfortable speaking with senior executives

 - Has a strong hunter mentality and isn't reliant on inbound applications

 - Enjoys building something from scratch

 - Uses technology and AI to work smarter and move faster

 - Has an entrepreneurial mindset and strong bias for action

An existing network across US lending would be valuable, but the ability to build one is just as important.

WHY OAKNORTH?

OakNorth was founded by entrepreneurs to help ambitious businesses scale.

Since launching in 2015, we've built one of the UK's leading commercial banks and are now building the next chapter of OakNorth in the United States.

This role gives you something unusual: the opportunity to create a talent intelligence capability from scratch and work directly with the leaders building our US lending business.

There isn't an established playbook to inherit.

You'll help write it.

Benefits and Perks

 - 401k plan with Principal (ON match up to 4%)

 - Medical Care (managed through Insperity) - employees can add their family to their plan if needed

 - Dental & Vision bundle

 - Insperity Health Savings Account Program - this is a tax-advantaged employee benefit which can help manage health care costs by allowing employees to set aside some of their current earnings on a pretax basis for reimbursement of qualified health care expenses during the plan year

 - EAP

 - 20 days Holiday

jobs.description:
OakNorth is a leading commercial digital bank, built by entrepreneurs for entrepreneurs. Founded in 2015, we support lower mid-market businesses — those with revenues between $1m and $100m — by providing fast, flexible debt finance and personalised banking services. To date, we have lent over $16bn to businesses globally, directly contributing to the creation of 56,000 jobs and 34,000 new homes.

We began operating in the US in mid-2023 and have since lent over $700m to US businesses. In March 2025, we announced an exciting milestone: the acquisition of Community Unity Bank (CUB), an FDIC-insured community bank based in Birmingham, Michigan, which marks a significant step in our US expansion.

This is a rare opportunity to join early and have real ownership over how we build People in the US. As we establish our American operation across New York and Michigan, this is the first dedicated People hire on the ground — you won't be inheriting a playbook, you'll be writing it.

GLOBAL COLLABORATION
