The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT PRODUCTION ENGINEERING

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

 - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

 - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

 - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

 - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

 - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

OUR TEAMS

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

 - Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

 - Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

 - Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

 - Developer Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

As a Tech Lead & Manager, you are a hands-on player-coach: you will lead and grow a team while remaining directly engaged in the technical work. Management at Ramp does not mean stepping away from the technology or the code. You will help set direction, develop engineers, and work alongside the team to deliver consequential infrastructure outcomes.

Day to day, you will:

 - Build, coach, and grow a high-performing team. Create clarity, give direct feedback, mentor engineers, and help each person expand their technical judgment, ownership, and leadership.

 - Set technical direction for your team’s domain. Identify the highest-leverage problems, define a path forward, bring the right people along, and stay engaged with the team until the work is delivered.

 - Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

 - Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

 - Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

 - Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

 - Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

 - Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

 - Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

 - Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

 - You love building teams, mentoring engineers, and helping people grow—and you are equally energized by writing code, reviewing designs, and digging into complex distributed systems.

 - You are a true player-coach. You know when to coach, delegate, and create space for others to lead; you also know when your direct technical involvement will create the most leverage.

 - You can set a technical direction, bring people along, and then lock in with the team to make it happen.

 - You do not believe managing engineers means stepping away from the technology or the code.

 - You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

 - You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

 - You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

 - You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

 - You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

 - You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

 - A sustained hands-on engineering track record. You are comfortable writing and reviewing production code, evaluating system designs, debugging incidents, and making difficult technical tradeoffs.

 - Hands-on experience building and operating distributed systems at production scale.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp is hiring its first dedicated Physical Security Lead to build and run the program that protects our people, our leaders, our events, and our offices. Our footprint now spans a multi-floor New York headquarters, Ramp-managed offices, and a growing set of hubs across North America and Europe. Our leaders are increasingly visible on public stages.

You'll own three areas in roughly equal measure: executive protection, event security, and office security (access control, cameras, guards, and building security). Your job is to turn a set of strong vendors and partner teams into one measurable, risk-based program.

This is a high-ownership IC role on the Corporate Security team. It reports to the Director of IT & Corporate Security and is based at our NYC HQ. This is a physical security role; cybersecurity and information security are owned by other Ramp security teams. We aren't looking for a guard supervisor or a box-checker. We want someone who makes it safe for Ramp to move fast, host great events, and keep our leaders accessible.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and run Ramp's executive protection program:
 
 - Protective risk assessments and residential security reviews.
 
 - Domestic and international travel security.
 
 - Advance work for high-visibility appearances.
 
 - Selecting, standing up, and managing our executive protection provider.

 - Turn threat intelligence into protective action. Partner with Detection & Response to move from online threat and exposure monitoring to threat assessments, personal-information exposure reduction, and clear escalation playbooks.

 - Own security for internal and external events, from all-hands and offsites to conferences, customer events, and executive dinners:
 
 - Risk-tiered intake and written security plans.
 
 - Coordination with venues and vendors.
 
 - On-site leadership for the highest-risk events.
 
 - After-action reviews.

 - Set Ramp's global physical security standards for access control, video surveillance, intercoms, visitor management, and alarm monitoring. Tier them for headquarters, Ramp-managed offices, and flexible or serviced hub spaces.

 - Build security into every new office, move, and expansion:
 
 - Write the security design requirements and review drawings.
 
 - Manage integrators through installation and acceptance testing.
 
 - Partner with IT on network and identity integration.

 - Manage the guard program and security vendors end to end: scope, post orders, SLAs and KPIs, budget, and quarterly business reviews. Own the security relationship with landlords and building management.

 - Lead emergency preparedness and physical incident response:
 
 - Emergency notifications, evacuation and shelter-in-place plans, and drills.
 
 - Liaison with local law enforcement.
 
 - Workplace-violence prevention, in partnership with People and Legal.

 - Run physical access governance with IT. Tie access to joiner/mover/leaver events, run regular access reviews, and keep audit-ready evidence for physical security controls.

 - Measure and report program health to leadership. Use AI and automation to scale the program without scaling headcount.
 
 

WHAT YOU NEED

 - 6+ years in corporate or physical security, including 3+ years owning a security program or major workstream at a multi-site company. Executing someone else's program doesn't count toward this.

 - Hands-on depth in at least two of the three areas (executive protection, event security, physical security systems such as access control and cameras) and solid working knowledge of the third.

 - Experience administering or deploying enterprise access control and video platforms (e.g., Avigilon Alta/Openpath, Verkada, Genetec, LenelS2), and partnering with IT on networking and SSO.

 - A track record of managing security vendors (guard, protection, integrator, event staffing) through contracts, SLAs, budgets, and performance reviews.

 - Strong risk judgment. You size controls to the actual threat, explain the tradeoffs, and lead with "here's how we do this safely" rather than "no."

 - Excellent writing. You can produce a crisp SOP, an event security plan, and a one-page executive brief.

 - Willingness to work from our NYC office 4 days a week, travel 10–15%, support occasional evening and weekend events, and serve as primary on-call for physical security incidents (with the Director as backup and guard and vendor partners as on-site first response).

 - Real, day-to-day use of AI tools in your work.
 
 

NICE-TO-HAVES

 - ASIS CPP or PSP; formal executive protection training; first aid or Stop the Bleed certification.

 - Experience at a high-growth tech, fintech, or financial services company with a high-profile founder or CEO.

 - Experience writing security design standards for office buildouts and reading architectural or low-voltage drawings.

 - Familiarity with physical and environmental control requirements in SOC 2, PCI DSS, or FedRAMP.

 - A government protective, law enforcement, or military background, combined with corporate program ownership.

 - An established network of protection, event security, and integrator vendors in NYC, SF, and internationally.
 
 

FAIR WARNING

 - This is a builder role. Parts of the program exist today (vendors, a responsibility matrix, some SOPs). You'll turn them into a system.

 - You're an IC who directs vendors and partner teams, not a manager of a security staff. You'll need to influence Workplace, Events, IT, Executive Assistants, People, and Legal without formal authority.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

Ramp is hiring a Brand Partnerships Manager to shape and accelerate our growth through strategic partnerships and collaborations.

You’ll build our brand partnerships strategy from the ground up: sourcing high-potential partners, developing relationships, structuring creative collaborations, and turning them into campaigns that drive awareness, engagement, and business growth.

Success in this role looks like building real, high-impact partnerships with tangible value for Ramp, our partners, and the audiences we reach together. The ideal candidate is a marketer who can also run a deal: you come up with the partnership, you know why it matters for the business, and you execute relentlessly to get it out the door. You should have an instinct for great ideas, a strong creative point of view, and a close read on what’s happening across media, sports, and culture. Most importantly, you’ve turned those ideas into campaigns that break through culture, get attention, and drive business outcomes.

Ramp is a place for people who move fast, take ownership, and are looking to do the best work of their careers. We want someone who can build this function out, bet on partners that matter, and create collaborations that move the needle and are unmistakably Ramp.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Ramp’s brand partnerships program end to end: partner strategy, sourcing, negotiation, and execution.

 - Find high-value partners across finance, sports, business, and media who can put Ramp in front of new audiences.

 - Build a system for spotting and tracking emerging talent so we can place smart bets early. We sponsored Neal Shipley while he was still an amateur golfer, and TBPN in the very early days. We like spotting emerging brands and talent before everyone else does.

 - Develop bold partnership concepts that tie into Ramp’s brand, product priorities, launches, and broader marketing campaigns.

 - Lead deal strategy and negotiation, including pricing, asset packages, usage rights, exclusivity, deliverables, timelines, and contract terms.

 - Work with teams across Ramp to run and test campaigns across paid, owned, and earned channels, so every partnership delivers both creative impact and business results.

 - Manage active partnerships day to day. Keep deliverables on track, and keep finding new ways to work with existing partners so Ramp gets the most out of every relationship.

 - Work closely with Ramp’s sales team to spot deals where a partner could help, and find timely, relevant ways to bring them in.

 - Handle reporting for every partnership. Track delivery and performance, share what you’re learning, and recommend when to renew, expand, change, or end a deal.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - 5+ years of experience in brand marketing, influencer marketing, partnerships, or a related role.

 - A track record of developing, negotiating, and executing high-profile brand, media, or strategic partnerships, ideally within a fast moving in-house team or at an agency. The ideal candidate has a builder mindset and is willing to challenge conventional approaches and take a first principles approach.

 - Strong creative judgment, with the ability to spot culturally relevant ideas and turn them into partnerships and campaigns that earn attention.

 - The ability to thrive in ambiguity, take initiative, and launch new programs quickly from scratch You can move from strategy to execution quickly, manage complexity, and drive work across teams.

 - Excel at balancing brand authenticity with performance metrics. Strong business acumen and judgment to balance efficiency with bold bets.

 - Ability to switch between strategy and in-the-weeds execution. In one meeting, you’re zooming out to set the vision and framework, the next you’re diving into day-to-day execution and delivery.

 - A strong interest in culture, entertainment, and sports.

BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend

UNITED STATES

 - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

 - One Medical annual membership

 - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

 - Pet insurance

 - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

 - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)
 
 

CANADA

 - Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

 - Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

 - Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

 - Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

 - Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

UNITED KINGDOM

 - Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

 - Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

 - Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

REFERRAL INSTRUCTIONS

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

OTHER NOTICES

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com http://Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

jobs.title: Senior Web Developer I
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

Web Development builds and runs relayfi.com http://relayfi.com — the pages, components, content platform, and infrastructure that turn organic search, AI-driven discovery, and paid traffic into new Relay accounts. We're a small team with a big impact, moving fast while holding a high bar for performance, accessibility, and SEO.

We're looking for a Senior Web Developer to lead complex web projects, shape technical decisions, and help scale the platform behind Relay's growth. You'll work in a modern Next.js codebase with React, TypeScript, Tailwind, and Contentful, tackling architectural challenges that directly impact site performance, scalability, and discoverability. You'll own projects from technical planning through launch, mentor other developers, and partner closely with teams across the company.

This is an ideal role for a front-end developer who thrives on ownership, enjoys solving complex technical problems, and wants to make a measurable impact. Your technical judgment will carry weight here, and you'll have the autonomy to challenge assumptions, influence priorities, and shape how we build.

Want to see what we're building? Check out relayfi.com http://relayfi.com and Telegraph https://storybook.relayfi.design/, the design system our engineers use across Relay.

What You’ll Be Doing

 - Project Ownership: Lead complex, multi-part projects end-to-end — define scope, set milestones, coordinate with cross-functional teams, and deliver high-quality work on time. Own what happens after launch by measuring performance, identifying opportunities, and iterating on improvements

 - Technical Architecture: Define the technical approach for features and projects, making thoughtful decisions around server/client boundaries, caching, revalidation, and CDN behaviour. Balance performance, scalability, and technical debt while proactively simplifying systems, improving maintainability, and addressing root causes

 - Performance, Accessibility & Technical SEO: Proactively improve site performance, accessibility, security, and technical SEO, including structured data, metadata, and semantic markup that improve discoverability across search engines and AI platforms

 - Content Platform Development: Build and optimize integrations between the headless CMS and front end, developing scalable content models and tools that empower non-technical teams to manage and publish content independently

 - AI-Driven Development: Build and integrate AI workflows and agents that improve development efficiency, from automated code reviews and performance monitoring to design-to-component generation. Establish testing and review guardrails to maintain quality and help the team adopt AI effectively

 - Measurement & Experimentation: Build and maintain analytics, event tracking, attribution, feature flags, and A/B testing infrastructure to support conversion optimization. Own integrations between the website, marketing tools, and CRM systems, including forms and lead routing

 - Code Quality & Testing: Set a high bar for maintainable, performant, and well-documented code. Define testing strategies across unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, ensuring quality and reliability are built into every project

 - Cross-Functional Leadership & Mentorship: Serve as a trusted technical partner to Marketing, Design, Product, and external agencies, translating business needs into technical solutions and driving alignment on priorities and tradeoffs. Mentor developers through pairing, code reviews, and knowledge sharing, while helping cross-functional partners navigate technical decisions

Who You Are

 - You have 4+ years of front-end development experience, ideally in a high-growth B2B SaaS or fintech environment, with a proven ability to work independently and deliver high-quality solutions

 - You're strong in React, Next.js, and Node, and you write TypeScript by default. Our repo is fully typed in strict mode with type checking enforced in CI, so strong TypeScript proficiency is essential

 - You're skilled in modern front-end architecture, with a strong understanding of server/client boundaries, caching, revalidation, and CDN behaviour. You think in systems, designing scalable solutions while anticipating downstream impacts

 - You're proficient in Tailwind and experienced working with design systems, reusable components, and headless CMS platforms. You understand content modelling and integrations, with experience in Contentful and GraphQL being valuable but not required

 - You have a strong understanding of web performance, accessibility, and technical SEO, including Core Web Vitals (LCP and CLS), image optimization, bundle analysis, WCAG 2.1 AA, semantic HTML, metadata, structured data, sitemaps, and heading hierarchy

 - You actively use AI tools and workflows to improve development efficiency, with the judgment to evaluate outputs, manage risks, and maintain code quality

 - You have strong project management and communication skills, with the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, manage competing priorities, and translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders

 - You're a proactive problem-solver who thinks beyond individual tasks, understands customer needs, challenges assumptions, anticipates downstream impacts, and adapts quickly to new technologies and feedback

Bonus Points

 - You've built analytics, experimentation, and marketing integrations using tools like Segment, GTM, Statsig, and HubSpot

 - You've worked with AWS Amplify Hosting or similar CI/CD platforms and built end-to-end tests using Playwright or equivalent tools

 - You've built animations using GSAP or Framer Motion and have experience with SCSS

The Interview Process

 - Stage 1: A 30-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent team

 - Stage 2: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with our Director, Web

 - Stage 3: A take-home technical challenge

 - Stage 4: A 60-minute review and live front-end exercise over Google Meet with the Web team

 - Stage 5: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team

Our Compensation Approach

We believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.

The annual salary range for this role is $107,100 CAD to $130,900 CAD.

For candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $119,000 CAD. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. Offers above this point reflect impact that meaningfully exceeds the role’s defined expectations or an expanded scope from day one.

We encourage you to have a conversation with your recruiter and ask questions about compensation throughout the hiring process. For more information on our compensation philosophy and perks and benefits, visit our Candidate Hub https://www.notion.so/Candidate-Hub-1c7da8b7f88580a893f7d7c7852b064e?pvs=21.

Why Relay Might Be the Perfect Fit For You 

 - You push relentlessly for reinvention: You're always asking "how can this be better?" -- in your work, in your craft, in yourself. Comfort is a signal to push harder, not coast. You'd rather build something better than defend something familiar.

 - You crave autonomy: We trust our team with big challenges and the freedom to solve them. If you’re someone who takes initiative, is comfortable taking risks, and seeks input when needed, you’ll find the freedom here empowering.

 - You own your work: You take pride in your work, follow through on commitments, and feel a deep sense of responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.

 - You build with AI, not just use it: You're actively embedding AI into how you work, pushing what's possible, and bringing your team along with you.

 - You care about impact, not noise: You care deeply about the substance of your work. You measure success by results, not recognition, and you let your work speak for itself. 

 - You’re energized by complexity and ambiguity: You enjoy tackling problems that don’t come with a playbook. You’re comfortable building from scratch, iterating as you go, and collaborating to shape the best path forward.

 - You seek out feedback: You see directness as respect, not criticism. You actively seek input, sit with hard truths, and use feedback as fuel for improvement.

 - Small businesses are why we're here: Relay exists to help them thrive -- and that mission has to resonate with you.

Join Us

We're looking for people who are relentless, curious, and care deeply about the work. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't perfectly match the job description -- your perspective and drive matter more. We welcome diverse backgrounds and people who think critically, challenge the status quo, and want to help small businesses thrive.

If you require accommodations at any stage of the hiring process, please reach out to your Talent Partner.

Disclaimer: For compliance reasons, all offers of employment at Relay are conditional upon a successful background check and employment verification through Certn.

Important Notice: Relay’s recruitment team only contacts candidates and corresponds from official corporate email addresses ending in @relayfi.com. We will never ask for sensitive personal data (such as bank account details, credit card numbers, or social security/insurance numbers) during the initial application or interview stages.

At Relay, product management is about outcomes, not outputs. We start with real customer problems and build solutions that move the needle for SMBs, and for our business. Our team pairs long-term vision with rapid iteration. We believe that trust is a product feature, and that usability, reliability, and polish aren’t afterthoughts, they’re core to how we earn the confidence of business owners.

Product Managers at Relay play a central role in solving these problems by building financial products that are simple, intuitive, and impactful.

 - Security & Compliance: Work closely with Trust, Security, and Governance teams to keep customer data safe through best-in-class security and compliance practices

 - You have 3+ years of Data Engineering experience

 - You write SQL that goes well beyond SELECT, WHERE and GROUP BY -- think complex window functions, query optimization, and schema design

 - You're fluent in Python and know how to write clean, maintainable, production-grade code

 - You have hands-on experience with our core stack: dbt for transformations, Dagster for orchestration, Snowflake as our data warehouse, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure)

 - You have experience with BI/data visualization tools (Looker, Metabase, Mode, etc.) and understand what it takes to support a great analytics layer

 - You have an understanding of applied statistics, are able to create quantitative models, and can clearly communicate findings to a technical and non-technical audience

jobs.title: Strategic Operations Manager - Partnerships
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

We’re looking for a Strategic Operations Manager - Partnerships to join our team supporting the Partner Sales team to empower accounting and bookkeeping professionals to better serve their SMB clients.

Joining Relay means a unique opportunity to make a huge impact by building a category-defining Partner Program from the ground up. You'll play a pivotal role in Relay's growth journey, defining and developing a critical function that will scale one of our most important growth channels. As a strategic connector, you'll work with cross-functional teams (Partner Sales, Marketing, Product, Data, RevOps, and Engineering) to deliver enablement, data, and operational tools for our partners to succeed and grow. If you thrive on building scalable systems, simplifying complexity, and equipping others with the tools to win, then Relay is the place for you.

What You’ll Be Doing

Channel Strategy & Planning

 - Own the revenue planning process for the A&B sales channel, including annual planning, quota design, territory modeling, and headcount forecasting.

 - Develop and maintain channel-specific go-to-market frameworks that define how we acquire, activate, and expand relationships with accounting and bookkeeping professionals.

 - Identify and drive strategic growth opportunities within the A&B segment and present data-backed recommendations to senior leadership to optimize partner sales in alignment with business priorities.

Sales Process & Enablement

 - Design, document, and continuously improve the end-to-end sales process for A&B channel reps, from prospecting through close and handoff.

 - Partner with Sales Enablement to ensure Sales team has the playbooks, tools, and training needed to effectively engage accounting and bookkeeping professionals.

 - Lead pipeline management best practices, deal inspection cadences, and stage conversion optimization using modern B2B go-to-market motions and key revenue metrics.

 - Monitor and optimize the partner onboarding journey, reducing time to value and friction points

Analytics & Reporting

 - Build and maintain dashboards and reporting frameworks that provide real-time visibility into channel health, pipeline trends, rep performance, and revenue attainment.

 - Conduct deep-dive analyses on funnel conversion, churn risk, partner engagement, and seasonal trends specific to the A&B market.

 - Establish and monitor channel KPIs, including ARR/MRR growth, client referral rates, partner retention, and bookings velocity.

 - Analyze partner activity, client outcomes, and workflow adoption to uncover insights, including tracking the realized value Relay delivers to partners' clients (e.g., cash flow impact, workflow ROI)

 - Use data to inform program improvements, partner segmentation, territory management and strategic focus areas

 - Design and maintain a partner-facing dashboard for incentive tracking, performance metrics, and earned rewards, while partnering with RevOps and Data to automate reporting workflows, set topline goals, and integrate performance tracking into internal systems

Systems & Tooling

 - Administer and optimize CRM workflows, data hygiene, and automation relevant to the A&B channel (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot).

 - Evaluate and implement tools that improve prospecting, pipeline visibility, and partner relationship management.

 - Ensure data integrity across all systems that feed A&B channel reporting.

 - Own and iterate on tools, systems, and processes to improve partner lifecycle management, drive partner engagement and achieve key revenue driving metrics

Cross-Functional Collaboration

 - Act as the primary RevOps liaison to the A&B channel sales team, ensuring alignment between field execution and company revenue goals.

 - Partner with Marketing to define channel-specific demand generation programs, lead routing, and campaign attribution.

 - Collaborate with Finance on revenue forecasting, commission plan design, and deal desk processes.

 - Work with Product and Customer Success to surface A&B partner feedback and inform roadmap prioritization.
 
 

Who You Are

 - You have 4+ years of experience in sales or partner enablement, partnerships, consulting, strategy and business operations, sales operations, or other sales channel-facing roles

 - You are a systems thinker with a focus on execution, able to take ideas from concept to launch and scale them effectively

 - Strong analytical skills with the ability to turn complex data sets into clear, actionable insights.

 - Proficient with CRM platforms (Salesforce and HubSpot) and BI/reporting tools (e.g., Metabase, Tableau, Looker, or similar).

 - You are a strong communicator who thrives in cross-functional environments and can translate complexity into clarity

 - You are curious about how AI and technology can improve your workflow and constantly explore ways to make partner enablement more scalable and intelligent

Bonus Points

 - You have experience working with accounting firms, GTM partner programs, or B2B software ecosystems

 - Experience building RevOps infrastructure from the ground up or scaling operations in a high-growth environment.

 - Familiarity with data infrastructure and analytics tools (e.g., dbt, BigQuery, Snowflake, Metabase, Looker).

 - Experience working directly with AI agents, LLM-based applications, or prompt engineering in a production environment.

 - Experience supporting a PLG and sales-assisted hybrid GTM motion.

 - Background in fintech or SMB-focused SaaS environments.

 - You have worked with SMBs in North America

The Interview Process

 - Stage 1: A 30-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent team

 - Stage 2: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with the Director, Revenue Operations and the Director, Sales

 - Stage 3: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team

 - Stage 4: A take-home case study followed by a 60-minute Google Meet video call with our team

jobs.description:

Relay processes millions of dollars in deposits, wires, checks, and card transactions every business day, and 321,000+ small business owners trust us with their money. The Transaction Monitoring team is why that trust is warranted. Every transaction we review is a decision: hold or release, investigate or clear.  - Suggest improvements to fraud rules and controls: flag rules that are generating false positives, spot gaps that let bad activity through, and bring recommendations to Risk Strategy so your findings shape how we detect fraud

 - You make calls and stand behind them. Holding a deposit means a business can't access their money; releasing it means betting your judgment that it's clean. You're comfortable owning both.

 - You're a problem solver with high agency. You don't just spot issues — you come with solutions and drive them forward without waiting to be asked.

 - You build with AI. You're actively using AI tools in how you work today and you're excited to push what's possible with them.

jobs.title: Compliance Strategist
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

Our mission is to increase the success rate of small businesses. Traditional banking has been a growth limiter rather than a growth enabler for business owners, and we're changing that. Relay is the all-in-one, collaborative money management platform. We're building for employer SMBs and their finance function, internal and external, and are focused on delivering a human-centric customer experience. Ultimately, we help SMBs be 'on the money'.

Relay is scaling rapidly, and we're growing our Compliance team to help safeguard our platform, our customers, and our regulatory standing as we scale. We're looking for a data-driven, detail-oriented problem solver who is excited to build out our compliance monitoring capabilities and strengthen how we partner with our sponsor bank – not just maintain existing processes.

As a Compliance Analyst, you'll own the development and ongoing management of Relay's compliance monitoring program end-to-end, designing the frameworks, testing, and reporting that ensure our products and operations meet regulatory requirements. You'll also be a key point of contact in managing the day-to-day partnership between Relay and our sponsor bank, ensuring alignment on compliance expectations, exam readiness, and issue resolution. Your work directly shapes how Relay identifies, monitors, and remediates compliance risk while maintaining a trusted relationship with our banking partner, meeting the needs of our fast moving business, and ensuring a seamless customer experience.

At Relay, your work has real reach – helping millions of SMBs operate safely and confidently, while protecting the integrity of our banking partnership. If you're passionate about using data and process rigor to solve meaningful problems, building compliance programs from the ground up, and being a trusted partner to both internal teams and external stakeholders, this is the role for you.

What You'll Be Doing

 - Compliance Monitoring Program: Develop and own Relay's compliance monitoring program, including designing testing methodologies, monitoring schedules, and reporting frameworks

 - Sponsor Bank Partnership: Manage the day-to-day relationship between Relay and our sponsor bank, serving as a primary point of contact on compliance matters, exams, and audits

 - Data-Driven Monitoring: Analyze account, transaction, and operational data to identify compliance gaps, emerging risks, and areas for control enhancement

 - Testing & Reporting: Execute ongoing compliance testing and reviews, document findings, and produce clear reporting for internal stakeholders and our sponsor bank

 - Issue Management: Track identified issues through to remediation, ensuring corrective actions are implemented and validated in a timely manner

 - Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Risk, Product, Engineering, and Operations to embed compliance requirements into new features, products, and processes

 - Regulatory Change Management: Monitor changes in applicable regulations and guidance, and translate them into updates to our monitoring program and controls

 - Continuous Improvement: Iterate on monitoring processes, tools, and documentation to increase efficiency and scalability as Relay grows

 - Stakeholder Communication: Translate compliance findings into clear, actionable recommendations for technical and non-technical stakeholders, including our sponsor bank

Who You Are

 - You have 2+ years of experience in compliance, risk, audit, or a related field, preferably in fintech, banking, or payments

 - You have experience building or running a compliance monitoring or testing program, or are eager to build one from the ground up

 - You're comfortable working directly with a bank partner or regulator, and understand the importance of a strong, trusted partnership

 - You’re proficient in SQL (joins, aggregations, window functions, subqueries) and can write efficient queries with minimal supervision

 - You own projects from start to finish, defining the problem, diving into the details, and driving solutions to completion

 - You're a strong communicator, translating complex compliance topics into clear, actionable recommendations for technical and non-technical stakeholders

 - You're collaborative and know how to navigate cross-functional work with Risk, Product, Engineering, and Operations

 - You thrive in fast-paced environments, tackling ambiguity, building process where none exists, and raising the bar across the team

 - You're actively using AI tools in how you work today and you're excited to push what's possible with them

Bonus Points

 - You have experience managing a sponsor bank or regulatory partnership directly

 - You have worked in a startup or scale-up environment

 - Stage 1: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent team

 - Stage 2: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with the Manager, Risk Strategy

 - Stage 4: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team

Relay is entering an exciting new chapter of growth, and we're looking for a Security Engineer to join the purple team in our security organization. This is a rare early-career opportunity to work across both offensive and defensive security with the mentorship and support to grow quickly.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Growth
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

At Relay, product management is about outcomes, not outputs. We start with real customer problems and build solutions that move the needle for SMBs, and for our business. Our team pairs long-term vision with rapid iteration. We believe that trust is a product feature, and that usability, reliability, and polish aren't afterthoughts, they're core to how we earn the confidence of business owners.

Why this role matters

Signing up for a business bank account is the easy part. The hard part is the distance between "account opened" and "this is where I run my business." That distance is where most SMBs quietly stall; the first deposit that never lands, the payroll still running out of the old account, the bookkeeper who was never invited in. Every business owner who doesn't cross it stays on the cashflow tightrope we exist to get them off of.

As Senior Product Manager, Growth (Activation), you own that crossing. You'll own the journey from first login to funded, transacting, habitual use of Relay — and the systems, experiments, and in-product moments that get customers there faster and in greater numbers. This is a metrics-owning role: you'll be accountable for activation rate, time-to-first-deposit, and depth of product adoption in the first 90 days, and for the revenue those unlock.

In your first year, you might:

 - Rebuild the post-signup experience so a new owner reaches their first funded transaction in days, not weeks

 - Diagnose where and why customers drop between account approval, funding, and first payment, then ship the sequenced interventions that close those gaps

 - Stand up the experimentation and lifecycle infrastructure that lets Relay run activation tests continuously rather than one-off

 - Drive adoption of the products that make Relay sticky (multiple accounts, cards, bill pay, accounting integrations) by getting them in front of the right owner at the right moment

 - Partner with Risk and Operations so that friction we add for good reasons (KYC, fraud controls) costs us as few good customers as possible

 - Build the narrative and roadmap that aligns leadership, Marketing, and CX around a shared definition of an activated customer

What you'll be doing:

 - Own activation end-to-end: define the vision, set the roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements to how quickly and completely SMBs start running their money through Relay

 - Treat activation like a business: define the activation metric that actually predicts retention and revenue, instrument it, monitor it, and make decisions rooted in data and customer insight

 - Run a real experiment engine: form hypotheses, design tests, read results honestly, and kill what doesn't work, while knowing when a problem calls for a rebuild rather than an A/B test

 - Ship high-quality product from ideation to launch: partner closely with design and engineering as part of a leadership trifecta, raising the bar for usability, craft, and polish. Onboarding copy and empty states are your job, not someone else's

 - Work across the whole first-run surface: in-product experiences, lifecycle messaging, and the handoffs between Marketing, Sales, and CX that make or break a new customer's first month

 - Stay deeply connected to SMB customers: watch real owners set up their accounts, understand what makes them hesitate to move their money, and design for the trust that earns

 - Build and tell the story: create clear narratives that inspire leadership and cross-functional partners, even in ambiguous situations

 - Champion product culture at Relay: bring curiosity, ownership, and a high bar for quality that elevates the product team as a whole

Who you are

 - At least five years of product management experience, with a track record of owning and materially moving a funnel or lifecycle metric

 - Direct experience with activation, onboarding, or early-lifecycle work in a product-led business

 - Strong data competency: you self-serve your metrics, write your own SQL, and can tell a real signal from a noisy test

 - Fluent in experimentation. You know what your infrastructure can and can't support, and you're rigorous about what counts as a win

 - Excellent storytelling and communication

 - Experience working closely with engineering and design as part of a leadership trifecta to deliver polished, high-quality experiences

 - Demonstrated success working cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Experience teams to ensure effective launches and adoption

 - Comfort working in ambiguous environments while bringing structure and clarity where needed

 - A hands-on operator's instinct. You're as comfortable in the details of a UX flow or a lifecycle trigger as in a roadmap review

 - You've worked on activation in fintech, where compliance, funding, and risk controls sit directly in the path of the customer journey

 - You've built lifecycle or CRM systems in partnership with a marketing team

 - Joining the team's rhythms: Two weekly standups, a biweekly security champions session with product engineers, and a weekly Hack The Box session.

 - Software supply chain: Enforce provenance: SBOM on every build, dependency pinning/owner verification, private registries/proxies, and runtime SCA detections.

 - You have 5 to 6 years of professional security experience. Application security, penetration testing, or product security engineering or similar roles.

 - You've shipped production code: Production-level software real users depended on. And you can read an unfamiliar codebase well enough to fix something in it, which is most of this job.

 - Clear communicator & collaborator: You are a collaborator who loves to partner with developers to bring value to customers in the most secure way possible.

jobs.description:

You'll join Core Banking, the team building the resilient banking infrastructure that Relay's customers and internal teams depend on — ACH and wire transfers, local and international, and everything that keeps money moving securely and predictably. Core and Risk Engineering are tied at the hip, and you'll be embedded across both. The team's north star is simple: scalable, reliable, on time, under budget — measured in escaped defects, test flakiness and duration, incident count, and uptime.

Your mission is to scale quality operations and build the tooling, frameworks and CI pipelines for a distributed system that make it easy to scale quality and increase development velocity across every engineering team at Relay.

This is not a role where you write UI tests against someone else's system. You will have the same leverage as a developer.

What You'll Be Doing

 - Own the quality roadmap for Risk Engineering and build the quality engineering frameworks for Core Banking systems, including ACH and domestic and international wire transfers.

 - Build and improve our CI infrastructure, including the migration to ministack — testing lambdas and microservices in CI with local implementations of Wiremock, Localstack and PSQL. You'll be measured on the same numbers the team is: escaped defects, test flakiness and duration, incident count, uptime.

 - Drive shift-left across the teams you're embedded in — attending sprint ceremonies and getting developers writing tests as part of their deliverables, not as a handoff to QA.

 - Find and remove the bottlenecks in quality operations, diagnosing pain points across Core Banking and Risk and championing the solutions.

 - Build tools that improve developer experience, with minimal dependency on third parties.

 - Mentor junior quality engineers and contribute to the direction and larger-scale initiatives of the Quality Engineering team.

 - Tell the quality story with data — gathering defect and quality data from across our systems and presenting it to engineering leadership and executives.

Roughly 75% of your week is hands-on building. The other 25% is influence: ceremonies, mentorship, evangelism, and getting teams to adopt what you've built.

Who You Are

 - You have built quality engineering systems from the ground up, hands on — frameworks, test suites and CI systems, not just tests written against someone else's harness.

 - You have tested distributed systems, not only UIs. Services, lambdas, microservices, real-time applications — you understand what makes them hard to test and you've done it in CI.

 - You understand and care deeply about system architecture - you have an in depth understanding of how a distributed system is architected - how systems communicate, how scaleability and resilience is built into a system and how to design tests for these complex systems instead of treating them like a black box.

 - You can influence and persuade development teams to adopt quality practices. You've changed how a team works, not just what you shipped.

 - You debug from first principles, using code, logs and traces to get to genuine root cause.

 - You can gather quality and defect data from multiple sources and present it to a wide audience, including executives, and make the numbers mean something.

 - You are AI-fluent in practice — using AI tools daily, comfortable with how agents work and with the systems underneath them, and able to critique AI output rather than accept it blindly.

 - You thrive in agile teams that move quickly and you're comfortable with ambiguity and abstract requirements.

Bonus Points

 - Mobile testing experience (Detox).

 - Experience with AWS systems.

Our stack: React, Nodejs, AWS Infrastructure (Queues, S3, DynamoDB etc.) , PSQL, Redis, Playwright, Detox, GitHub Actions, Ministack/Localstack, Wiremock, Bruno, Sentry, Datadog, Cursor, Claude, JIRA, Notion.

 - Be the DRI for Relay's 2027 referral pilot, from discovery and design through launch and distribution, and reporting back on what's working.

 - You've personally run several campaigns or programs end to end through paid media: newsletter, paid social, search, or experimental channels like audio, AI ads or direct mail.

 - You've delivered programs through other people. You rally Analytics, Lifecycle, Partnerships, CX and Sales without needing to own them.

 - You enjoy collaborating with other departments and mentoring or coaching junior team members

 - You have strong interpersonal skills, a growth mindset, and the adaptability to thrive in a fast-scaling, evolving environment

jobs.title: Data Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

Relay's data engineering team has tripled in size, from 4 to 12, and is now splitting into two teams. Analytics Data Engineering works close to the business, building the models, pipelines and dashboards that teams use to run the company. Data Platform, the team you'll lead, owns the foundation underneath: infrastructure, cost, real-time data, observability, and the AI capabilities the rest of Relay builds on.

The team's north star is platform health. That means a fast, reliable, cost-efficient platform with strong observability, and partners across the company who can do their work without waiting on us.

What You'll Be Doing

 - Lead and grow a senior team of data engineers. With an experienced team in place, your role is to provide direction, challenge thinking, and help the team make decisions and move work forward.

 - Own Snowflake cost. In your first 90 days, you’ll develop and execute a plan to reduce Snowflake costs month over month, working closely with the team to identify and deliver savings.

 - Get data into stakeholders' hands faster. You'll define and drive Relay's approach to real-time data and platform enablement, including streaming (Kafka) and a Snowflake MCP server that opens our data to AI tooling.

 - Make platform health visible. Build observability so the team finds a problem before a stakeholder does.

 - Translate platform work into business outcomes. You’ll help the team prioritize upgrades, migrations and refactors by linking technical investments to business value, whether that’s driving revenue, improving efficiency or reducing risk.

 - Balance speed against technical debt, in both directions. Sometimes you'll persuade the team to ship with some debt because the business value is there. Sometimes you'll persuade the business to give the team more time. You'll know which is which.

 - Run the team's operating rhythm. That includes standups, sprint and roadmap planning, architectural decisions, code review, and the requests that come in from across Relay.

Who You Are

 - You have at least two years of experience managing engineers, including senior team members with strong technical perspectives and the expertise to back them up.

 - You have deep, hands-on production experience with Snowflake and dbt, including building data models.

 - You've owned a production data platform, and ideally you've led meaningful improvements to one, such as cutting cost, improving reliability or adding new capability.

 - You challenge decisions with curiosity, not authority. You ask why before you ask how long, and you can find a path that serves both the engineer's concern and the business deadline.

 - You lead with context. You explain the problem, the metric and the business case before the architecture.

 - You're highly fluent with AI tools, both in how you work and in how you'd guide a team building AI-enabled data capabilities.

Bonus Points

Experience with:

 - AWS or GCP

 - Dagster or another data orchestrator

 - Fivetran and Hightouch

 - Terraform

 - Kafka or other real-time data infrastructure

The Interview Process

 - Stage 1: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with a member of our Talent team

 - Stage 2: A 60-minute Google Meet video call with the Hiring Manager

 - Stage 3: A take-home case study followed by a 60-minute Google Meet video call with our Engineering team

 - Stage 4: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with a member of our leadership team

jobs.title: Founding Account Executive, Los Angeles
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

We’re seeking a Los Angeles sales professional with a track record of success in achieving new business and growing a current book of business. The ideal candidate will be driven, organized, and display a natural ability to build rapport and trust. We’re looking for that perfect blend of sales drive coupled with a customer-first mentality that will help us create loyal, happy customers.

Rho has built a substantial community in the New York startup market. Hosting community-driven events, curated get-togethers, and more for founders and teams in the ecosystem has spread the Rho brand across many verticals. Los Angeles will be growing at the same speed and the Rho team with it. You will be responsible for organizing and attending Rho-sponsored events throughout the market geared towards building community and onboarding new business.

Responsibilities

 - Event-Driven Role – Attend multiple in-person networking events every week to build relationships and engage with the startup community. Must be comfortable with frequent face-to-face interactions.

 - Identify and target high-growth startups in the Los Angeles area for Rho’s cash management platform.

 - Win new business in competitive sales against the industry’s incumbents and newer players.

 - Attend Rho-sponsored events in person to build relationships and community.

 - Develop and execute sales strategies to meet and exceed revenue targets.

 - Ramp relationships and expand referral volume through networking.

 - Advocate for client needs to inform Rho’s roadmap.

 - Win new business in competitive sales against the industry’s incumbents and newer players.

 - Construct, forecast, and manage your sales pipeline to meet company goals.

 - Deliver comprehensive product demos and answer technical inquiries.

 - Coordinate closely with customer success and implementation teams to maintain the highest level of service and experience.

 

Qualifications

 - 3+ years of professional experience in a closing sales role.

 - 1+ years of experience managing a book of business and carrying a quota, focusing on net-new acquisitions.

 - Previous experience working in any one of the following areas is preferred:
 
 - Experience selling subscription-based software technologies (SaaS), other software products, and/or financial services products.
 
 - Experience working with startups.

 - Top-performer with a track record of consistently exceeding quota.

 - A consummate team player who enjoys wearing multiple hats and inspiring everyone around you to do great work.

 - A builder who is excited to help shape the foundation for Rhos’ Startup Banking team in Los Angeles.

Nice-to-Have

 - Familiarity with the startup ecosystem and venture accelerators

Our people are our most valuable asset. The budgeted base salary for this role is $83,000 - $115,000 with an OTE of $126,000 - $220,000 Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

Diversity is a core value at Rho. We’re passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems, and drive solutions that align with our mission. We welcome all qualified applications and support each of our Rho’ers with ongoing professional growth opportunities.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer at Rho, you'll build the financial infrastructure powering the next generation of founders. This isn't a role where you sit inside a lane. You'll move across the stack, own problems end-to-end, and talk directly to the customers using what you ship. We're hiring engineers who are restless about impact, reach for AI tools the way other people reach for documentation, and genuinely want to understand why what they're building matters.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own problems from scoping to production. Write the code, ship it, watch it land.

 - Work across the stack. You go where the problem is, not where your comfort zone ends.

 - Talk to customers. Sit in on calls, read support tickets, watch session replays. Build what people actually need.

 - Use AI in your daily workflow. Code generation, debugging, spec drafting, and spot where it changes what's possible.

 - Move fast and iterate in the open. Get something in front of users, then make it better.

 - Pick up what's falling. If something's broken, fix it.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of software engineering experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

 - Genuine full-stack flexibility. You've shipped across the stack and don't treat the backend/frontend divide as a hard boundary.

 - Genuine AI fluency. You use these tools every day and think about where they raise the ceiling on what you can build.

 - A bias to ship. You'd rather get something in front of a user than perfect it in a doc.

 - Customer curiosity. You want to know the person on the other side of what you're building, and you'll go find out.

 - High agency. You make progress when things are unclear, surface problems early, and own your outcomes.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $170,000 - $270,000. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

Diversity, empathy and transparency are core values at Rho. We are passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission including employees, contractors, candidates, customers and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems and drive solutions that align with our mission of making finance frictionless for business.

jobs.title: Design Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

A ROLE FOR THOSE COMMITTED TO DESIGNING WITH UNCOMMON CARE.

Most of a banking product is invisible when it's done right. The transfer that confirms with a motion so clean you feel it settle. The card that materializes like it was always going to. The empty state you almost want to keep looking at. Nobody files a support ticket about these things. They just trust the product a little more, and they can't tell you why.

We're hiring a Lead or Staff Design Engineer to own exactly that layer: the feel. The motion, the microinteractions, the details most companies never get to because they're too busy shipping features. We are not too busy. We think this is the work.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You live in the browser, in code, in the space between "it functions" and "it feels inevitable." You build the interactions, the transitions, the animations, and the components that make Rho feel like the most considered product our customers use all day. Then you write the libraries that let the rest of the team hit that bar without you in the room.

This is not a product design role. You're not writing PRDs, running discovery, or owning a roadmap. You're the person who takes something that works and makes it sing, and who builds the systems that make singing the default.

If you've ever reimplemented an animation three times because the first two were 40ms too slow and felt cheap, you already understand the job.

 - Own the feel of the product. Motion, microinteractions, transitions, gestures, the physics of how things move and respond. Every one of them earns trust or spends it.

 - Build the libraries no one else has built. Animation primitives, interaction patterns, and components that are genuinely new, not a re-skin of what's already on npm. We want work that other design engineers screenshot.

 - Ship in code. You build the real thing, in the real medium, at production quality. Figma is where a conversation starts, not where craft is decided.

 - Set the craft bar in motion. Define what "good" feels like at Rho and encode it into a system, tokens, easing curves, timing, springs, so the whole product moves with one considered voice.

 - Sweat details nobody asked you to sweat. The half-pixel. The 20ms. The focus ring. The way a number ticks up. This is the entire job, not a footnote to it.

WHO YOU ARE

You've been doing this for a while, and you have the receipts: at least 7 years building production interfaces, with a body of work that is visibly, unusually crafted. This is a lead role: you set the craft bar for the feel of the product and raise everyone around you to it, through the work itself and the systems you leave behind. We need to see it. A portfolio, a personal site, a component library, shipped work, live demos, something we can open and feel the care in.

You are the kind of person who:

 - Thinks Emil Kowalski and Josh Puckett are describing the job, not the aspiration. If those names mean nothing to you, this role probably isn't yours yet. If they make you nod, keep reading.

 - Has strong opinions about motion. You know why the default ease is wrong, when a spring beats a curve, what makes an animation feel expensive versus cheap, and when the answer is no animation at all. You can defend every one of these.

 - Writes real code. React, TypeScript, CSS at a level where you're building the hard interaction, not styling someone else's. You've probably published a library, or wanted to.

 - Is a genuine craftsperson, not a generalist who dabbles in polish. Your happiest hours are spent alone with a hard interaction problem, iterating past the point most people would call it done.

 - Has taste and can't turn it off. Sloppy motion physically bothers you. You notice the jank in other people's products. You've rebuilt things for free just because they annoyed you.

WHO THIS IS NOT FOR

 - Product designers looking to move into engineering. This is the reverse: a builder who obsesses over feel. If your portfolio is flows, journey maps, and product cases, that's a different (great) role, apply for our Product Designer opening instead.

 - Engineers who tolerate design. You have to love the pixel, not just implement it.

 - Anyone early or mid-career. This is a lead/staff craft role. You need years of taste, reps, and shipped work behind you, and the standing to set the bar for others. We'd love to meet you down the line.

 - People who think "good enough, ship it" is a virtue. It sometimes is. Not here, not on this layer.

 - Anyone who needs the interaction spec handed to them. You define what great feels like; nobody's going to define it for you.

THE BAR

We want Rho to feel like the most crafted financial product in the world, calm, confident, alive. Restraint over decoration. Motion with a reason. Details that reward the customer even when they don't consciously notice. If you've read this far and you're already thinking about how you'd rebuild one of our transitions, we should talk.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

THE ROLE

Rho is hiring Product Managers, but what we truly seek are GMs/Product CEOs. You'll own a meaningful surface of the platform end-to-end — close enough to the work and close enough to the customer that your judgment is earned, not inherited from a roadmap. You'll know what founders need before they ask, because you've built the intuition that comes from proximity, not process.

How products get built is fundamentally changing. AI is collapsing the line between thinking about something and making it real. The best PMs right now aren't just writing specs — they're prototyping with frontier models, testing ideas the same afternoon they have them, and building product that couldn't have existed a year ago. If that's already how you work, keep reading.

Rho is rebuilding the finance stack for the innovation economy. What happens next depends on the quality of our decisions and the speed at which we make them. The PMs we hire are how we get there.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Operate like a founder. Your surface is your company: its metrics are your P&L, its problems are yours whether or not they're in your job description. Nobody assigns founders their work. Default to motion — ship the scrappy version, learn, ship again, and unblock yourself instead of waiting. The surfaces you touch move faster because you're on them.

And build for them. Develop a deep, almost unfair understanding of how early-stage companies think about money, time, and risk. Design for the workflow they don't know they want yet — the desire path, not the paved one.

Own a problem space, not a problem. Not a feature, not a ticket queue — a living territory of customer problems that shift and collide. Frame the ones that matter, sharpen the hypothesis, define success before you build, and see it through to landing in a founder's hands. The map will change under you; redraw it and keep moving.

Decide what matters most — and re-decide when the facts change. Make deliberate calls about what to do now, next, and never. Hold them loosely: when the evidence says pivot, you pivot without ego. A PM who can't say no is just a project manager with better slides.

Work at the frontier. AI is your leverage in both directions: it 10x's how you work — more ideas tested, more prototypes built, more customer insight absorbed, more shipped — and it expands what you can build, product experiences that weren't possible twelve months ago. You're expected to find both. When a new capability drops, you're the one asking what it unlocks for our customers.

Get in the weeds. You're prototyping, pressure-testing, and iterating alongside design and engineering — with opinions about the details. Bring people along while you're there: partner deeply across Engineering, Design, Operations, GTM, and leadership, and communicate the why so well the team could make your calls without you in the room.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 3+ years building products — as a founder, PM, or engineer or equivalent experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment — and you've shipped work you're proud to put your name on.

 - You have frontier fluency. You work with AI daily — prototyping, analyzing, drafting, automating — and you can point to something you shipped or changed because a new capability made it possible. Not theorizing; doing.

 - You have taste. You hold your own view of what good looks like, obsess over the details, and know that in a banking product, every interaction carries trust.

 - You have discovery rigor. You can articulate the problem, the hypothesis, and how you'll know it worked before you've written a spec.

 - You build. You're not above opening a prototype, sketching a flow, or pulling the data yourself.

 - You think like a founder. You've been one, worked next to one, or operated like one — you take ownership past the edges of your role, and you pull things over the line that would die in someone else's backlog.

 - You're at home in ambiguity. You make calls on incomplete information and treat a pivot as new information, not a setback. Plans change; you're the steady one when they do.

 - You bring people with you. You build trust quickly, communicate proactively, and can align a room even when the answer is no.

 - You crave a team that pushes you — smart, ambitious people who make the work fun and help you grow faster than you thought possible.

Compensation will be determined by leveling and performance throughout the interview process. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.
