jobs.title: Staff / Principal Product Designer, Design Systems
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Rho — New York (in person)

Rho is building the best business banking platform on earth. Not "one of." The best.

We're looking for a Staff or Principal Product Designer to own our design system, the governed, in code foundation that everything we ship stands on. This is not a role where you maintain a Figma library and file tickets. This is the role where you define the frontend layer of a financial operating system that companies trust with their money.

It's a long post on purpose. We'd rather you know exactly what this is before you apply.

What you'd actually own

Our design system is becoming the governed frontend layer of the product, components in code, rules enforced through lint and CI, documentation an AI agent can query and build against on spec. You would own that. The architecture, the tokens, the primitives, the motion language, the governance, the contribution model, and the standards that let 80 plus engineers and PMs ship on bar without a designer babysitting every pixel.

You'll partner with our frontend guild, our engineers, and the design team as genuine equals, not as a service desk. You'll decide what a component is, how it behaves, how it moves, what it enables, and where it must not bend. You'll set the craft bar for the entire org and then build the system that makes hitting that bar the path of least resistance.

Who this is for

You've been doing this for a while. We mean it, at least 7 years of product design experience, with real design systems ownership at scale. Not "contributed to a design system." Owned one. Built one. Governed one. Watched it get abused and fixed the governance so it couldn't happen again.

You are the kind of person who:

 - Designs in code, or is hungry to. You believe Figma is not the build environment, and that designing in the real medium eliminates a whole category of hidden QA cost. If the phrase "design engineer" makes you lean forward, hi.

 - Has genuine taste and a serious bar for it. Branding, typography, motion, microinteractions: you sweat all of it. You have opinions about easing curves and you can defend them. A transition that feels half a beat off bothers you until it's fixed.

 - Owns your craft, doesn't inherit it. You can point at a visual language and say "I built that," not "that was set before I got there and I adjusted the fonts."

 - Builds systems, not screens. You think in primitives, states, edge cases, and two-way doors. When something breaks at a thousand users, you already designed for it.

 - Ships, then sharpens. You move fast, you work out loud, you share the messy middle instead of disappearing for three weeks and returning with a monument. Perfect but late is a fail here.

 - Has low ego and high standards at the same time. You hold a firm craft bar and you genuinely want the critique. You defend decisions with reasoning, not with "it's my stylistic choice."

 - Gets the domain, or is dying to. Financial workflows are dense, multi-role, permission scoped, and unforgiving. You find that fun, not frightening.

Who this is NOT for

A few honest filters, to save us both time.

Do not apply to this role if you are junior. This is a Staff/Principal position. If you're earlier in your career, we'd genuinely love to meet you, we just want you in the right process. Apply for our product designer role instead: https://www.rho.co/careers/f4ece49b-3b53-4ffb-861f-9cc972c10b27

It's also probably not your fit if:

 - Your portfolio is process decks, tiny mockups, and journey maps, and the actual UI is nowhere to be found. We evaluate craft at the pixel level. If we can't see it, we can't hire it.

 - Your idea of a design system is a color palette and a component library nobody governs.

 - Motion and micro interactions are afterthoughts to you rather than part of the craft.

 - You need a fully specced ticket before you can move, and ambiguity makes you freeze.

 - You want to be handed the vision. We want someone who brings one.

 - "Move fast" reads to you as "lower the quality bar." Here it means the opposite, the bar is high AND the pace is high, and the system you build is how those two coexist.

 - You lead with an AI chatbot case study. We love AI and use it every day. But a conversational UI is not a demonstration of end-to-end product craft.

How we work

Small pods. Artifact first. Designers own their surfaces end to end, including research, QA, and the fight to get it shipped right. We use AI natively and expect you to. The design team is heads down on building the governed frontend layer this quarter, and this role is central to it.

We're in the office in New York because the best systems work happens shoulder to shoulder, obsessing over a real screen.

The bar

Restraint over decoration. Confidence over noise. Interfaces that feel calm because someone sweated every detail so the user never has to, and that feel alive because the motion is considered, not bolted on. We care about how money moving feels, how a card creation confirms, how a state transition lands. If "it looks fun, but does it do anything" is a question you ask yourself unprompted, you'll fit right in.

How to apply

If you've read this far and you're already thinking about how you'd architect our token layer, we should talk.

Come ready to do two things when we meet, walk us through a real, working file (not just the polished case study frames), and show us a design system you actually built and governed. Bring one deeply complex, systems level project and one piece you're proud of at the pixel level, and tell us plainly which decisions were yours.

This is intentionally a hybrid role. At Rho, we need someone who can do both, someone who can build the model and reason clearly about how it gets deployed, monitored, and retrained in production. You'll work on high-leverage problems like our transaction coding suggestion engine, OCR/document understanding pipeline, and RAG-based and agentic systems, while also helping build the underlying foundation: evaluation frameworks, model deployment and monitoring practices, and the infrastructure decisions that determine whether ML at Rho is reliable and scalable. This role requires genuine fluency in ML infrastructure and evals, not just modeling - you should be as comfortable discussing feature store design or eval harness architecture with data engineers as you are validating a model's statistical soundness.

Technologies we use for data: Python, Snowflake, DBT, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, MLflow, Terraform, Prometheus, Google Cloud Services, Omni, Hex, PowerBI

Responsibilities:

 - Set technical standards and best practices that help the ML/DS practice scale as the team grows

 - Translate ambiguous business problems into well-scoped modeling questions

Requirements:

- 6+ years of experience in data science, applied ML, or a related quantitative field, with a track record of shipping models into production

 - Comfortable operating as a hybrid DS/infrastructure practitioner:, someone who doesn't hand a model off to a platform team and walk away, but who can own it end to end when needed

 - Experience helping establish or mature ML practices, standards, or infrastructure within a team and company

 - Strong programming skills in Python, with solid SQL

 - Comfortable making infrastructure trade-off decisions jointly with data/platform engineers, and able to speak credibly on both the modeling and systems sides

 - Experience with statistical modeling, machine learning techniques, and experiment design

 - Excellent communication skills; able to influence technical direction and bring both technical and non-technical stakeholders along

Nice To Haves:

 - Familiarity with workflow orchestrators such as Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect

 - Experience with BI tools such as Omni or Power BI

 - Background in fintech, banking, or financial services data

What we offer

About You

 - Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

jobs.title: Law Firm & Accounting Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Rho is looking for a Law Firm & Accounting Partnerships Lead to own two of our highest-leverage referral channels: the startup law firms that incorporate companies on day one, and the accounting, bookkeeping, and outsourced CFO firms that run their books from day two onward. These are the advisors founders trust before they ever pick a bank — and the firms that shape which financial stack a company lands on.

You'll own this channel end to end: strategy, partner sourcing, negotiation, launch, enablement, and the revenue that comes out of it. This is a builder role, not a maintenance role. You'll inherit early relationships and a real product story, and your mandate is to turn that into a repeatable, quota-carrying channel with a named partner roster, a working referral motion, and reporting leadership can trust.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

OWN THE CHANNEL STRATEGY

 - Define the segmentation and target list for both sides of the channel: startup-focused law firms (formation, emerging companies, venture practices) and accounting/bookkeeping/OCFO firms

 - Build the business case for where to invest — which firms, which geographies, which practice groups drive the most qualified client referrals

 - Set the partner tiering model and the value exchange at each tier (co-marketing, dedicated support, revenue share, product access)

 - Own the channel number: sourced pipeline, referred accounts, funded accounts, and revenue contribution

SOURCE AND CLOSE PARTNERS

 - Prospect, pitch, and close new law firm and accounting firm partnerships — this is a hunting role, not an inbound one

 - Build relationships with multiple stakeholders inside each firm: managing partners, practice group leads, business development, and the associates and staff who actually make the referral

 - Structure and negotiate partnership terms alongside Legal and Finance

 - Represent Rho at the conferences, bar association events, CPA gatherings, and founder dinners where these relationships get built (expect meaningful travel to major tech hubs)

DRIVE REFERRALS AND PARTNER REVENUE

 - Turn signed partnerships into activated ones — a logo on a page is not a partnership

 - Run onboarding and enablement so partner teams know exactly when and how to introduce Rho to a client

 - Build the co-marketing motion with Marketing: webinars, CPE-eligible content, perk pages, newsletters, and joint events

 - Run MBRs/QBRs with top partners against shared goals, and prune the partners who aren't producing

BE THE VOICE OF THE CHANNEL INTERNALLY

 - Work cross-functionally with Sales, Onboarding, Support, and Product to make sure referred clients get a white-glove handoff

 - Bring structured feedback to Product on what law firms and accounting partners need from Rho — multi-entity views, advisor access, close workflows, integrations

 - Partner with Sales leadership so channel-sourced deals are worked, tracked, and credited cleanly

BUILD THE OPERATING SYSTEM

 - Stand up the infrastructure that makes the channel scale: partner CRM hygiene, referral attribution, pipeline tracking, and a partner portal experience

 - Document the playbook — partner onboarding, referral handoff, enablement, and event workflows — so the next hires ramp fast

 - Produce clear, regular reporting on channel-sourced pipeline and revenue for leadership
 
 

WHO YOU ARE

 - 5+ years in partnerships, channel, or a closing sales role — ideally at a fintech, B2B SaaS, or professional services platform selling into or through advisors

 - You've carried a number and hit it. You're comfortable with a quota tied to partner-sourced revenue

 - You've built something from scratch. You know the difference between running a program and starting one, and you want the second

 - Credible with professionals: you can hold a real conversation with a managing partner about their book of business, not just pitch a product

 - Strong commercial instincts — you can structure a deal, run a negotiation, and know when to walk away

 - Excellent written and verbal communicator; you can present to an executive audience and write a partner email that actually gets replies

 - Data-driven: you instrument the channel, read the numbers, and reallocate effort accordingly

 - Thrives in ambiguity, moves fast, and doesn't need a playbook handed to you — you're writing it

 - Based in the Bay Area and willing to travel (~25–35%)

BONUS POINTS

 - Existing network among startup law firms and/or accounting, bookkeeping, and OCFO firms

 - Background in accounting or law (CPA, JD, or time inside a firm) — you've lived the workflow you're selling into

 - Experience launching a partner program at a fintech or spend management company

 - Familiarity with the startup ecosystem — VCs, accelerators, formation platforms, fund admins

 - Experience with partner CRM/PRM tooling and referral attribution

Why This Role

Law firms and accountants are the highest-trust distribution channel in the startup market — at comparable companies, the accounting channel alone has grown into one of the largest sources of new customers. Rho hasn't built it yet. You'd own that from the ground up, with a direct line to leadership, a clear number, and the room to build a team behind you as the channel proves out.

COMPENSATION

$150-200K OTE
Equity, health/dental/vision, 401(k), and other benefits included.

jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Financial Crime Analyst

We're looking for an experienced financial crime analyst to support our overall fraud and anti-money laundering (AML) strategy and operations, working alongside and supporting the Financial Crime lead as a critical member of the team. As a core member of the team, you will have a unique opportunity to learn and apply your previous experience, design and innovate financial crime detection systems, while conducting data analysis and being actively engaged cross-functionally. jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Marketing Operations Manager to be the backbone of Rho’s marketing org. This person keeps our work across the team running smoothly, so we can move quickly and leadership always knows what’s live, what’s working, and where to focus next.

In Brand, you’ll own campaign project management, keeping launches on schedule from brief to go-live. You’ll also run brand lift analysis so we can measure what each campaign actually moves. In Growth, you’ll facilitate our experimentation program, from setting up tests to sharing what we learned. You’ll also manage the systems and tech stack the team depends on every day.

Across the org, you’ll build and run the system of record: one place where every workstream’s owner, status, and key metric lives. You’ll partner with Growth Engineering and the data science team to turn their work into a reporting cadence that marketing, the exec team, and the board rely on. Working closely with the VP of Marketing, you’ll have the context to spot what needs attention and the process discipline to raise it early, so the whole team stays aligned, hits its numbers, and scales.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the system of record: one place where every workstream across Growth, Brand, and Community is tracked against its owner, status, and the metric it's supposed to move.

 - Run a weekly written review across all three pillars (not a dashboard nobody opens) so slipping work surfaces early instead of reaching the VP of Marketing the night before it matters.

 - Translate the outputs of Growth Engineering and the data science team (funnel performance, cost per funded account, channel health) into reporting marketing, exec, and the board actually run on. You consume these models, you don't build them.

 - Track every vendor and spend commitment against sign-off status; flag anything moving forward without it before it becomes a fait accompli.

 - Maintain a single, current version of marketing strategy and planning docs, replacing the scattered state across Slack, Notion, and individual owners' heads.

 - Run the cadence on hiring, budget, and planning asks that go to Devonaire, Bojan, and other cross-functional partners, so those requests are tracked to a decision instead of going quiet.

 - Keep a live map of who owns what, including backup owners for anything with single-threaded risk, so no function or vendor relationship depends on one person.

 - Flag ownership gaps and conflicting priorities across pillars directly, rather than letting them resolve themselves by default.

 - Run the experimentation program for Growth: intake, prioritization, test design standards, sprint cadence, and a shared learnings log.

 - Facilitate a weekly or bi-weekly experiment cadence across Growth, including hypothesis writing, success criteria, and kill and scale decisions.

REQUIREMENTS

 - You've designed and run an incrementality or lift test (holdout, geo-lift, PSA-style), not just read about the concept. You know what breaks a naive test — seasonality, cross-channel halo, saturation — and how to control for it.

 - Fluent SQL, and you've built and owned dbt models in a real warehouse. This isn't a role you can do from platform UIs.

 - You've owned marketing or GTM data where the number mattered financially, and defended a CAC or attribution figure to a skeptical exec.

 - You've reconciled conflicting numbers across ad platforms, a CRM, and a warehouse, and can explain the gap rather than picking the flattering one.

 - Systems experience, not just analysis: forms, routing, CRM sync, reverse ETL, taxonomy. Comfortable owning plumbing.

 - You define metrics instead of waiting to be handed them.

 - Judgment on PII and compliance in a regulated financial services context.

 - Comfortable as the only person in your function, working across marketing, data engineering, sales ops, and growth without authority over any of them.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Fintech, banking, or another regulated environment.

 - Snowflake, dbt, Hightouch, Salesforce, HubSpot.

 - Measurement for AI search and answer engine visibility. It's an active channel for us and barely instrumented anywhere.

jobs.title: Payment Operations Associate
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the role

We're looking for a Payment Operations Associate to support Rho's day-to-day payment processing. You'll process client repayments, issue rewards and credits, resolve payment exceptions, and keep credit and card program settings up to date, working alongside Credit Risk, Client Services, Fraud, Compliance, and our partner bank. The work is deadline-driven and detail-oriented, and it feeds directly into client statements and month-end close.

What you will do

 - Process client repayments. Run recurring ACH pulls for monthly credit repayments on a fixed due-date schedule, handling non-standard accounts manually, and process interim payments as they arise. Confirm each payment is captured accurately from initiation through posting.

 - Issue rewards, credits, and incentives. Calculate and release cashback rewards on a set monthly schedule, reconcile against system-generated figures, and process statement credits, sign-up bonuses, and promotional incentives with the appropriate review and approval. Provide cashback breakdowns to clients on request.

 - Maintain credit and card program settings. Update client credit limits, payment terms, statement cycles and custom pricing, keeping records consistent across systems and documenting every change.

 - Manage wire operations. Handle wire trace requests, recalls, returns, and non-posted wires with our partner bank, and administer enrollments and limit changes for drawdown wire services.

 - Manage ACH operations. Initiate ACH returns and reversals in line with NACHA rules, applying the correct return code and meeting NACHA return/reversal timeframes that apply to each request.

 - Support fraud and credit review. Expedite settlement on transactions once Fraud or Credit has approved them, and hold transactions for review when something looks unusual. Manage RDC returns with outreach to the relevant teams, and set the appropriate settlement delay or instant release on credit repayments based on client credit risk.

 - Report on delinquency. Produce a weekly past-due report for Credit Risk, Finance, Client Services, and Fraud, monitor 30-day credit repayment returns and overdue balances daily, and escalate for client outreach.

 - Route compliance, fraud and legal escalations. Flag sanctions-related inquiries from our partner bank to the right internal teams, forward legal notices to Legal, coordinate Letter of Indemnity and Hold Harmless requests with the Fraud team and request limit increases when transaction thresholds are reached.

 - Support our Letter of Credit program. Coordinate Standby Letters of Credit with our partner bank, fund the collateral account, process the associated fees, and provide Client Services with the figures for month-end fee statements.

 - Improve the process. Identify manual steps worth automating, keep procedure documentation current, and partner with Product and Engineering to close gaps in payment workflows.

 

You have

 - 2+ years in payment operations, banking operations, treasury operations, or a similar function at a fintech, bank, or payment processor.

 - Working knowledge of payment rails — ACH, Fedwire, RTP, card networks, and remote deposit — and what happens when a payment fails, returns, or settles late.

 - Exceptional attention to detail. You reconcile before you release, and you catch the transposed digit.

 - Comfort with recurring hard deadlines and high transaction volume without losing accuracy.

 - Hands-on with operational tooling: ticketing systems (Jira), BI dashboards (Looker), spreadsheets, and bank portals. SQL is a plus, not a requirement.

 - Clear written communicator. Much of this role is coordinating across Credit Risk, Client Services, Fraud, and Compliance in writing.

 - Sound judgment on escalation. You know which items you can resolve and which need Fraud, Credit, or Legal before you touch them.

Our people are our most valuable asset. Our target compensation range for this role is $70,000 - $100,000. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager
jobs.description:
We are a profitable, mission-driven fintech company building financial solutions for people whose needs go unmet by traditional institutions – people with disabilities, older adults, and people in recovery, and the families and professionals who care for them. We get to wake up every day knowing our work has a profound impact on our customers' lives, and we run the business with the discipline to keep doing it for the long haul. That track record has earned us a spot on the Forbes Fintech 50 and the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing companies for the last two years.

We're hiring a Principal Product Manager to lead us in building the right thing for our bank and card partnership-based capabilities. You’ll shape what we deliver to our Family Banking partners and their account holders, balancing customer needs, partner realities, technical constraints, regulatory considerations, and business strategy. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who works hypothesis-first, and is comfortable in the complexity of financial services.

You’ll love this role if you’re energized by difficult product problems with real-world consequences, enjoy working directly with sophisticated external partners and clients, and want to help shape the next generation of family banking. Because our products sit at the intersection of banking, payments, operations, compliance, and deeply human customer needs, the work requires rigor, judgment, and unusually strong cross-functional thinking. Our customers and partners depend on us to execute thoughtfully and reliably - and we care deeply about getting it right.

What You’ll Do

 - Own product areas related to our card and family banking partner ecosystem, helping shape both near-term execution and long-term strategy.

 - Work directly with bank partners and sophisticated external clients to understand needs, shape a compelling “why,” solve problems collaboratively, and turn partnership opportunities into scalable products and systems.

 - Build full-stack fintech products spanning customer experience, operational workflows, APIs, payment rails, and partner infrastructure.

 - Partner deeply with engineering, design, operations, compliance, customer support, and go-to-market teams to ensure we are building the right things in the right sequence - and shipping them with high quality.

 - Use AI, prototyping, data, customer conversations, and direct product exploration to accelerate learning and compress feedback loops.

 - Bring clarity to ambiguity. Navigate competing priorities, evolving constraints, and operational complexity while helping the broader organization stay focused on what matters most.

 - Lead through influence, judgment, and execution rather than org structure or management authority.

 - Go deep when execution requires it - refining edge cases, writing clear specs, improving operational processes, and unblocking teams.

Who You Are

 - An experienced product leader with 10+ years in product management and deep fintech experience, with strong instincts around how financial products actually work in the real world.

 - Someone who loves being an individual contributor and wants to stay close to the work: solving problems, shipping products, refining systems, and collaborating directly with teammates and customers.

 - Comfortable moving fluidly between big-picture strategy and nitty-gritty implementation details, especially in complex, fast-moving environments with many stakeholders and competing constraints.

 - Strong with both external partners and internal stakeholders - thoughtful, credible, low-ego, and able to build trust quickly across a wide range of audiences.

 - Technically curious and architecturally literate. You want to understand how the systems work underneath the product, not just what appears on the surface.

 - Motivated more by customer impact, execution, and building excellent products than by status, empire-building, or trend-chasing.

Great work happens in spaces designed for it. Wealthsimple's Workplace Operations team is responsible for delivering safe, functional, and welcoming environments for our people. We believe in unreasonable hospitality - going beyond what's expected, in ways big and small, to remove friction and create space for people to focus on what matters. As part of the team, you'll help shape how our office experience scales, creating a best-in-class workplace that enables our employees to do their best work and helps drive the business forward.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As Lead, Workplace Operations, you own the experience of the physical workplace itself: the systems, facilities, F&B, and workplace safety that every Wealthsimpler relies on, across every hub in Canada and the US. You set the roadmap and govern the standard for all of it, end to end. This is a hands-on operational role reporting to the Senior Manager, Real Estate Operations within People Operations, so you're the person people escalate to when there’s an operational issue with no playbook, and you’ll be trusted to make the call. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the annual workplace operations roadmap across all hubs, set priorities against department goals, and drive programs from planning through rollout. Act as the primary escalation point for operational issues where there is no established playbook.

 - Run day-to-day workplace operations across building systems, facilities, F&B, and physical space, setting the service standard across hubs and ensuring issues are resolved quickly, consistently, and with a hospitality mindset.

 - Own the maintenance and physical space lifecycle across all locations, including preventive maintenance, reactive repairs, capital planning, minor works, moves, and refurbishments. Ensure work is planned properly, business continuity is protected, and standards remain consistent regardless of who executes locally.

 - Lead workplace vendor and contract management, including sourcing and vetting partners, RFPs, contract standards, SLAs, performance management, and escalation. Hold vendors accountable for cost, quality, and service.

 - Own the workplace operating budget across all hubs, set the annual envelope, allocate spend across programs and sites, manage forecasting and approvals, and drive cost optimization while maintaining service standards.

 - Own a visible, proactive workplace health and safety framework across all locations, keeping requirements, processes, and practices aligned with local regulations across Ontario, other provinces, and US states.

 - Turn ticketing, utilization, occupancy, and service data into decisions that improve workplace operations and inform portfolio planning. Identify recurring bottlenecks, build scalable solutions, and take on team oversight as the function grows.
 
 

SKILLS YOU’LL BRING

 - 6-8+ years in Workplace Operations, Facility Management, or Property Management, with real ownership of programs, budgets, and vendor relationships rather than just delivery support

 - An activated vendor network: contractors, trades, facilities vendors you already know and trust, so you can move on day one - and you can speak to how you vet them and hold them to a high standard.

 - Hands-on experience running minor works and moves from scope to completion - budgets, contractors, business continuity, and consistency of standard regardless of who’s executing locally, with real accountability for the result.

 - Contract and RFP

experience:

you can turn a service need into a standard, run the RFP process end to end and negotiate the SLA yourself.

 - A data-driven approach: you build the framework and the measurement to inform workplace decisions, and use good judgment to bring AI tools into the mix, speeding up reporting, spotting patterns, and driving faster solutions.

 - Strong communicator, built for change. You take a rollout that could land as noise and turn it into a clear plan so people understand what's changing and why, not just that it happened.

 - Working knowledge of Ontario's Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHSA), along with building code and fire safety requirements, with the judgement to keep a framework current as local requirements shift.
 

WHO YOU ARE

 - High agency. You see a gap and close it, and you’d rather ask forgiveness than permission

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities. You make great decisions without a perfect playbook and build the answers as you go.

 - An instinct for hospitality. You notice the small things and don’t wait to be asked before fixing them.

 - A builder. You’d rather design the scalable solution than patch around the same problem again. You take ownership of the outcome, not just your piece of the process.

ABOUT THE OBSERVABILITY PLATFORM TEAM

The Observability Platform team exists to make production legible to every engineer and AI agent at Wealthsimple, on their first day and every day after. Every request, job, and user action produces a signal, and our job is to turn that signal into a fast, high-cardinality data asset that anyone can question. A business stakeholder investigating a drop in conversions, a service owner tracing a slow endpoint, an engineer validating a release, and an AI agent confirming its own change should all reach for the same data and get an answer in seconds.

We treat the platform as a product, and the engineers, service owners, and business stakeholders who depend on it as our partners. Our mission is to build the wide-event data model, the query foundation, and the golden paths that connect people to production data. We instrument on open standards such as OpenTelemetry so switching costs are a configuration change rather than a rewrite, and we optimize for the questions people did not anticipate rather than for pre-built dashboards.

As the founding Software Development Manager for this team, you will hire and lead the engineers who build this foundation, and set the technical vision that shapes how Wealthsimple understands its systems for years to come.

IN THIS ROLE YOU'LL HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO:

 - Build the wide-event data model at the heart of the platform. Lead an events-first foundation on open standards such as OpenTelemetry, including the schema, SDKs, libraries, and instrumentation defaults that make rich, consistent, high-cardinality telemetry the path of least resistance for every team.

 - Build the query foundation that connects people to production data, and make it legible to AI agents. Design the columnar or streaming backends, the tagging and context-propagation standards, and the access patterns, including protocols such as MCP, that let a business stakeholder, a service owner, an engineer, or an AI agent ask an unanticipated question and get a fast answer.

 - Connect production data to business impact. Tie telemetry to client experience and business outcomes through SLOs and user flows, so teams see a problem in the numbers that matter before clients feel it. This is detection framed as a data question, not a wall of machine-state alerts.

 - Define what observability means at Wealthsimple, set a multi-year roadmap, and align engineering and leadership behind it.

 - Own the tool and vendor strategy across the observability stack, including how we get the most from Datadog while reducing lock-in and managing cost.

 - Prove value on pilots. Start with one or two teams to validate the approach before scaling it across the organization.

 - Hire and lead the team, and own career development, performance management, coaching, and a culture of technical excellence.

 - Stay hands-on, and move fast with AI coding tools such as Claude Code fluently to prototype, unblock the team, and raise its bar for building with AI.

 - Make test signal fast, deterministic, and actionable. Flakiness a human can shrug off is fatal to an agent iterating unattended. You'll attack flake detection, test selection, and failure output that is legible enough to act on without a person interpreting it.

Location: Toronto, ON (Hybrid)

Term: 8 months, beginning January 11,
2027. This is an 8 month internship designed for co-op students, non-co-op students, and recent graduates who are ready to ship impactful work.

During your internship, you will have the opportunity to contribute to projects that are changing the landscape of financial services for Canadians. You will be on a team that supports your growth, provides mentorship, and connects you to the broader Wealthsimple community!

Our internship program operates on a hybrid model, where you’ll be working from our Toronto headquarters on Wednesdays and Thursdays. This structure offers the flexibility of remote work, while also providing the collaboration, connection, and mentorship that come from being together in person.

This posting covers two tracks: Workflow Optimization and Enablement. Please apply to the one that best fits your interests.

Please note: the role you apply for is the role you will be assessed on throughout the interview process. We are unable to accommodate requests to switch between Workflow Optimization and Enablement tracks after submission.

 

ABOUT THE CX OPERATIONS TEAM

The CX Operations team is responsible for enabling exceptional client and agent experiences across Wealthsimple through optimized systems, content, AI solutions, and strategic initiatives. We manage the technology, knowledge, and processes that power our customer experience organization, driving continuous improvement in efficiency and effectiveness.

 

CHOOSE YOUR TRACK:

 

WORKFLOW OPTIMIZATION, INTERN

Workflow Optimization (WFO) streamlines the workflows, systems, and automations that span our entire ecosystem of tools. We partner with teams across the organization to identify and simplify toilsome workflows through process mapping, automation, and AI tool implementations.

As a WFO Intern, you'll partner with WFO managers and internal SMEs to: design and build AI tools for analysis; audit and improve automations; map and redesign workflows; and deliver measurable improvements in containment, resolution time, and operational risk.

You'll develop core skills in project planning, process design, AI tool deployment, and AI‑enhanced automation while contributing directly to CX efficiency and client experience.

 

IN THIS ROLE, YOU’LL HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO

 - Partner with the AI Experiences team to launch net-new features to our clients and support agents.

 - Map current-state workflows with SMEs, identify optimization opportunities, and implement AI-enhanced changes across macros, automations, and documentation.

 - Build comprehensive automation inventories across multiple systems, to propose consolidations and net-new automations and AI optimizations.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Structured problem solving and process thinking, with the ability to translate ambiguous workflows into clear maps and requirements

 - Basic familiarity with AI concepts (LLM, RAG, context windows, hallucination, etc.)

 - Basic familiarity with customer operations tools or ticketing systems (Zendesk, JIRA)

 - Basic familiarity with data and testing concepts – to be applied in the context of testing the accuracy of AI models (A/B testing, sample sizes, statistical significance, etc.)

 - Strong documentation and communication skills to collaborate with SMEs and present proposals

 - Bias to action and ownership to drive projects from discovery to implementation

ENABLEMENT, INTERN

Our enablement group is responsible for how our support workforce learns, performs, and grows. We build the systems, programs, and culture that keep our support teams performing at a high bar. Quality, learning, change readiness, and performance measurement all sit within this group. Underneath all of it is a simple belief: every client interaction should be fast, high-quality, and trustworthy. Our job is to turn that belief into measurable reality.

As an Enablement Intern, you'll support the group's analytical work. You'll partner with the managers who own quality and performance measurement to test the data, run original analyses, spot trends early, and turn your findings into recommendations leaders can act on. This goes beyond reporting, the question is never only "what does the number say?" It's also "is this measuring the right thing, and what should we do about it?"

You'll build skills in analysis, metric design, and structured problem solving, and see up close how an AI-first quality and performance program runs in a regulated industry. The best person for this role doesn't only meet a high bar; they hold their own work to one.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Fund Operations is the team that keeps our Alternative Investment Funds products running accurately and at scale. We own the operational functions behind private credit, private equity, private markets, venture, and infrastructure fund structures, including NAV oversight, capital activity, and financial reporting. We're a small, high-ownership team that works closely with Legal, Compliance, Investment Research, and external Fund Administrators, GPs, Custodians, and Auditors to build institutional-grade processes as our alternatives platform grows.

 - Collaborate with Asset Management, Compliance, Product, Trading, and Engineering to ensure the accuracy of client records and flag operational issues before they become client-facing problems

 - Respond to client inquiries and prepare ad-hoc reports that give clients clarity on their portfolios

 - Coordinate with auditors during the annual audit process and help prepare audit workpapers

 - Use data to identify inefficiencies in our processes and propose solutions, leveraging AI where it helps us move faster without sacrificing accuracy

 - Maintain and update process documentation as our operations scale

 - 1-2 years of experience at a fund management or fund administration company, with exposure to NAV calculations, tax and audit preparation, and settlement of orders, distributions, redemptions, and capital calls

 - Strong Excel skills, with SQL or other programming experience considered a plus, along with progress toward or completion of an industry designation (CPA, CFA, CAIA, CSC) also a plus
